title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients.
abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the global underutilization of antiviral therapy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its impact on survival outcomes. The central question is whether antiviral therapy improves survival in HBV-related HCC and how its utilization varies across populations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis and meta-analysis of 78 studies involving 68,243 patients, published between 2006 and 2024. The studies were selected following PRISMA guidelines, and random-effects models were used to pool study estimates. The initial search identified 4556 studies, of which 178 underwent full-text review.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is associated with improved long-term survival in HBV-related HCC. Treated patients had higher 3- and 5-year overall survival (OS) rates compared to untreated patients. However, the use of antiviral therapy remains underutilized in clinical practice, with only 17.2% of patients receiving it before HCC diagnosis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates between treated and untreated patients. Additionally, the review highlights a critical gap in care, suggesting that earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation is needed. The evidence also indicates that the association between antiviral therapy and survival may vary depending on the activity of HCC.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings emphasize the need for updating clinical guidelines to include HCC as an antiviral treatment criterion. Further research is required to determine the optimal timing and duration of antiviral therapy in HBV-related HCC and to address the variability in treatment outcomes across different HCC subtypes.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 78 studies involving 68,243 patients examines the underutilization of antiviral therapy in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its impact on survival. The review found that antiviral therapy is associated with improved 3- and 5-year overall survival rates in HBV-related HCC, with treated patients showing higher survival compared to untreated ones. However, only 17.2% of patients received antiviral therapy before HCC diagnosis, highlighting a critical gap in care. The study also notes no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates between treated and untreated patients, suggesting the need for more consistent and earlier antiviral initiation in clinical practice. These findings underscore the importance of revising guidelines to incorporate HCC as a criterion for antiviral treatment and call for further research to optimize treatment strategies.

abstract_zh: 使用核苷(酸)类似物进行抗病毒药物治疗被推荐用于所有具有病毒血症的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝硬化的患者,无论其病毒载量或肝酶水平如何。然而,肝细胞癌(HCC)并不是美国HBV 治疗指南中的治疗标准。尽管之前的研究报告指出,在HBV相关HCC患者中,抗病毒药物治疗与改善生存率相关,但目前仍缺乏明确的指南。为了指导指南制定,我们估计了抗病毒药物治疗率及其与生存率和HCC复发率之间的关联。我们按照PRISMA指南,对2006年至2024年间发表的、报告了HBV相关HCC成人患者抗病毒药物治疗率、生存率和/或HCC复发率的研究进行了系统综述和荟萃分析。使用随机效应模型汇总研究估计值。初始共有4556项研究,其中178项进行了全文审查,最终分析了78项(共68,243名患者)。汇总的抗病毒药物治疗率(52项研究,41,345名患者)为53.1%。在报告了HCC前抗病毒药物治疗启动的研究中,17.2%的HBV相关HCC患者在HCC发生前接受了治疗。接受治疗(与未接受治疗相比)的患者3年和5年总生存率(OS)更高(80.4% vs. 46.8%,两者p < 0.01)。在非活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为78.0% vs. 56.4%(p < 0.01),而在活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为48.2% vs. 22.6%(p = 0.14)。在多变量荟萃回归分析中,抗病毒药物治疗仍与改善5年OS独立相关。HCC复发率没有显著差异。抗病毒药物治疗与改善长期生存率相关,但在HBV相关HCC中仍被低估使用。这些发现突显了护理中的关键差距,并强调了在HBV相关HCC患者中更早和更一致地启动抗病毒药物治疗的必要性。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注全球在乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝细胞癌(HCC)患者中对抗病毒药物疗法的应用不足及其对生存结局的影响。核心问题是抗病毒药物疗法是否能改善HBV相关HCC患者的生存率,以及其应用在不同人群中的差异。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一项系统分析和荟萃分析,纳入了2006年至2024年间发表的78项研究,共涉及68,243例患者。研究遵循PRISMA指南进行筛选,采用随机效应模型合并各研究的估计值。初始检索共获得4556项研究,其中178项进行了全文审阅。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 使用核苷(酸)类似物的抗病毒药物疗法与HBV相关HCC患者的长期生存率改善相关。接受治疗的患者3年和5年总体生存率(OS)均高于未接受治疗的患者。然而,抗病毒药物疗法在临床实践中仍应用不足,仅有17.2%的患者在HCC发生前接受该疗法。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 治疗组与未治疗组在HCC复发率方面无显著差异。此外,综述还指出在护理方面存在关键缺口,建议需要更早且更一致地启动抗病毒药物疗法。证据还表明,抗病毒药物疗法与生存率之间的关联可能因HCC的活动性而有所不同。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调需要更新临床指南,将HCC纳入抗病毒药物治疗的考虑因素。还需要进一步研究以确定HBV相关HCC中抗病毒药物疗法的最佳时机和持续时间,并解决不同HCC亚型中治疗结局的差异性。}}.{

title: Similar Long-Term Incidence of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B Initiating Entecavir Versus Tenofovir Alafenamide: A REAL-B Study.
abstract: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC incidence and the association between antiviral regimen and HCC were analysed using competing-risk analysis. A total of 1437 patients (710 ETV, 727 TAF) were included, with similar mean follow-up durations (55.5 ± 29.8 vs. 58.0 ± 25.5 months; p = 0.077). ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis. After IPTW, both groups had balanced characteristics (all standardised differences < 0.1). After IPTW adjustment, during follow-up, 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively (p = 0.853). There was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent findings across subgroups by age, sex, cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, HBeAg, baseline liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, diabetes mellitus and in sensitivity analysis using PSM. In this real-world multinational study of treatment-naïve CHB patients, HCC incidence did not significantly differ between ETV and TAF groups, suggesting therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients initiating entecavir (ETV) or tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) therapy. A retrospective multinational analysis of 1437 treatment-naïve adults with CHB without prior HCC was conducted across 23 centres in four countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). The study found that 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC during follow-up, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively. After IPTW adjustment, there was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent results across subgroups. The findings suggest that therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors rather than HCC risk. However, the study noted that ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis, which may introduce potential biases.

title_zh: 恩替卡韦与替诺福韦艾拉酚胺在慢性乙型肝炎患者中对肝细胞癌长期发病率的比较:REAL-B研究
source_body_en: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC incidence and the association between antiviral regimen and HCC were analysed using competing-risk analysis. A total of 1437 patients (710 ETV, 727 TAF) were included, with similar mean follow-up durations (55.5 ± 29.8 vs. 58.0 ± 25.5 months; p = 0.077). ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis. After IPTW, both groups had balanced characteristics (all standardised differences < 0.1). After IPTW adjustment, during follow-up, 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively (p = 0.853). There was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent findings across subgroups by age, sex, cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, HBeAg, baseline liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, diabetes mellitus and in sensitivity analysis using PSM. In this real-world multinational study of treatment-naïve CHB patients, HCC incidence did not significantly differ between ETV and TAF groups, suggesting therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors.
abstract_zh: 关于恩替卡韦(ETV)和替诺福韦艾拉酚胺(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中对肝细胞癌(HCC)发病率潜在差异的数据有限。本回顾性多国研究纳入了2016年以来在4个国家的23个中心开始接受ETV或TAF治疗的、无HCC病史且未接受过抗病毒药物治疗的CHB成人患者。使用逆概率加权(IPTW)和倾向评分匹配(PSM)方法平衡基线特征。采用竞争风险分析方法分析HCC发病率及抗病毒治疗方案与HCC之间的关联。共纳入1437名患者(ETV组710名,TAF组727名),其平均随访时间相似(ETV组55.5 ± 29.8个月 vs. TAF组58.0 ± 25.5个月;p = 0.077)。接受ETV治疗的患者年龄更大,男性比例更高,且更可能患有肝硬化。在IPTW调整后,两组患者的特征趋于平衡(所有标准化差异均<0.1)。调整后随访期间,ETV组有23例患者和TAF组有20例患者发展为HCC,其HCC发病率分别为每100人年0.67和0.65(p = 0.853)。两组之间HCC风险无统计学显著差异(SHR:1.09;95% CI:0.44-2.65;p = 0.851),且在按年龄、性别、肝硬化、脂肪肝、HBeAg状态、基线肝酶水平、HBV DNA水平、糖尿病等亚组分析以及使用PSM进行敏感性分析中结果一致。在这一真实世界多国研究中,对于未接受过抗病毒治疗的CHB患者,ETV和TAF组的HCC发病率无显著差异,提示治疗选择应考虑成本和患者个体因素。

title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study. METHODS: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. RESULTS: At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. CONCLUSION: GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959.

title_zh: GST-HG131在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中的安全性、耐受性和功能性治愈活性:一项随机、双盲IIa期研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study. METHODS: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. RESULTS: At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. CONCLUSION: GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959.

title: Finite Versus Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy in HBeAg‐Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: Continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) effectively maintains viral suppression but rarely results in functional cure. Finite NA therapy has been proposed to increase rates of HBsAg loss; however, international guidelines provide conflicting recommendations. This study compares the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous NA therapy in HBeAg-negative adults using randomized controlled trials. We included parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) cessation versus continuation in non-cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg-negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. analysis.scope_and_question: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy in HBeAg-negative adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The central question is whether finite therapy increases the likelihood of HBsAg loss while maintaining viral suppression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review includes four parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing NA cessation versus continuation in non-cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg-negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Paule-Mandel estimation were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss compared to continuous therapy, although the evidence is of low certainty. The study found that discontinuation of therapy was associated with a risk ratio of 5.02 (95% CI: 0.47-53.47) for HBsAg loss, corresponding to approximately 53 additional losses per 1000 patients. However, finite therapy significantly increased virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94) while reducing sustained off-therapy virologic response (RR 0.46). No hepatic decompensation or serious adverse events were reported.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: International guidelines provide conflicting recommendations on finite versus continuous NA therapy. The evidence for HBsAg loss is of low certainty, and the wide confidence interval suggests uncertainty in the effect estimate. Additionally, the study does not address long-term outcomes or the impact of finite therapy on HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma or cirrhosis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the long-term safety and efficacy of finite NA therapy, particularly in relation to HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma and cirrhosis. The findings suggest that finite therapy could be considered as a selective strategy in expert centers for achieving functional cure, but more data are required to support its broader implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy in HBeAg-negative adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included, comparing NA cessation versus continuation in non-cirrhotic, virally suppressed patients. The study found that finite therapy may increase HBsAg loss, with a risk ratio of 5.02 (95% CI: 0.47-53.47), but also significantly raises the risk of virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94). Sustained off-therapy virologic response was reduced (RR 0.46). No serious adverse events were reported. The evidence is of low certainty, and international guidelines remain conflicting. These findings support finite therapy as a potential strategy for functional cure in expert settings, but further research is needed to address long-term outcomes and confirm its safety and efficacy across different disease manifestations.

title: Projected Effect of 2026 Federal Changes to the Childhood Immunization Schedule on Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infections in the United States.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections. DESIGN: Markov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection. DATA SOURCES: Published data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection. TARGET POPULATION: One-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million). TIME HORIZON: 20 years. INTERVENTION: Universal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making. OUTCOME MEASURES: Numbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis. RESULTS OF BASE-CASE ANALYSIS: Compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. These strategies would also increase the number of HBV-susceptible people at year 20 (474 000 and 1 806 000) compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (232 000). RESULTS OF SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS: In a scenario with lower vaccine coverage (84.5%) and higher HBV prevalence (maternal prevalence of 0.72% and higher risk for horizontal infection), chronic HBV infections would increase to 1700 and 2192, respectively, with the deferred and shared decision-making strategies. LIMITATION: Uncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk. CONCLUSION: Proposed policy changes for vaccination through shared decision making are projected to result in an 83% increase in childhood HBV infections, and between 50% and 70% of children entering adulthood annually would be susceptible to HBV infection. Policymakers should reimplement recommendations for universal birth-dose vaccination. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the potential impact of proposed changes to the U.S. childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination schedule on chronic HBV infections. Using a Markov cohort state transition model, the researchers projected outcomes for a one-year birth cohort of 3.6 million U.S.-born infants over a 20-year time horizon. The analysis compared three vaccination strategies: universal birth-dose, deferred (2-month), and shared decision-making. Results indicated that the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections by 19% and 83%, respectively, compared to the universal birth-dose strategy. Additionally, these strategies would lead to higher numbers of HBV-susceptible individuals at year 20. The study highlights the importance of maintaining universal birth-dose vaccination to prevent chronic HBV infections and emphasizes the need for policymakers to consider these projections when revising immunization guidelines. However, the findings are limited by uncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk, which affects the reliability of the projections.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过共享决策进行的疫苗接种接种政策调整预计会导致儿童HBV感染增加83%,并且每年有50%至70%的儿童进入成年时仍对HBV感染易感。

title: Long-term temporal trends in hepatitis B and C among blood donors in Brazil: Prevalence, incidence, and demographic correlates from the REDS multicenter program.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral hepatitis remains a major public health challenge. We evaluated long-term trends in hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, incidence, and force of infection (FOI) among blood donors from five Brazilian blood centers and investigated associated demographic factors. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Data from the NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study program were analyzed. Prevalence was estimated among 2,062,816 first-time donors for HBV (2008-2023) and 1,673,745 for HCV (2012-2023). Incidence was estimated among 1,346,256 repeat donors for HBV and 1,151,209 for HCV. Active HBV infection was defined by reactive HBsAg and anti-HBc or reactive HBV nucleic acid testing (NAT), and active HCV infection by reactive NAT. Historical FOI was estimated using a Bayesian serocatalytic model. RESULTS: Active infection prevalence was 136.2 per 100,000 donors (95% CI, 131.2-141.3) for HBV and 57.4 (95% CI, 53.8-61.1) for HCV. Incidence rates were 3.54 (95% CI, 3.01-4.11) and 3.99 (95% CI, 3.33-4.72) per 100,000 person-years, respectively. Prevalence decreased annually by 7.6% for HBV and 11.0% for HCV. Higher prevalence and incidence were associated with male sex, older age, lower educational attainment, and Black or mixed-race skin color. Regional differences persisted, and FOI declined markedly for both infections. DISCUSSION: HBV and HCV prevalence, incidence, and FOI declined substantially among Brazilian blood donors, suggesting reduced transmission, although improved donor selection and screening may also have contributed. Persistent demographic and regional disparities support continued surveillance and targeted prevention.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed long-term trends in hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, incidence, and force of infection among blood donors in Brazil from 2008 to 2023. It found that HBV and HCV prevalence and incidence decreased over time, with HBV prevalence dropping by 7.6% annually and HCV by 11.0%. The decline was associated with demographic factors such as male sex, older age, lower educational attainment, and Black or mixed-race skin color. Regional disparities persisted, and the force of infection for both viruses declined significantly. The authors suggest that reduced transmission may be due to improved donor selection and screening. These findings highlight the importance of continued surveillance and targeted prevention strategies to address persistent disparities in HBV and HCV infection rates among blood donors in Brazil.

title: Abstract C042: Awareness of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses as causes of cancer among U.S. adults: Findings from HINTS 7
abstract: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections are major causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet public awareness that these infections can cause cancer remains poorly characterized. We examined sociodemographic predictors of awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer among U.S. Methods: Data were analyzed from the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), a nationally representative survey of U.S. Two separate survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression models assessed factors associated with correctly identifying HCV and HBV as causes of cancer. Analyses incorporated jackknife replicate weights and adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, household income, rurality, Appalachian residence, health insurance status, self-rated health, and cancer history. Complete-case analysis was used for each model. Results: The sample included 7,278 U.S. After weighting, 50.8% were male, 48.4% were female, 60.6% were non-Hispanic White, 87.0% resided in urban areas, and 91.4% had health insurance. Approximately 16.7% correctly identified HCV as a cause of cancer, and 18.0% correctly identified HBV as a cause of cancer. Rurality, Appalachian residence, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance status, and cancer history were not independently associated with awareness. Conclusions: Awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer was low nationally, with fewer than one in five U.S. adults correctly identifying these associations. Lower educational attainment and older age were associated with lower awareness, highlighting priority populations for HCC prevention and viral hepatitis education efforts. Citation Format: Rachel A. Awareness of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses as causes of cancer among U.S. adults: Findings from HINTS 7 [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 19th AACR Conference on the Science of Cancer Health Disparities; 2026 Oct 18-21; Atlanta, GA. Philadelphia (PA): AACR; Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):Abstract nr C042.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)和乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是肝细胞癌(HCC)的主要病因,但公众对这些感染可能导致癌症的认知仍不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用2024年健康信息国家趋势调查(HINTS 7)的数据,研究了美国成年人中对HCV和HBV作为癌症病因的认知的社会人口学预测因素,HINTS 7是一项具有全国代表性的调查。
elements_zh.methods: 两个独立的加权多变量逻辑回归模型评估了正确识别HCV和HBV作为癌症病因的因素。分析采用了jackknife复制权重,并调整了年龄、性别、种族/民族、教育程度、家庭收入、农村地区居住、阿巴拉契亚地区居住、健康保险状况、自我评价健康状况和癌症史。每个模型均采用完整案例分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 样本包括7,278名美国成年人。加权后,50.8%为男性,48.4%为女性,60.6%为非西班牙裔白人,87.0%居住在城市地区,91.4%拥有健康保险。约16.7%正确识别HCV为癌症病因,18.0%正确识别HBV为癌症病因。农村地区居住、阿巴拉契亚地区居住、性别、种族/民族、保险状况和癌症史均未独立与认知相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 较低的教育水平和较大的年龄与较低的认知相关,突显了HCC预防和病毒性肝炎教育的重点人群。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了需要有针对性的教育努力以提高对HBV和HCV作为癌症病因的认知,尤其是在教育水平较低和年龄较大的人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于依赖自我报告数据和使用完整案例分析,这可能引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

title: Passive acquisition of hepatitis B virus antibodies after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 193 adults who underwent allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT. RESULTS: Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. Among patients receiving neither fresh frozen plasma nor intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-HBs concentrations increased significantly after HCT (p< .0001), with a greater increase among those receiving ≥24 versus ≤23 platelet transfusions (p = .0437). DISCUSSION: Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.

title: Hepatitis B surface antigen-targeting strategies for clearance: A review of progress from mechanistic exploration to clinical translation
abstract: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) persistence hinders the achievement of a functional cure in patients with chronic hepatitis B. Strategies to suppress or eliminate HBsAg and break the host immune tolerance while restoring immune response become key components of immune therapy-directed clinical cure.Agents that target HBsAg include monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, gene editing technologies, capsid assembly modulators, and therapeutic agents targeting secretion pathways.Immune checkpoint inhibitors and other immune-based clearance approaches are also included within this strategic framework.These agents target the HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, including covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA in the host genome.This article reviews these strategies by synthesizing the latest information from preclinical studies and clinical trials, summarises their mechanism and efficacy, discusses challenges and prospects for combinations, and aims to provide a scientific basis for chronic hepatitis B curative research.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on strategies to clear Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in patients with chronic hepatitis B, aiming to achieve a functional cure by suppressing or eliminating HBsAg and breaking host immune tolerance while restoring immune response.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes the latest information from preclinical studies and clinical trials, summarizing the mechanisms and efficacy of various agents targeting HBsAg, including monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, gene editing technologies, capsid assembly modulators, and therapeutic agents targeting secretion pathways. It also includes immune checkpoint inhibitors and other immune-based clearance approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that targeting HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, such as covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA in the host genome, is a key component of immune therapy-directed clinical cure. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies heterogeneity in the efficacy of different agents and challenges in combining strategies. It also notes the need for further research to address unresolved mechanisms and improve the outcomes of immune-based clearance approaches.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests specific priorities for research, including the development of more effective agents targeting HBsAg and its source templates, as well as the exploration of combination therapies to enhance immune response and achieve a functional cure.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores strategies for clearing Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in patients with chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing the importance of targeting HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, such as covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA. It synthesizes preclinical and clinical data on various agents, including monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, and immune checkpoint inhibitors, and discusses their mechanisms, efficacy, and challenges. The review highlights the need for further research to address heterogeneity in treatment responses and to develop more effective combination therapies. These findings provide a scientific basis for advancing curative research in chronic hepatitis B.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 综述聚焦于清除慢性乙型肝炎患者中的乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(HBsAg)的策略,旨在通过抑制或清除HBsAg并打破免疫耐受、恢复免疫应答来实现功能性治愈。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 综述综合了预临床研究和临床试验的最新信息,总结了针对HBsAg的各种药物的机制和疗效,包括单克隆抗体、小干扰RNA、反义寡核苷酸、基因编辑技术、衣壳组装调节剂以及靶向分泌途径的治疗药物。它还涵盖了免疫检查点抑制剂和其他基于免疫的清除方法。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述强调,靶向HBsAg生命周期及其来源模板,如共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)和整合在宿主基因组中的乙型肝炎病毒DNA,是免疫治疗导向临床治愈的关键组成部分。它讨论了这些策略组合的挑战与前景。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出不同药物在疗效上的异质性以及策略组合的挑战。它还提到需要进一步研究以解决未明确的机制并改善基于免疫的清除方法的疗效。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议了具体的研究优先事项,包括开发更有效的针对HBsAg及其来源模板的药物,以及探索组合疗法以增强免疫应答并实现功能性治愈。

title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)]. RESULTS: At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.

abstract_zh: 背景:肝细胞癌(HCC)是全球癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一。丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)是病毒性肝炎中最严重的形式。然而,与HDV相关的HCC的临床、病毒学和全身炎症特征仍不够明确。方法:本研究为单中心回顾性研究,纳入了162例因慢性乙型肝炎(HBV-HCC;n=108)或慢性丁型肝炎(HDV-HCC;n=54)导致的HCC患者。使用邻近扩展检测法(proximity extension assay)对HCC患者的血浆中92种可溶性炎症介质(SIMs)水平进行了定量分析,包括50例HBV-HCC、30例HDV-HCC以及匹配的非HCC对照组(HBV=19,HDV=17)。结果:在HCC诊断时,慢性乙型肝炎患者年龄较小,肝合成和解毒功能受损更严重,AST、CRP和白细胞水平较低。HDV-HCC肿瘤体积较小,门静脉浸润较少见,且更常符合米兰标准(所有p<0.01)。全身免疫特征分析显示两种病因的HCC具有不同的炎症模式。与HBV-HCC相比,HDV-HCC表现出更强的IL-10相关免疫调节特征,而HBV-HCC则表现出更显著的促炎特征,涉及IL-6和磷酸化及增殖相关信号。尽管存在这些差异,各组的无事件生存率没有显著差异。结论:HBV-HCC更常表现为晚期肿瘤阶段,而HDV-HCC则与更严重的潜在肝病但较小的肿瘤相关。重要的是,HBV相关和HDV相关的HCC表现出不同的全身炎症特征,这可能反映了两种病因之间系统性免疫调节的差异。这些发现可能对生物标志物的开发和未来针对病因的治疗策略具有重要意义。

title: Comprehensive Prevention and Control Service Capacity for Hepatitis B in Medical and Health Institutions: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Jiangsu Province, China
abstract: Abstract Background Despite substantial progress in hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevention in China, important gaps remain in diagnosis, referral, treatment, and long-term follow-up. To further strengthen viral hepatitis prevention and control, the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention formulated the Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Viral Hepatitis in China (2025–2030) in 2025. Jiangsu Province is classified as a region with moderate endemicity of HBV in China. The capacity of medical and health institutions to deliver comprehensive HBV prevention and control services is essential for effective implementation of HBV control strategies. This study aimed to assess the capacity of medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province across key components of the HBV prevention and control service chain, including testing, diagnosis reporting, referral, antiviral treatment and follow-up management. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across all 13 prefecture-level cities in Jiangsu Province, encompassing 183 medical and health institutions—comprising 135 hospitals and 48 disease control and prevention centers (CDCs). The survey encompassed the following core items: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing, HBV-DNA testing, case diagnosis, case referral, antiviral treatment, patient follow-up, and public health prevention and control initiatives implemented by CDCs. Results Among the 183 surveyed institutions, 86.9% (159/183) reported having the capacity to perform HBsAg testing. In 2025, a total of 3.75 million HBsAg tests had been completed, over 90% of which were carried out in tertiary hospitals. HBV-DNA testing was available in 56.8% (104/183) of the surveyed institutions, and all primary hospitals offering this service outsource testing to independent clinical laboratories. Case referral services were provided by 37.2% (68/183) of the institutions, with antiviral treatment resources highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals. Follow-up management was implemented in 34.1% (46/135) of hospitals, mainly among tertiary hospitals. Conclusion Medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province have established relatively strong capacity for HBV laboratory testing, particularly for HBsAg testing. However, HBV treatment and follow-up services remain highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals, indicating limited participation of primary-level institutions in long-term HBV management. Future efforts should focus on strengthening the HBV prevention and control service chain by unifying clinical diagnostic criteria, enhancing referral mechanisms, expanding grassroots follow-up capacity, and promoting coordinated information sharing between healthcare institutions and CDCs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the capacity of medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province to deliver comprehensive HBV prevention and control services, addressing gaps in diagnosis, referral, treatment, and follow-up management despite progress in HBV prevention in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted across 13 prefecture-level cities in Jiangsu Province, encompassing 183 medical and health institutions, including 135 hospitals and 48 disease control and prevention centers.
analysis.methods: The survey assessed the capacity for HBsAg testing, HBV-DNA testing, case diagnosis, referral, antiviral treatment, patient follow-up, and public health prevention and control initiatives implemented by CDCs.
analysis.main_results: Among the 183 surveyed institutions, 86.9% reported having the capacity to perform HBsAg testing, while HBV-DNA testing was available in 56.8% of institutions, and follow-up management was implemented in 34.1% of hospitals, mainly among tertiary hospitals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that while HBV laboratory testing capacity, particularly for HBsAg testing, is strong, HBV treatment and follow-up services remain highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals, indicating limited participation of primary-level institutions in long-term HBV management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for future efforts to strengthen the HBV prevention and control service chain by unifying clinical diagnostic criteria, enhancing referral mechanisms, expanding grassroots follow-up capacity, and promoting coordinated information sharing between healthcare institutions and CDCs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The survey's reliance on self-reported data may introduce bias, and the high concentration of HBV treatment and follow-up services in tertiary hospitals limits the generalizability of the findings to primary-level institutions.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the capacity of medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province to deliver comprehensive HBV prevention and control services. While HBsAg testing capacity is strong, HBV treatment and follow-up services are concentrated in tertiary hospitals, indicating a need for future efforts to improve long-term management in primary-level institutions.

title_zh: 江苏省医疗和健康机构乙型肝炎综合预防与控制服务能力调查:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Despite substantial progress in hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevention in China, important gaps remain in diagnosis, referral, treatment, and long-term follow-up. To further strengthen viral hepatitis prevention and control, the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention formulated the Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Viral Hepatitis in China (2025–2030) in 2025. Jiangsu Province is classified as a region with moderate endemicity of HBV in China. The capacity of medical and health institutions to deliver comprehensive HBV prevention and control services is essential for effective implementation of HBV control strategies. This study aimed to assess the capacity of medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province across key components of the HBV prevention and control service chain, including testing, diagnosis reporting, referral, antiviral treatment and follow-up management. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across all 13 prefecture-level cities in Jiangsu Province, encompassing 183 medical and health institutions—comprising 135 hospitals and 48 disease control and prevention centers (CDCs). The survey encompassed the following core items: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing, HBV-DNA testing, case diagnosis, case referral, antiviral treatment, patient follow-up, and public health prevention and control initiatives implemented by CDCs. Results Among the 183 surveyed institutions, 86.9% (159/183) reported having the capacity to perform HBsAg testing. In 2025, a total of 3.75 million HBsAg tests had been completed, over 90% of which were carried out in tertiary hospitals. HBV-DNA testing was available in 56.8% (104/183) of the surveyed institutions, and all primary hospitals offering this service outsource testing to independent clinical laboratories. Case referral services were provided by 37.2% (68/183) of the institutions, with antiviral treatment resources highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals. Follow-up management was implemented in 34.1% (46/135) of hospitals, mainly among tertiary hospitals. Conclusion Medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province have established relatively strong capacity for HBV laboratory testing, particularly for HBsAg testing. However, HBV treatment and follow-up services remain highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals, indicating limited participation of primary-level institutions in long-term HBV management. Future efforts should focus on strengthening the HBV prevention and control service chain by unifying clinical diagnostic criteria, enhancing referral mechanisms, expanding grassroots follow-up capacity, and promoting coordinated information sharing between healthcare institutions and CDCs.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

title: Patient-reported treatment burden, communication, and persistence intention during add-on peginterferon alfa-2b therapy for chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Add-on peginterferon alfa-2b (Peg-IFN) may help reduce hepatitis B surface antigen levels and achieve a functional cure in selected patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but the treatment burden can make a finite course difficult to complete. We examined the patient-reported factors associated with thoughts of discontinuation and intentions to persist with treatment during add-on Peg-IFN therapy. Methods This anonymous cross-sectional online survey used outcome-specific analytic populations. All 412 eligible respondents were included in discontinuation-related analyses, and the primary persistence analysis included 289 respondents who were still receiving Peg-IFN. The main outcomes included whether respondents had ever wanted to stop Peg-IFN due to adverse effects and a four-item persistence/value intention score. Psychological distress was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4). Results Among 412 eligible respondents, 175 (42.5%) had wanted to stop Peg-IFN because of adverse effects, 136 (33.0%) had asked a physician about dose reduction or discontinuation, and 39 (9.5%) reported actual premature discontinuation. In the adjusted analysis, adverse-effect burden (odds ratio 1.86 per standard deviation (SD), 95% confidence interval 1.37–2.51) and the PHQ-4 score (odds ratio 1.76, 95% confidence interval 1.28–2.41) were associated with a history of adverse-effect-related discontinuation thoughts. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究调查了在接受附加peginterferon alfa-2b(Peg-IFN)治疗的慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中,患者报告的与治疗负担、沟通和持续治疗意愿相关的因素。核心问题是不良反应负担和心理压力是否与中断治疗的想法相关,以及治疗信念和医患沟通是否与持续治疗意愿相关。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本横断面研究使用了匿名在线调查,并基于结果分析了特定人群。主要的持续分析包括289名仍在接受Peg-IFN治疗的受访者,而中断相关分析包括所有412名符合条件的受访者。主要结果包括受访者是否因不良反应想要停止Peg-IFN治疗,以及一个包含四项的持续/价值意愿评分。心理压力通过患者健康问卷-4(PHQ-4)进行评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 不良反应负担和当前心理压力与不良反应相关中断治疗的想法有关。相比之下,治疗信念和医患沟通与仍在接受治疗的患者更高的持续/价值意愿相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究未探讨HBV基因型对治疗负担或持续治疗意愿的潜在影响。此外,它也未研究其他因素如社会经济状况、文化影响或治疗依从策略在塑造患者行为中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要前瞻性研究来评估结构化教育、症状和压力筛查以及分级随访是否能提高治疗治疗的完成率。这些干预措施对于支持患者应对Peg-IFN治疗的挑战可能是关键的。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本横断面研究使用了匿名在线调查,并基于结果分析了特定人群。主要的持续分析包括289名仍在接受Peg-IFN治疗的受访者,而中断相关分析包括所有412名符合条件的受访者。主要结果包括受访者是否因不良反应想要停止Peg-IFN治疗,以及一个包含四项的持续/价值意愿评分。心理压力通过患者健康问卷-4(PHQ-4)进行评估。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 不良反应负担和当前心理压力与不良反应相关中断治疗的想法有关。相比之下,治疗信念和医患沟通与仍在接受治疗的患者更高的持续/价值意愿相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究未探讨HBV基因型对治疗负担或持续治疗意愿的潜在影响。此外,它也未研究其他因素如社会经济状况、文化影响或治疗依从策略在塑造患者行为中的作用。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要前瞻性研究来评估结构化教育、症状和压力筛查以及分级随访是否能提高治疗治疗的完成率。这些干预措施对于支持患者应对Peg-IFN治疗的挑战可能是关键的。

title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people.The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs.In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospitalbased testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals;(2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

priority_tier_reason: 高相关性，且具备高等级研究设计、全文证据或较强数据库/引用支持
relevance_llm_reason: The record reports on HBV testing and prevalence in Italy, which is directly relevant to the target hepatitis B virus.
abstract_original: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people.The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs.In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospitalbased testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals;(2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.
title_original: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, genotypes, and associated diseases. It examines the current testing scenarios and management strategies for HBV in Italy, with an emphasis on improving testing and linkage to care. The central question is how to enhance the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy, particularly for HBV, through coordinated efforts and targeted interventions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an expert-opinion piece summarizing the experience of tertiary-level Italian centers involved in hospital-based testing for HBV, HCV, and HDV. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or meta-analysis methods. The review is based on the authors' expertise and the practices observed in Italian healthcare settings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, the implementation of centralized reporting systems, and the expansion of testing in high-risk populations. It also emphasizes the importance of providing resources to public addiction treatment services and prisons to enhance HBV testing and management. These measures are proposed to help Italy achieve its goals of eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps specific to HBV. It focuses on identifying practical pathways to improve testing and management without addressing conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to HBV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes specific priorities for research, surveillance, and practice, including strengthening coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, implementing a centralized reporting system, increasing testing in public addiction treatment services and prisons, promoting screening in high-risk populations, and launching a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These recommendations aim to improve the effectiveness of HBV management in Italy.

analysis.summary_en: This expert-opinion review addresses the current testing scenarios and management strategies for hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Italy. It highlights the importance of HBV testing and the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners. The review proposes measures such as implementing a centralized reporting system, increasing testing in high-risk populations, and launching a national awareness campaign to enhance HBV management. These recommendations aim to support Italy's efforts to control HBV infection and align with its public health goals. The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps but focuses on actionable priorities for research and practice.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染、基因型及其相关疾病。它考察了意大利当前HBV的检测状况和管理策略,特别强调了如何通过协调努力和针对性干预来提高HBV的检测和治疗连接性。核心问题是:如何通过协调努力和针对性干预提高意大利病毒性肝炎的管理效果,特别是针对HBV。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一篇专家意见文章,总结了意大利三级医疗机构在医院内进行HBV、HCV和HDV检测的经验。它并未报告特定数据库、搜索日期、纳入标准或元分析方法。综述基于作者的专业知识和在意大利医疗环境中的观察实践。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述强调了改善医院单位与全科医生之间协调的必要性,实施集中报告系统,并扩大高风险人群的检测。它还强调了为公共成瘾治疗服务和监狱提供资源以增强HBV检测和管理的重要性。这些措施被提议以帮助意大利在未来十年内实现消除HCV感染和控制HBV/HDV感染的目标。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述未报告与HBV相关的具体争议或证据缺口。它专注于识别改进检测和管理的可行途径,而未涉及与HBV相关的矛盾发现或未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了针对研究、监测和实践的具体优先事项,包括加强医院单位与全科医生之间的协调,实施集中报告系统,增加公共成瘾治疗服务和监狱中的检测,推广高风险人群的筛查,并启动全国性的病毒性肝炎意识宣传活动。这些建议旨在提高意大利HBV的管理效果。

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. The research was conducted across six countries involving 1601 participants, with 421 (26.3%) found to have SLD and 219 (13.7%) with severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). title: Becoming Physically Active and Risks of Mortality and Liver-Related Events in Adults With Chronic Hepatitis B: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear. We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database. We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2). Among them, 58,703 initiated moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcomes were liver-related events (hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma [HCC]) and HCC. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Grey competing-risk models were adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioural factors. During a median 7.9-year follow-up (IQR, 5.2-9.5), 7609 deaths occurred. MVPA initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), a lower risk of liver-related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared with those remaining inactive. The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03). Initiating MVPA among physically inactive adults with CHB was associated with lower risks of mortality and liver-related outcomes. These findings provide large-scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between initiating moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and reduced risks of mortality and liver-related events in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Using the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database, the researchers followed 318,131 physically inactive adults with CHB over a median of 7.9 years. They found that MVPA initiation was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), reduced liver-related events (subHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and a modest decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared to those who remained inactive. The associations were stronger in specific subgroups, including older adults, women, and untreated participants. The study highlights the potential public health significance of promoting physical activity in CHB patients, though it does not provide direct causal evidence.

title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 成人的体力活动和 死亡率 风险以及肝脏相关事件:一项全国范围的 队列研究 研究。
source_body_en: Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear. We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database. We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2). Among them, 58,703 initiated moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcomes were liver-related events (hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma [HCC]) and HCC. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Grey competing-risk models were adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioural factors. During a median 7.9-year follow-up (IQR, 5.2-9.5), 7609 deaths occurred. MVPA initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), a lower risk of liver-related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared with those remaining inactive. The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03). Initiating MVPA among physically inactive adults with CHB was associated with lower risks of mortality and liver-related outcomes. These findings provide large-scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.

title: Abstract C081: Immigration history and acculturation-related factors in relation to health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms among Korean American patients with Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB)
abstract: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) disproportionately affects Asian Americans, especially Korean Americans, and increases risk for long-term complications, including liver cancer. Immigration history, such as age/life stage at U.S. arrival, and acculturation-related factors, such as English proficiency and cultural identity, may shape physical and mental health-related quality of life among individuals living with CHB, but these relationships remain understudied. We examined whether these factors are associated with physical and mental health-related quality of life, and depressive symptoms among Korean American patients with CHB. Methods: We used baseline survey data collected in 2022-2023 from 365 Korean American CHB patients receiving care at two clinical settings in Philadelphia and Los Angeles. Outcomes were the SF-12v2 Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS) scores, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) depressive-symptom score. Results: Participants had a mean age of 60.1 years and were 55.6% male and predominantly foreign-born (82.9%), with most arriving in the U.S. Overall mean PCS, MCS, and PHQ-9 scores were 48.56±7.25, 47.65±7.00, and 3.66±4.16, respectively. Age/life stage at arrival was significantly associated with PCS (p≤0.001), but not MCS or PHQ-9. PCS was highest among U.S.-born participants (53.81±4.72) and those who arrived during childhood or adolescence (51.99±5.28), and lower among adult arrivals ages 18–34 (48.07±7.29) and ages 35 years or older (47.16±7.56). English proficiency was associated with PCS (p≤0.001), MCS (p≤0.05), and PHQ-9 (p≤0.05); participants with poor or no English proficiency had the lowest PCS (45.68±8.07) and highest PHQ-9 scores (4.48±4.89). Cultural identity was associated with PCS (p<0.001), with the highest PCS among mostly or very Westernized participants (53.35±3.91) and the lowest PCS among very/mostly Korean participants (47.66±7.48). Multivariable analyses will examine whether these relationships remain after adjustment for sociodemographic factors. Conclusions: Immigration history and acculturation-related factors were most consistently associated with physical health-related quality of life. English proficiency was also related to mental health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms. These preliminary findings highlight the value of culturally and linguistically responsive support in CHB care and liver cancer prevention for Asian American communities. Citation Format: Eunji Kim, Ann Klassen, Giyoung Lee, Amy Auchincloss, Sandra Bloom, Stephanie Ewing, Mimi Chang, Kyunghee Koh, Hee-Soon Juon. Immigration history and acculturation-related factors in relation to health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms among Korean American patients with Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 19th AACR Conference on the Science of Cancer Health Disparities; 2026 Oct 18-21; Atlanta, GA. Philadelphia (PA): AACR; Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):Abstract nr C081.

We examined whether these factors are associated with physical and mental health-related quality of life, and depressive symptoms among Korean American patients with CHB. We used baseline survey data collected in 2022-2023 from 365 Korean American CHB patients receiving care at two clinical settings in Philadelphia and Los Angeles. Outcomes were the SF-12v2 Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS) scores, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) depressive-symptom score. Participants had a mean age of 60.1 years and were 55.6% male and predominantly foreign-born (82.9%), with most arriving in the U.S. Overall mean PCS, MCS, and PHQ-9 scores were 48.56±7.25, 47.65±7.00, and 3.66±4.16, respectively. Age/life stage at arrival was significantly associated with PCS (p≤0.001), but not MCS or PHQ-9. PCS was highest among U.S.-born participants (53.81±4.72) and those who arrived during childhood or adolescence (51.99±5.28), and lower among adult arrivals ages 18–34 (48.07±7.29) and ages 35 years or older (47.16±7.56). Multivariable analyses will examine whether these relationships remain after adjustment for sociodemographic factors. Immigration history and acculturation-related factors were most consistently associated with physical health-related quality of life. English proficiency was also related to mental health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms. These preliminary findings highlight the value of culturally and linguistically responsive support in CHB care and liver cancer prevention for Asian American communities. analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates how immigration history and acculturation-related factors influence physical and mental health-related quality of life and depressive symptoms among Korean American patients with chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional survey of 365 Korean American CHB patients conducted in 2022–2023 at two clinical sites in Philadelphia and Los Angeles, measuring SF‐12v2 PCS/MCS and PHQ‐9 scores.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Older age at arrival and higher English proficiency were consistently linked to better physical health‐related quality of life; English proficiency also correlated with better mental health‐related quality of life and lower depressive symptoms. Cultural identity showed a similar pattern for physical health.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Associations were identified in unadjusted analyses; multivariable analyses are pending, and the cross‐sectional design limits causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This cross‐sectional survey of 365 Korean American patients with chronic hepatitis B examined how immigration history and acculturation factors affect health‐related quality of life and depressive symptoms. Older age at arrival and better English proficiency were linked to higher physical health‐related quality of life, while English proficiency also related to better mental health and fewer depressive symptoms. Cultural identity similarly influenced physical health. The study’s unadjusted analyses and cross‐sectional design limit causal conclusions, and multivariable analyses are forthcoming. The results highlight the importance of culturally and linguistically responsive care for Asian American CHB patients and liver cancer prevention.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)主要影响亚洲裔美国人,尤其是韩国裔美国人,并增加长期并发症(包括肝癌)的风险。移民史(如抵达美国时的年龄/人生阶段)以及与适应相关因素(如英语熟练程度和文化认同)可能影响患有CHB的人群的身心健康相关生活质量,但这些关系尚未得到充分研究。我们探讨了这些因素是否与韩国裔美国人慢性乙型肝炎患者的身心健康相关生活质量及抑郁症状相关。方法:我们使用了2022-2023年从费城和洛杉矶两家临床机构收集的365名韩国裔美国人慢性乙型肝炎患者的基线调查数据。结果:参与者平均年龄为60.1岁,其中55.6%为男性,且大多数为出生在国外(82.9%),大部分在抵达美国时处于不同年龄段。总体平均的SF-12v2身体成分总结(PCS)得分、心理成分总结(MCS)得分和PHQ-9抑郁症状得分分别为48.56±7.25、47.65±7.00和3.66±4.16。抵达美国时的年龄/人生阶段与PCS显著相关(p≤0.001),但与MCS或PHQ-9无显著相关性。PCS得分最高的是美国出生的参与者(53.81±4.72)以及在童年或青少年时期抵达的参与者(51.99±5.28),而18-34岁成人抵达的参与者(48.07±7.29)和35岁及以上成人抵达的参与者(47.16±7.56)得分较低。英语熟练程度与PCS(p≤0.001)、MCS(p≤0.05)和PHQ-9(p≤0.05)均相关;英语熟练程度差或没有的参与者PCS得分最低(45.68±8.07),PHQ-9得分最高(4.48±4.89)。文化认同与PCS相关(p<0.001),其中主要或非常西方化的参与者PCS得分最高(53.35±3.91),而非常或主要韩国化的参与者PCS得分最低(47.66±7.48)。多变量分析将探讨这些关系在调整社会人口学因素后是否仍然存在。结论:移民史和与适应相关因素最一致地与身体相关的健康生活质量相关。英语熟练程度也与心理健康相关生活质量及抑郁症状相关。这些初步发现强调了为亚洲裔美国人社区提供文化及语言适应性支持在慢性乙型肝炎治疗和肝癌预防中的重要性。引用格式:Eunji Kim,Ann Klassen,Giyoung Lee,Amy Auchincloss,Sandra Bloom,Stephanie Ewing,Mimi Chang,Kyunghee Koh,Hee-Soon Juon. 韩国裔美国人慢性乙型肝炎患者移民史及与适应相关因素与健康相关生活质量及抑郁症状的关系 [摘要]. 出处:第19届AACR癌症健康差异科学会议论文集;2026年10月18-21日;佐治亚州亚特兰大市。费城(PA):AACR;Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):摘要编号C081。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 一项2022–2023年在费城和洛杉矶两家临床机构进行的横断面调查,收集了365名韩国裔美国人慢性乙型肝炎患者的资料,测量了SF-12v2 PCS/MCS和PHQ-9得分。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 抵达美国时的年龄较大和较高的英语熟练程度与更好的身体相关健康生活质量一致相关;英语熟练程度也与更好的心理健康相关生活质量及较低的抑郁症状相关。文化认同在身体相关健康方面也表现出类似模式。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在未调整分析中发现了相关性;多变量分析尚未完成,横断面设计限制了因果推论。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现强调了为亚洲裔美国人社区提供文化及语言适应性支持在慢性乙型肝炎治疗和肝癌预防中的必要性。

title: Whole-Brain Magnetic Susceptibility Alterations in Minimal Hepatic Encephalopathy Associated With Hepatitis B Virus-Related Decompensated Cirrhosis
abstract: Abstract Minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE) is a clinically covert complication of cirrhosis, but its whole-brain magnetic susceptibility pattern remains incompletely characterized. We investigated regional relative susceptibility in 31 healthy controls (HCs), 26 patients with hepatitis B virus-related decompensated cirrhosis without MHE (NMHE), and 13 patients with MHE. Multi-echo 3.0-T gradient-echo data were reconstructed using quantitative susceptibility mapping, and 249 regional labels were analyzed with nonparametric pairwise tests and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Twenty-one labels differed between HCs and MHE and 21 between HCs and NMHE, whereas no label differed between MHE and NMHE after FDR correction. Seven cortical regions were shared by both patient-versus-control comparisons and showed a numerical HC

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the whole-brain magnetic susceptibility pattern in minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE), a covert complication of cirrhosis, particularly in the context of hepatitis B virus-related disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared 31 healthy controls (HCs), 26 patients with hepatitis B virus-related decompensated cirrhosis without MHE (NMHE), and 13 patients with MHE to identify regional susceptibility differences.
analysis.methods: Quantitative susceptibility mapping was used to analyze multi-echo 3.0-T gradient-echo data, with nonparametric pairwise tests and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied to 249 regional labels.
analysis.main_results: Twenty-one regional labels showed differences between HCs and MHE, and 21 between HCs and NMHE, but no labels differed between MHE and NMHE after FDR correction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest distinct susceptibility patterns in MHE compared to healthy controls and non-MHE cirrhosis patients, highlighting potential neuroimaging biomarkers for MHE detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of non-invasive neuroimaging techniques for early detection of MHE in patients with hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence is based on statistical comparisons without detailed clinical or biological mechanisms, resulting in moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whole-brain magnetic susceptibility patterns in patients with hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis, focusing on minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE). Using quantitative susceptibility mapping, the researchers compared 31 healthy controls, 26 patients without MHE, and 13 patients with MHE. They identified 21 regional labels differing between healthy controls and MHE patients, and 21 between healthy controls and non-MHE cirrhosis patients. However, no differences were observed between MHE and non-MHE groups after false discovery rate correction. The findings suggest distinct susceptibility patterns in MHE, potentially offering neuroimaging biomarkers for early detection. The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are interpreted with moderate confidence due to the absence of detailed clinical or biological mechanisms.

title_zh: 与乙型肝炎病毒相关失代偿性肝硬化中伴发的轻微肝性脑病的全脑磁化率改变
source_body_en: Abstract Minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE) is a clinically covert complication of cirrhosis, but its whole-brain magnetic susceptibility pattern remains incompletely characterized. We investigated regional relative susceptibility in 31 healthy controls (HCs), 26 patients with hepatitis B virus-related decompensated cirrhosis without MHE (NMHE), and 13 patients with MHE. Multi-echo 3.0-T gradient-echo data were reconstructed using quantitative susceptibility mapping, and 249 regional labels were analyzed with nonparametric pairwise tests and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Twenty-one labels differed between HCs and MHE and 21 between HCs and NMHE, whereas no label differed between MHE and NMHE after FDR correction. Seven cortical regions were shared by both patient-versus-control comparisons and showed a numerical HC
abstract_zh: 摘要 轻微肝性脑病(MHE)是肝硬化的一种临床隐匿性并发症,但其全脑磁化率模式仍未被完全阐明。我们研究了31名健康对照(HCs)、26名无MHE的乙型肝炎病毒相关失代偿性肝硬化患者(NMHE)以及13名MHE患者的区域相对磁化率差异。使用定量磁化率映射分析多回波3.0-T梯度回波数据,并对249个区域标签进行非参数成对检验和Benjamini-Hochberg假发现率(FDR)校正。在FDR校正后,HCs与MHE之间有21个标签存在差异,HCs与NMHE之间有21个标签存在差异,而MHE与NMHE之间没有标签存在差异。七个皮层区域在两种患者与对照的比较中均有重叠,并显示出数值上的HC差异。

title: Hepatitis B vaccination and neonatal mortality in the United States
abstract: We estimate the plausibly causal effect of hepatitis B birth dose vaccination on neonatal mortality using U.S. county-level panel data (2011–2019) and a shift-share instrument that interacts historical fertility rates with national vaccine price variation. With county fixed effects and a control for the historical fertility share interacted with a linear trend, a one percentage point increase in birth dose coverage reduces 0–3 day mortality by 0.022 deaths per 1,000 live births, representing a 1.04% decline at the mean. The effect is concentrated in the first day of life and is indistinguishable from zero at later infant ages, a profile consistent either with an early life mechanism or with an administrative one, and we identify neither. The estimate is an unweighted county average conditional on a linear fertility trend, and we report the diagnostics that qualify it alongside those that support it.
