title: Exploratory associations of gut microbiota composition with HBeAg and HBsAg status in nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B
abstract: ABSTRACT HBeAg and HBsAg reflect viral replication and host immune status and are important determinants of treatment responsiveness in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The gut microbiota, a key component of the gut-liver axis, may influence immune regulation and antiviral outcomes. This study characterized gut microbiota profiles across different HBeAg and HBsAg statuses in CHB patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. Fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 29 healthy controls (HC) and 101 NA-treated CHB patients without cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, including 30 HBeAg-positive (EP) and 71 HBeAg-negative (EN) individuals. The EN group was further stratified by serum HBsAg levels into an advantageous subgroup (<1,500 IU/mL, n = 57) and a non-advantageous subgroup (≥1,500 IU/mL, n = 14). Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly among EP, EN, and HC groups. Species-level analyses identified nominal group-related differences in several Bacteroidales- and Firmicutes-associated anaerobic commensals, including Bacteroides uniformis, Blautia obeum, Eubacterium ventriosum, Anaerobutyricum, and Parabacteroides timonensis; however, none remained significant after global FDR correction across all detected species. Within the EN group, selected taxa showed directionally consistent associations with HBsAg strata in downsampling, leave-one-out, and CLR-based sensitivity analyses, but these subgroup findings also did not remain significant after FDR correction. NA-treated CHB was associated with exploratory taxonomic differences without detectable loss of microbial diversity. The observed associations with HBeAg status and HBsAg burden were hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger longitudinal cohorts incorporating absolute microbial quantification, targeted metabolomics, host immune profiling, and more complete dietary, anthropometric, and other relevant clinical covariates.

Using fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing, the study analyzed 29 healthy controls and 101 CHB patients, including 30 HBeAg-positive and 71 HBeAg-negative individuals. The EN group was further divided based on HBsAg levels. While some nominal differences in microbial taxa were observed, none remained significant after FDR correction. The study's limitations include the lack of statistical significance and insufficient clinical data, which reduce the strength of the evidence.

analysis_zh.main_results: EP、EN和HC组的α多样性和β多样性均无显著差异。种群水平分析发现,与Bacteroidales和Firmicutes相关的厌氧共生菌存在组间差异,但这些差异在全局FDR校正后均不显著。在EN组中,选定的菌群在下采样、留一法和CLR基础上的敏感性分析中显示出方向一致的关联,但这些发现同样在FDR校正后不显著。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 观察到的与HBeAg状态和HBsAg负担的关联具有假设生成性,提示肠道微生物群可能与CHB患者的病毒结果存在潜在联系,但需要进一步验证。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来研究肠道微生物群在CHB进展和治疗应答中的作用提供信息,可能有助于开发基于微生物群的生物标志物或干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 观察到的关联在FDR校正后均不具有统计学意义,且本研究缺乏纵向数据、绝对微生物定量以及全面的临床协变量,限制了证据的强度。

title: Serum hepatitis B virus markers reflect intrahepatic covalently closed circular DNA and transcriptional activity across chronic hepatitis B phases
abstract: BACKGROUND Covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) maintains hepatitis B virus (HBV) persistence through its transcriptional activity.While cccDNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) are central to HBV replication, serum markers reflecting active cccDNA remain poorly defined across the phases of chronic hepatitis B (CHB).AIM To identify serum markers reflecting intrahepatic cccDNA and its activity, we analyzed a large CHB cohort encompassing all immunological phases.METHODS Samples from 406 treatment-naïve CHB patients were analyzed by disease phase, including 56 hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-positive chronic HBV infection (EPCI), 153 HBeAg-positive-chronic hepatitis B (EPCH), 83 HBeAg-negative chronic HBV infection (ENCI), and 114 HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (ENCH).Serum markers [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg), and HBV RNA]and intrahepatic markers (cccDNA and pgRNA) were quantified with commercial assays.Transcriptional activity was evaluated in patients with comparable intrahepatic cccDNA levels. RESULTSAll serum and intrahepatic markers were inversely associated with age and were higher in HBeAg-positive than in HBeAg-negative patients.Correlations among serum and intrahepatic markers appeared higher in HBeAg-positive patients.Serum markers correlated more closely with pgRNA than with cccDNA.Serum HBcrAg and HBV RNA better reflected intrahepatic markers than HBsAg.Among 120 patients with comparable 5 / 34 cccDNA levels, intrahepatic cccDNA transcriptional activity (pgRNA/cccDNA) varied across CHB phases: Highest in EPCI, lowest in ENCI, moderate in EPCH, and reelevated in ENCH.HBcrAg and HBV RNA showed stronger associations with cccDNA transcriptional activity than HBsAg across the EPCH and ENCH phases.Notably, no serum marker reliably reflected pgRNA or transcriptional activity in the ENCI phase. CONCLUSIONHBcrAg and HBV RNA are phase-dependent surrogates of transcriptionally active cccDNA.The lack of reliable markers in ENCI highlights its virologic heterogeneity.These findings support phase-specific monitoring and treatment decisions.

RESULTSAll serum and intrahepatic markers were inversely associated with age and were higher in HBeAg-positive than in HBeAg-negative patients.Correlations among serum and intrahepatic markers appeared higher in HBeAg-positive patients.Serum markers correlated more closely with pgRNA than with cccDNA.Serum HBcrAg and HBV RNA better reflected intrahepatic markers than HBsAg.Among 120 patients with comparable 5 / 34 cccDNA levels, intrahepatic cccDNA transcriptional activity (pgRNA/cccDNA) varied across CHB phases: Highest in EPCI, lowest in ENCI, moderate in EPCH, and reelevated in ENCH.HBcrAg and HBV RNA showed stronger associations with cccDNA transcriptional activity than HBsAg across the EPCH and ENCH phases.Notably, no serum marker reliably reflected pgRNA or transcriptional activity in the ENCI phase. CONCLUSIONHBcrAg and HBV RNA are phase-dependent surrogates of transcriptionally active cccDNA.The lack of reliable markers in ENCI highlights its virologic heterogeneity.These findings support phase-specific monitoring and treatment decisions.

title_original: Serum hepatitis B virus markers reflect intrahepatic covalently closed circular DNA and transcriptional activity across chronic hepatitis B phases

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify serum markers reflecting intrahepatic cccDNA and its transcriptional activity across the phases of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The background highlights the need for better understanding of serum markers that correlate with cccDNA, which is central to HBV persistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed samples from 406 treatment-naïve CHB patients, categorized by immunological phases: 56 HBeAg-positive chronic HBV infection (EPCI), 153 HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B (EPCH), 83 HBeAg-negative chronic HBV infection (ENCI), and 114 HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (ENCH).
analysis.methods: Serum markers [HBsAg, HBcrAg, and HBV RNA] and intrahepatic markers (cccDNA and pgRNA) were quantified using commercial assays. Transcriptional activity was evaluated in patients with comparable intrahepatic cccDNA levels.
analysis.main_results: All serum and intrahepatic markers were inversely associated with age and higher in HBeAg-positive than in HBeAg-negative patients. Serum HBcrAg and HBV RNA showed stronger associations with cccDNA transcriptional activity than HBsAg across the EPCH and ENCH phases. Notably, no serum marker reliably reflected pgRNA or transcriptional activity in the ENCI phase.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that HBcrAg and HBV RNA are phase-dependent surrogates of transcriptionally active cccDNA, while the lack of reliable markers in ENCI highlights its virologic heterogeneity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of phase-specific monitoring and treatment decisions for chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing the importance of selecting appropriate serum markers for different disease phases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on commercial assays and the focus on a single cohort. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on correlations rather than direct causation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify serum markers reflecting intrahepatic cccDNA and its transcriptional activity across the phases of chronic hepatitis B. It analyzed a cohort of 406 treatment-naïve patients categorized by immunological phases. Serum markers such as HBcrAg and HBV RNA showed stronger associations with cccDNA transcriptional activity than HBsAg, particularly in HBeAg-positive phases. However, no serum marker reliably reflected pgRNA or transcriptional activity in the HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B phase. The authors concluded that HBcrAg and HBV RNA are phase-dependent surrogates of transcriptionally active cccDNA, highlighting the virologic heterogeneity in ENCI. These findings support the need for phase-specific monitoring and treatment decisions. The study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on correlations and a single cohort.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别反映慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)各阶段肝内共价闭合环状DNA及其转录活性的血清标志物。背景强调了更好地理解与共价闭合环状DNA相关的血清标志物的重要性,因为共价闭合环状DNA是HBV持续感染的核心。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了406名未接受治疗治疗的CHB患者的样本,按免疫学阶段分类:56例HBeAg阳性慢性HBV感染(EPCI)、153例HBeAg阳性慢性乙型肝炎(EPCH)、83例HBeAg阴性慢性HBV感染(ENCI)和114例HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎(ENCH)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用商业检测方法量化血清标志物(HBsAg、HBcrAg和HBV RNA)以及肝内标志物(共价闭合环状DNA和pgRNA)。在肝内共价闭合环状DNA水平相似的患者中评估转录活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有血清和肝内标志物均与年龄呈负相关,且HBeAg阳性患者的水平高于HBeAg阴性患者。在EPCH和ENCH阶段,血清HBcrAg和HBV RNA与共价闭合环状DNA的转录活性关联比HBsAg更强。值得注意的是,在ENCI阶段,没有血清标志物能可靠反映pgRNA或转录活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,HBcrAg和HBV RNA是共价闭合环状DNA转录活性的阶段依赖性替代标志物,而ENCI阶段缺乏可靠标志物突显了其病毒学异质性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持在不同疾病阶段进行阶段特异性监测和治疗决策,强调了选择适当血清标志物的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于依赖商业检测方法,并且仅针对单一队列研究进行分析。证据强度中等,因为结果基于相关性而非直接因果关系。

abstract_zh: 背景 共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)通过其转录活性维持乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)的持续感染。尽管共价闭合环状DNA和前基因组RNA(pgRNA)是HBV复制的核心,但反映共价闭合环状DNA活性的血清标志物在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)各阶段仍不明确。目的 为了识别反映肝内共价闭合环状DNA及其活性的血清标志物,我们分析了一组涵盖所有免疫学阶段的CHB患者队列。方法 对406名未接受治疗治疗的CHB患者按疾病阶段进行分析,包括56例乙肝e抗原(HBeAg)阳性慢性HBV感染(EPCI)、153例HBeAg阳性慢性乙型肝炎(EPCH)、83例HBeAg阴性慢性HBV感染(ENCI)和114例HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎(ENCH)。使用商业检测方法量化血清标志物(乙肝表面抗原(HBsAg)、乙肝核心相关抗原(HBcrAg)和HBV RNA)以及肝内标志物(共价闭合环状DNA和pgRNA)。在肝内共价闭合环状DNA水平相似的患者中评估转录活性。结果 所有血清和肝内标志物均与年龄呈负相关,且HBeAg阳性患者的水平高于HBeAg阴性患者。血清和肝内标志物之间的相关性在HBeAg阳性患者中更为显著。血清标志物与pgRNA的相关性比与共价闭合环状DNA的相关性更紧密。血清HBcrAg和HBV RNA比HBsAg更能反映共价闭合环状DNA的转录活性。在5/34具有相似共价闭合环状DNA水平的120例患者中,肝内共价闭合环状DNA的转录活性(pgRNA/共价闭合环状DNA)在CHB各阶段有所不同:EPCI阶段最高,ENCI阶段最低,EPCH阶段中等,ENCH阶段再次升高。HBcrAg和HBV RNA在EPCH和ENCH阶段与共价闭合环状DNA的转录活性关联更强。值得注意的是,在ENCI阶段,没有血清标志物能可靠反映pgRNA或转录活性。结论 HBcrAg和HBV RNA是共价闭合环状DNA转录活性的阶段依赖性替代标志物。ENCI阶段缺乏可靠的标志物突显了其病毒学异质性。这些发现支持针对不同疾病阶段进行阶段特异性监测和治疗决策。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别反映慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)各阶段肝内共价闭合环状DNA及其转录活性的血清标志物。背景强调了更好地理解与共价闭合环状DNA相关的血清标志物的重要性,因为共价闭合环状DNA是HBV持续感染的核心。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了406名未接受治疗治疗的CHB患者的样本,按免疫学阶段分类:56例HBeAg阳性慢性HBV感染(EPCI)、153例HBeAg阳性慢性乙型肝炎(EPCH)、83例HBeAg阴性慢性HBV感染(ENCI)和114例HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎(ENCH)。

analysis_zh.main_results: 所有血清和肝内标志物均与年龄呈负相关,且HBeAg阳性患者的水平高于HBeAg阴性患者。在EPCH和ENCH阶段,血清HBcrAg和HBV RNA与共价闭合环状DNA的转录活性关联比HBsAg更强。值得注意的是,在ENCI阶段,没有血清标志物能可靠反映pgRNA或转录活性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,HBcrAg和HBV RNA是共价闭合环状DNA转录活性的阶段依赖性替代标志物,而ENCI阶段缺乏可靠标志物突显了其病毒学异质性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持在不同疾病阶段进行阶段特异性监测和治疗决策,强调了选择适当血清标志物的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于依赖商业检测方法,并且仅针对单一队列研究进行分析。证据强度中等,因为结果基于相关性而非直接因果关系。

title: Outcomes of hepatitis B and hepatitis delta infection in hospitalized pregnant women in the United States: a nationwide study, 1998–2022
abstract: Hepatitis delta (HDV) is a severe viral hepatitis disease that occurs only in individuals with hepatitis B (HBV). In the pregnant population, HDV has been scarcely studied, and no guidance exists for its management. We aim to describe and compare a cohort of pregnant women with concurrent HBV/HDV infection to a cohort of pregnant women with only HBV. Utilizing the National Inpatient Sample, a database of hospitalizations throughout the United States, we extracted data from 1998 to 2022 on pregnant women with HBV and HDV using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. Demographics and clinical data including co-infection, comorbid condition, pregnancy complications, fetal outcomes, and mortality were collected. Analysis was performed using chi-square and logistic regression. We identified 390 pregnancies with HDV and 127,332 with HBV only. In the HDV cohort, median age was 30 years, and the predominant ethnicity/race was Asian or Pacific Islander at 27.4%. There were no cases of maternal deaths in the HDV group. Rates of hepatitis C (12.1% vs. Of those with HDV, 318 (81.5%) had known delivery. abstract_zh: 丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)是一种严重的病毒性肝炎,仅发生在乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染者中。在孕妇人群中,HDV的研究非常有限,且目前尚无相关管理指南。本研究旨在描述并比较同时感染HBV/HDV的孕妇与仅感染HBV的孕妇的临床结局。利用美国全国住院样本数据库,我们提取了1998年至2022年间患有HBV和HDV的孕妇数据,使用的是ICD-9和ICD-10编码。收集了包括共感染、合并疾病、妊娠并发症、胎儿结局和死亡率在内的流行病学和临床数据。分析采用卡方检验和逻辑回归分析。我们确定了390例HDV感染的妊娠和127,332例仅HBV感染的妊娠。在HDV感染的孕妇中,中位年龄为30岁,主要人种/种族为亚洲或太平洋岛屿居民,占27.4%。HDV组中没有产妇死亡病例。HDV感染孕妇的肝炎C病毒感染率(12.1%)高于仅HBV感染孕妇(318例中81.5%已知分娩)。HDV感染孕妇的死产率显著高于仅HBV感染孕妇(2.8% vs. 0.5%),而早产和过期产率相似(p > 0.05)。HDV在妊娠中仍较为罕见,但可能被低估。同时感染HBV/HDV的妊娠可能比仅HBV感染的妊娠具有更高的不良胎儿结局风险,尤其是死产。

title: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen and Hepatitis C Antibody Seroprevalence Among Male Blood Donors in Lahore, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study at Four Blood Banks
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) pose important challenges to blood safety, highlighting the need for continued surveillance among blood donors. This cross-sectional study assessed the seroprevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HCV antibodies among male blood donors at four blood banks in Lahore, Pakistan, and examined their associations with age and ABO/Rh blood group. A total of 600 donors were included, with 150 recruited from each of General Hospital Lahore, Services Hospital Lahore, Noor Thalassaemia Centre, and Zaib Ali Foundation. Serum samples were screened using immunochromatographic rapid tests. Seroprevalence estimates were calculated with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Associations with blood group were assessed using chi-square tests, and age distributions were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p < 0.05. HBsAg seroprevalence was 4.8% (29/600; 95% CI, 3.4–6.9%), and anti-HCV seroprevalence was 4.5% (27/600; 95% CI, 3.1–6.5%). B-positive was the most frequent blood group (33.0%). Neither HBsAg nor anti-HCV reactivity was significantly associated with ABO/Rh blood group (χ2 = 10.17, p = 0.179 and χ2 = 4.16, p = 0.762, respectively). Age distributions did not differ significantly between reactive and nonreactive donors for either marker (p = 0.210 and p = 0.922, respectively). No significant association was observed between HBsAg and anti-HCV reactivity (p = 0.858). Approximately one in twenty donors screened reactive for each marker, underscoring the importance of reliable donor screening, appropriate confirmatory testing, donor counselling and referral. These findings represent screening-marker seroprevalence rather than confirmed active infection and should be interpreted within the limitations of rapid testing and the sampled male donor population.

title_zh: Lahore,Pakistan男性献血者中乙型肝炎表面抗原和丙型肝炎抗体血清流行率:一项在四个血库进行的横断面研究
source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) pose important challenges to blood safety, highlighting the need for continued surveillance among blood donors. This cross-sectional study assessed the seroprevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HCV antibodies among male blood donors at four blood banks in Lahore, Pakistan, and examined their associations with age and ABO/Rh blood group. A total of 600 donors were included, with 150 recruited from each of General Hospital Lahore, Services Hospital Lahore, Noor Thalassaemia Centre, and Zaib Ali Foundation. Serum samples were screened using immunochromatographic rapid tests. Seroprevalence estimates were calculated with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Associations with blood group were assessed using chi-square tests, and age distributions were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p < 0.05. HBsAg seroprevalence was 4.8% (29/600; 95% CI, 3.4–6.9%), and anti-HCV seroprevalence was 4.5% (27/600; 95% CI, 3.1–6.5%). B-positive was the most frequent blood group (33.0%). Neither HBsAg nor anti-HCV reactivity was significantly associated with ABO/Rh blood group (χ2 = 10.17, p = 0.179 and χ2 = 4.16, p = 0.762, respectively). Age distributions did not differ significantly between reactive and nonreactive donors for either marker (p = 0.210 and p = 0.922, respectively). No significant association was observed between HBsAg and anti-HCV reactivity (p = 0.858). Approximately one in twenty donors screened reactive for each marker, underscoring the importance of reliable donor screening, appropriate confirmatory testing, donor counselling and referral. These findings represent screening-marker seroprevalence rather than confirmed active infection and should be interpreted within the limitations of rapid testing and the sampled male donor population.

title: Interferon-based HBV function cure therapy reduces hepatocellular carcinoma risk in low-HBsAg chronic hepatitis B patients: a propensity-matched cohort study and dynamic prediction model
abstract: Background Functional cure through HBsAg loss is a key treatment goal in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet its impact on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk remains incompletely characterized, especially when achieved via interferon (IFN)-based therapy. We aimed to evaluate the HCC risk reduction associated with IFN-based therapy in low-HBsAg CHB patients and develop a validated prediction model for this population. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3,367 CHB patients with HBsAg <1,500 IU/mL, including 1,780 receiving IFN-based therapy and 1,587 on nucleos(t)ide analogue (NAs) monotherapy. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Cox regression and time-dependent ROC analyses were employed to develop a dynamic nomogram for HCC prediction. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the impact of interferon-based therapy on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in low-HBsAg chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. A propensity-matched cohort study of 3,367 patients showed that IFN-based therapy significantly reduced HCC incidence compared to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) monotherapy (1.2% vs. 4.9%, p<0.001). A dynamic nomogram incorporating treatment modality, AFP, cirrhosis, age, and other variables demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy (5-year AUC: 0.888 in derivation, 0.956 in validation cohorts), outperforming existing HCC prediction models. The study highlights the potential of IFN-based therapy to reduce HCC risk in low-HBsAg CHB patients, particularly those with cirrhosis, and suggests the utility of a personalized prediction model for surveillance and treatment decisions. However, the study is retrospective and relies on propensity score matching, which may not fully eliminate confounding, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.main_results: 基于干扰素的治疗与核苷类似物单药治疗相比,与显著降低的HCC 发病率相关(1.2% vs. 4.9%,p<0.001),在PSM后,风险比为3.03(95% CI:1.82–5.06)。一个结合治疗模式、AFP、肝硬化、年龄及其他变量的新颖列线图显示出卓越的预测准确性(衍生集5年AUC:0.888,验证集5年AUC:0.956 队列研究),优于现有的HCC预测模型。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3,367 CHB patients with HBsAg <1,500 IU/mL, including 1,780 receiving IFN-based therapy and 1,587 on nucleos(t)ide analogue (NAs) monotherapy.
analysis_en.methods: Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Cox regression and time-dependent ROC analyses were employed to develop a dynamic nomogram for HCC prediction.
analysis_en.main_results: IFN-based therapy was associated with a significantly lower HCC incidence compared to NAs monotherapy (1.2% vs. 4.9%, p<0.001), with a hazard ratio of 3.03 (95% CI: 1.82–5.06) after PSM. A novel nomogram incorporating treatment modality, AFP, cirrhosis, age, and other variables demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy (5-year AUC: 0.888 in derivation, 0.956 in validation cohorts), outperforming existing HCC prediction models.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk in low-HBsAg CHB patients, particularly those with cirrhosis. title_zh: 基于干扰素的乙型肝炎病毒功能性治愈治疗降低低HBsAg慢性乙型肝炎患者肝细胞癌风险:一项倾向匹配研究及动态预测模型
source_body_en: Background Functional cure through HBsAg loss is a key treatment goal in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet its impact on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk remains incompletely characterized, especially when achieved via interferon (IFN)-based therapy. We aimed to evaluate the HCC risk reduction associated with IFN-based therapy in low-HBsAg CHB patients and develop a validated prediction model for this population. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3,367 CHB patients with HBsAg <1,500 IU/mL, including 1,780 receiving IFN-based therapy and 1,587 on nucleos(t)ide analogue (NAs) monotherapy. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Cox regression and time-dependent ROC analyses were employed to develop a dynamic nomogram for HCC prediction. Results IFN-based therapy was associated with a significantly lower HCC incidence compared to NAs monotherapy (1.2% vs. 4.9%, p<0.001), with a hazard ratio of 3.03 (95% CI: 1.82–5.06) after PSM. The protective effect was most pronounced in cirrhotic patients (absolute risk reduction 8.8%, NNT = 11). A novel nomogram incorporating treatment modality, AFP, cirrhosis, age, and other variables demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy (5-year AUC: 0.888 in derivation, 0.956 in validation cohorts), outperforming existing HCC prediction models. Conclusions IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk in low-HBsAg CHB patients, particularly those with cirrhosis. We developed and validated a dynamic prediction model that may facilitate personalized surveillance and treatment decisions in functionally cured patients.
abstract_zh: 背景:通过HBsAg丢失实现功能性治愈是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)治疗的关键目标,但其对肝细胞癌(HCC)风险的影响尚未完全阐明,尤其是在通过干扰素(IFN)为基础的治疗实现时。我们旨在评估IFN为基础的治疗在低HBsAg CHB患者中与HCC风险降低的相关性,并为这一人群开发一个经过验证的预测模型。方法:我们对3,367名HBsAg <1,500 IU/mL的CHB患者进行了回顾性研究,其中包括1,780名接受IFN为基础的治疗和1,587名接受核苷(酸)类似物(NAs)单药治疗的患者。使用倾向评分匹配(PSM)来平衡基线特征。采用Cox回归和时间依赖ROC分析来开发HCC的动态列线图预测模型。结果:与NAs单药治疗相比,IFN为基础的治疗与显著更低的HCC发生率相关(1.2% vs. 4.9%,p<0.001),在PSM后,风险比为3.03(95% CI:1.82–5.06)。保护效应在肝硬化患者中最为显著(绝对风险降低8.8%,NNT = 11)。一个结合治疗方式、AFP、肝硬化、年龄及其他变量的新列线图模型显示出出色的预测准确性(5年AUC:推导集为0.888,验证集为0.956),优于现有的HCC预测模型。结论:IFN为基础的治疗显著降低低HBsAg CHB患者的HCC风险,尤其是肝硬化患者。我们开发并验证了一个动态预测模型,可能有助于功能性治愈患者进行个性化的治疗和监测决策。科学及公共卫生意义:这些发现可能为功能性治愈患者提供个性化的治疗和监测决策,从而改善HBV相关肝硬化的患者预后。局限性及证据强度:该研究为回顾性研究,依赖于倾向评分匹配,可能无法完全消除混杂因素。由于研究的观察性质和潜在偏倚,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 通过HBsAg丢失实现功能性治愈是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)治疗的关键目标,但其对肝细胞癌(HCC)风险的影响仍未完全阐明,尤其是在通过干扰素(IFN)为基础的治疗方案实现时。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对3,367例HBsAg <1,500 IU/mL的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行了回顾性队列研究研究,其中包括1,780例接受基于干扰素的治疗和1,587例接受核苷(酸)类似物(NAs)单药治疗的患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 倾向评分匹配(PSM)被用于平衡基线特征。采用Cox回归和时间依赖性ROC分析来构建用于肝细胞癌(HCC)预测的动态列线图。
analysis_zh.main_results: 基于干扰素的治疗与核苷类似物单药治疗相比,与显著降低的HCC 发病率相关(1.2% vs. 4.9%,p<0.001),在PSM后,风险比为3.03(95% CI:1.82–5.06)。一个结合治疗模式、AFP、肝硬化、年龄及其他变量的新颖列线图显示出卓越的预测准确性(衍生集5年AUC:0.888,验证集5年AUC:0.956 队列研究),优于现有的HCC预测模型。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于干扰素的治疗显著降低低HBsAg水平慢性乙型肝炎患者患肝细胞癌的风险,尤其是那些伴有肝硬化的患者。我们开发并验证了一个动态预测模型,可能有助于功能性治愈患者进行个性化的监测和治疗决策。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为功能性治愈患者提供个性化的监测和治疗决策,可能改善与乙型肝炎病毒相关肝硬化的患者预后。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究为回顾性研究,依赖于倾向评分匹配,这可能无法完全消除混杂因素。由于研究的观察性质和潜在偏倚,证据等级为中等。

title: Concurrent Fabry disease and Hepatitis-B virus-associated IgA nephropathy: A case report with pain as a precursor
abstract: We report a 35-year-old man with Fabry disease coexisting with Hepatitis-B virus (HBV)-associated IgA nephropathy who had been treated for “rheumatism” for many years. He presented with severe burning pain in his extremities, microscopic hematuria and nephrotic-range proteinuria, while kidney function was preserved. Autoimmune tests were negative, but HBV markers were positive. Renal biopsy showed IgA-dominant mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis with mesangial HBsAg deposits, and electron microscopy revealed myelin-like inclusions in podocytes and tubules. Markedly reduced α-galactosidase A activity, elevated lyso-GL-3 and a splice-site GLA mutation confirmed Fabry disease. Treatment with renin-angiotensin blockade, entecavir and enzyme replacement improved pain and proteinuria and stabilized renal function. This case illustrates that Fabry disease coexisting with HBV-associated IgA nephropathy is uncommon and easily underdiagnosed, and that persistent neuropathic pain with proteinuria should prompt consideration of metabolic and genetic renal disorders.

Treatment with renin-angiotensin blockade, entecavir and enzyme replacement improved pain and proteinuria and stabilized renal function. This case illustrates that Fabry disease coexisting with HBV-associated IgA nephropathy is uncommon and easily underdiagnosed, and that persistent neuropathic pain with proteinuria should prompt consideration of metabolic and genetic renal disorders.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在报告一例罕见的Fabry病与HBV相关IgA肾病并发病例,强调在出现持续性神经病理性疼痛和蛋白尿的患者中考虑代谢性和遗传性疾病的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一例35岁同时患有Fabry病和HBV相关IgA肾病的男性患者进行了病例报告,该患者多年来被误诊为“风湿病”并接受治疗,且出现严重灼痛、显微镜下血尿和肾病范围蛋白尿,同时保持肾功能正常。

title: Prevalence and risk factors of HIV, HBV, and HCV among women who inject drugs in five Mozambican cities: a subgroup analysis of a cross-sectional biological and behavioral survey, 2023–2024
abstract: Abstract Background Women who inject drugs (WWID) are disproportionately affected by HIV and viral hepatitis, yet data on prevalence and risk factors in Mozambique remain scarce. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), and antibodies against hepatitis C virus (anti-HCV) among WWID and to identify associated sociodemographic and behavioral risk factors. Methods This cross-sectional study is a subgroup analysis of WWID from the second round of the Bio-behavioral survey (BBS) among people who injected drugs of any gender, conducted in five Mozambican cities (Maputo, Beira, Tete, Quelimane, Nampula) between July 2023 and March 2024, using respondent-driven sampling (RDS); this analysis focuses on the subsample of 524 WWID recruited within that survey. Participants completed structured questionnaires and underwent rapid testing for HIV, HBsAg, and anti-HCV. RDS-weighted prevalence estimates were calculated for all outcomes. Modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors was used to identify factors associated with HIV infection. Results The weighted prevalence was 28.6% (95% CI: 15.5–41.6) for HIV, 5.3% (95% CI: 3.4–7.3) for HBsAg positivity, and 19.7% (95% CI: 3.1–36.2) for anti-HCV positivity. Unadjusted HIV prevalence peaked among women aged 25–34 years, increased markedly with age and duration of injection and was highest in Maputo City. In adjusted analyses, older age (≥ 35 years vs. 16–17 years; aPR = 11.9; 95% CI: 4.0–35.6), and residence in Maputo were independently associated with HIV infection, while secondary or higher education and absence of recent sexually transmitted infection (STI) symptoms were associated with lower HIV prevalence. Among WWID living with HIV, 85.0% were aware of their status, 86.6% of those aware were on antiretroviral therapy, and 75.7% of those on treatment were virally suppressed. Conclusion WWID in Mozambique face a high burden of HIV and anti-HCV positivity, with marked geographic variation. Gaps in the HIV care continuum, particularly between ART initiation and viral suppression, warrant further investigation into potential barriers to sustained treatment and care. Expanded harm-reduction services, integrated HIV, HBV and HCV testing and treatment, and prevention targeted to high-burden areas are needed.

title: Outcomes of Virus-like Particle-based Therapies in Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review
abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) are emerging nanostructures that mimic the structure of native viruses while lacking viral genetic material, making them safe and highly adaptable platforms for drug and gene delivery. Their unique physical characteristics and capacity for surface modification have attracted considerable attention for their applications in cancer therapy. This systematic review aimed to evaluate therapeutic outcomes of VLP-based approaches in human breast cancer models. A literature search was carried out in PubMed and Scopus databases to identify studies investigating the therapeutic use of VLPs in breast cancer. Screening was performed focusing on experimental studies utilizing human breast cancer models. Extracted information included study characteristics, type of VLP platform, therapeutic strategy, and reported outcomes. In addition, study design, use of experimental controls, outcome assessment, and reporting transparency were described. Six studies that fulfilled the eligibility criteria were selected. The studies used different VLP platforms (hepatitis B virus [HBV], bacteriophage P22, adeno-associated virus, hepatitis C virus [HCV], and polyoma virus-derived particles). Main therapeutic methods included targeted drug delivery, gene or nucleic-acid delivery, and multifunctional enzyme-based nano-therapies. Results showed favorable effects of VLP-based systems in breast cancer therapy, such as enhanced intracellular delivery of drugs, cytotoxic effects, inhibition of tumor cell invasion, and increased sensitivity to tamoxifen. In conclusion, VLP-based platforms showed promising effects in breast cancer therapy; however, the results are limited to laboratory studies. Future clinical studies would be necessary to confirm the potential of VLP-based approaches in breast cancer therapy.

This systematic review aimed to evaluate therapeutic outcomes of VLP-based approaches in human breast cancer models. A literature search was carried out in PubMed and Scopus databases to identify studies investigating the therapeutic use of VLPs in breast cancer. Screening was performed focusing on experimental studies utilizing human breast cancer models. Extracted information included study characteristics, type of VLP platform, therapeutic strategy, and reported outcomes. In addition, study design, use of experimental controls, outcome assessment, and reporting transparency were described. Six studies that fulfilled the eligibility criteria were selected. The studies used different VLP platforms (hepatitis B virus [HBV], bacteriophage P22, adeno-associated virus, hepatitis C virus [HCV], and polyoma virus-derived particles). Main therapeutic methods included targeted drug delivery, gene or nucleic-acid delivery, and multifunctional enzyme-based nano-therapies. Results showed favorable effects of VLP-based systems in breast cancer therapy, such as enhanced intracellular delivery of drugs, cytotoxic effects, inhibition of tumor cell invasion, and increased sensitivity to tamoxifen. In conclusion, VLP-based platforms showed promising effects in breast cancer therapy; however, the results are limited to laboratory studies. Future clinical studies would be necessary to confirm the potential of VLP-based approaches in breast cancer therapy.

title: Brief communication: hepatitis B, human papillomavirus, pneumococcal and influenza vaccination in an Australian metropolitan HIV service
abstract: People living with HIV experience a disproportionate burden of vaccine-preventable infections. This retrospective audit assessed the proportion of patients with adequate vaccination against hepatitis B, human papillomavirus, pneumococcus and influenza within an Australian HIV service. There was a significantly higher proportion ( p < 0.001) with adequate hepatitis B vaccination (47.9%), compared to pneumococcal conjugate (19.0%), pneumococcal polysaccharide (6.6%), and human papillomavirus (7.4%) vaccination. Influenza vaccination rates (30.6%) were similar to general population rates in Western Australia. Adequate vaccination requires review to prevent hepatitis B acquisition and HPV-associated neoplasia, particularly in the context of tenofovir-free antiretroviral regimens and routine anal cancer screening.

title: Abstract B154: Identifying gaps in hepatocellular carcinoma awareness and hepatitis B prevention among Southeast Asian adults in Minnesota: Findings from a community-engaged survey and evidence for targeted interventions
abstract: Abstract Background: Southeast Asian American adults experience a higher burden of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), nearly half of which is caused by chronic infection of hepatitis B virus (HBV). Vaccination and early detection can be critical in reducing HCC burdens, but little is known about which groups are not receiving preventive efforts. This study identified demographic and socioeconomic characteristics of those who did not report HCC-related prevention. Methods: Data was collected in three urban centers in Minnesota through a community-engaged survey in 2025. A sample of 501 Southeast Asian adults (age 18 or older) were recruited via convenience and snowball sampling. The sample (n=501) consisted of individuals from various countries of origin, including Cambodia (n=102), Laos (n=102), Vietnam (n=122), and others (n=177; e.g., Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand). HCC-related measures were (1) HCC screening awareness, (2) HBV testing, and (3) HBV vaccination. Chi-square tests were used to compare affirmative (“yes”) versus non-affirmative responses (“no” “don’t know” “don’t remember or not interested”) across demographics (age, gender, relationship status, whether born in the US, country of origin) and socioeconomic characteristics (highest education attained, insurance status, 2025 federal poverty level determined by income per household member). Fisher’s exact tests were used when cell counts were <5. Analysis was conducted in SAS Studio 3.82. Results: Affirmative responses (“yes”) varied across the three outcomes. HCC screening awareness was highest among aged 50–69 years (50.5%) compared to adults aged 18-29 (24.8%) (p=0.001), in a relationship (40.5% vs 30.2%, p=0.044), and foreign-born (39.7% vs 27.6%, p=0.026). HBV testing was higher among women (40.8% vs 30.7%, p=0.046), insured (38.6% vs 19.5%, p=0.002), and at or above federal poverty level (44.2% vs 30.5%, p=0.002). HBV vaccination was highest among aged 18-29 (54.0%) (p=0.010), women (48.3% vs 36.7%, p=0.013), in a relationship (49.2% vs 35.1%, p=0.006), more highly educated (p<0.001), insured (45.9% vs 19.5%, p<0.001), and at or above federal poverty level (52.3% vs 36.1%, p<0.001). They differed by country of origin (p<0.001) with Laotian participants reporting the highest proportion of non-affirmative HBV vaccination responses at 80%. Conclusion: HCC screening awareness and related prevention were not evenly distributed across Southeast Asian adults in Minnesota. Gaps in HCC screening awareness was seen among younger adults, US-born participants, and those not in a relationship, whereas HBV testing and vaccination gaps were evident in access to health care and socioeconomic needs. Findings suggest that targeted interventions are needed for high-risk population to improve HCC prevention. Given the high proportion of undiagnosed HBV infections, improving awareness, testing, and vaccination among those who are not reached by preventive efforts may be critical for reducing HCC burden in the future. title: Abstract A168: Developing a culturally sensitive interview guide to assess barriers to Hepatitis B screening and care in Asian American communities
abstract: Abstract Background: Asian American populations carry a higher burden of chronic hepatitis B (HBV) and related complications such as liver cancer but remain under-screened and undertreated in the U.S. Language barriers, cultural stigma, and structural inequities contribute to these gaps, yet few qualitative studies capture both community and institutional perspectives. We aimed to create a culturally sensitive interview guide to better understand barriers to HBV screening and care from the perspectives of coalition leaders and healthcare professionals, including physicians, nurses, and community health workers. Methods: The semi-structured interview guide was developed through an iterative process involving multiple rounds of research team co-learning and refinement. This process included: (1) revising question wording to improve neutrality, (2) reducing leading or prescriptive language, (3) incorporating culturally relevant considerations informed by the literature and community context, (4) reflecting on power dynamics and strategies to promote participant openness and trust, and (5) conducting piloting sessions to assess question flow, clarity, and interviewer consistency. The final guide was designed to facilitate open-ended discussion while ensuring consistency across interviews. Results: The final interview guide includes domains on patient demographics, language services, institutional policies, screening workflows, and perceived barriers to HBV screening and treatment. The revised guide places greater emphasis on culturally specific factors such as interpreter availability across clinical settings, differences across Asian ethnic subgroups, and the role of community partnerships. Importantly, question framing was modified throughout to minimize defensiveness among participants, particularly healthcare administrators. For example, potentially sensitive topics (e.g., insurance status or undocumented patients) were approached using indirect, open-ended probes rather than direct critique. These changes improved the flow of the interview and are expected to facilitate more candid responses. Conclusions: This stakeholder-informed interview guide was developed using an iterative approach grounded in principles of cultural sensitivity, reflective practice, and participant-centered qualitative research. By integrating these considerations throughout the development process, the final interview guide is designed to elicit rich, contextually grounded perspectives on multilevel barriers to HBV screening and care. This process can help provide a practical framework to the development of culturally responsive qualitative research tools in future healthcare settings. title: Targeted redox gene-expression profiling reveals shared and distinct expression patterns in HBV- and HCV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress and redox dysregulation are important features of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their expression patterns in hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-associated HCC remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated redox-related gene expression and its potential functional and prognostic relevance. METHODS: A predefined 84-gene oxidative stress and redox-related quantitative real-time PCR array was used to profile 11 HCC samples (7 HCV-associated and 4 HBV-associated tumors) and 4 controls. Analyses included hierarchical clustering, gene-list overlap, functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction networks, gene-expression correlations, and exploratory survival analysis. RESULTS: Both HCC groups exhibited altered expression of genes associated with antioxidant defense, glutathione metabolism, mitochondrial redox regulation, and ferroptosis-related processes. In HCV-associated HCC versus controls, TXN, SPINK1, HSP90AA1, and DUSP1 showed increased expression. In HBV-associated HCC versus controls, GCLC, peroxiredoxins, CAT, and SOD1 showed increased expression. Eighteen genes were shared between comparison lists, including GPX4, GPX2, GPX3, PRDX1, PRDX5, TXN, GCLM, SOD2, and FTH1. Enrichment analyses implicated glutathione metabolism, oxidative stress, peroxisome function, and ferroptosis-associated processes. Network analysis identified GPX2, GPX3, GPX4, and SOD2 in a connected module. External exploratory survival analysis associated higher SPINK1 and HSP90AA1 expression with poorer overall survival. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify redox-related expression patterns warranting further investigation. title: Colorimetric polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) assay for the rapid detection of hepatitis B virus
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global health concern, particularly in low-resource settings with limited access to sophisticated diagnostic tools. Conventional molecular diagnostic assays, such as qPCR, are often restricted to centralized laboratories in urban settings due to their high cost and the need for skilled personnel. This limits its use in lower levels of the healthcare system, highlighting the need for affordable point-of-care (PoC) assays. In this study, we have developed a visual detection method for HBV using a polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) incorporated with hydroxy naphthol blue (HNB) dye. A set of primers was designed targeting a specific region of the S gene of HBV, and the reaction runs in an isothermal condition. The assay conditions were optimized, and the optimal reaction temperature and time were 63 °C and 60 min, respectively. This developed HBV-PSR assay showed a detection limit of 5.04 copies, reaching 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in clinical evaluation ( n = 85), and colorimetric visualization in 60 min by naked eye. The specificity test revealed no cross-reactivity with other hepatitis-causing viruses and the tested non-HBV pathogens. The assay was tested with 45 HBV-positive clinical samples, which were initially screened by a serological test, and showed a good concordance rate and diagnostic reliability. The HBV-PSR assay designed in this study could potentially be used as a point-of-care diagnostic tool for HBV detection, aiming at early surveillance and detection, focusing on healthcare in poor-resource settings. The combination of isothermal amplification with dye-based visual detection eliminated the need for complex instruments, enabling PoC detection. Key points • A rapid and sensitive PSR assay was developed for HBV detection, with results obtained within 1 h . • HNB dye enabled naked eye visual detection without the need for complex equipment . • The assay detected as few as 5.04 DNA copies and demonstrated high diagnostic performance, outperforming conventional PCR in the evaluated clinical samples .

title: DISTRIBUTION OF FIVE HEPATITIS B VIRUS MARKERS IN HIV INFECTED AND UNINFECTED INJECTING DRUG USERS IN COASTAL KENYA
abstract: Aims: This study determined HBV sero-markers profile in HIV-1 infected (n=157) and uninfected (n=214) IDUs from Mombasa, Kenya HIV-1 diagnosis was performed using DetermineTM and UnigoldTM rapid tests. Methodology: The CD4+ T cells were enumerated using the FacsCalibur flow cytometer and categorized according to the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) immunological staging criteria. HBV seroprofile was determined using HBV-5 panel rapid test cassettes. Clinical staging was based on serological profile of the five HBV markers. Results: HBsAg (P=0.004) and HBcAb-IgM (P=0.008) positivities were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals while the opposite was observed for HBsAb positivity (P=0.019). Rates of acute (P=0.033) and chronic (P=0.021) clinical stages were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals but the inverse was noticed for vaccine type response rate (P=0.008). Only genotype A, sub-genotype A1 was detected with higher frequencies noted in the HIV-1 infected (n=12) compared to the uninfected (n=4) individuals. Conclusion: HBsAg and HBcAb-IgM sero-markers and acute and chronic clinical categories are higher while HBsAb sero-marker and vaccine type response stage are lower in HIV-1 infected compared to uninfected IDUs at Mombasa, Kenya. Taken together, HIV infected injection drug users are at risk of acquiring HBV and progressing to chronic infection.

title: Seroprevalence of TORCH ınfections and hepatitis B serological status among pregnant women in southeastern Türkiye: a retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: TORCH infections are among the major causes of congenital infections and adverse perinatal outcomes during pregnancy. Furthermore, the assessment of hepatitis B serostatus and bloodborne infections is a fundamental component of antenatal care. Given the limited regional seroprevalence data available in southeastern Turkey, this study presents data obtained from a large, single-center cohort; the study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of TORCH infections, the serological status of hepatitis B, and the prevalence of bloodborne infections among pregnant women, as well as to evaluate the association of these serological findings with selected demographic characteristics. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 2,300 pregnant women who presented during the first trimester. Serological results for rubella, Toxoplasma gondii, cytomegalovirus, syphilis, Anti-HBs, Anti-HCV, and Anti-HIV were evaluated. Seroprevalence rates were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Associations between demographic variables and serological findings were examined using chi-square tests. Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with serological results. Rubella IgG seropositivity was 92.3%, Toxoplasma gondii IgG seropositivity was 11.9%, and CMV IgG seropositivity was 99.9%. Accordingly, 88.1% of the pregnant women were found to be seronegative for Toxoplasma gondii. While anti-HBs seropositivity was determined to be 37.1%, anti-HBs levels were found to be below 10 mIU/mL—the serological threshold considered protective—in 62.9% of pregnant women. The seropositivity rates for anti-HCV and anti-HIV were 0.3% and 0.1%, respectively. Toxoplasma IgG seropositivity showed a significant association with age ( p < 0.001), and in multivariate analysis, age was found to be independently associated with seropositivity (OR = 1.37; 95% CI: 1.22–1.54). In contrast, increasing age was independently and inversely associated with Anti-HBs seropositivity (OR = 0.73; 95% CI: 0.67–0.79). This study demonstrates that, due to the low prevalence of Toxoplasma gondii seropositivity among pregnant women, there is a large susceptible population, and that Anti-HBs seropositivity is at a relatively low level. However, the extent to which Anti-HBs values detected below the reference threshold reflect clinical immunity cannot be determined with the current study design due to the unavailability of vaccination history. The findings should be interpreted in conjunction with further studies that include vaccination records and additional clinical variables.

title: Perspectives on primary care management of chronic hepatitis B in refugees: findings from qualitative interviews with healthcare providers in Melbourne, Victoria.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In Australia, healthcare providers face significant challenges in meeting the niche health needs of refugees. Social determinants of health, including limited health literacy and finances, complicate refugees' access to treatment for conditions, such as chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Understanding the strategies utilised by a specialised general practice for refugees can offer guidance for treating this population. The aim of this study was to explore how primary care is currently managing CHB care tailored to refugees and to identify areas for potential improvements. METHODS: Between August and December 2024, we conducted 15 semi-structured interviews with nine general practitioners, four nurses, one pharmacist and one infectious disease specialist. We used a convenience sample and snowballing; most participants worked at a refugee-focused general practice in the west of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. All interviews were recorded and transcribed; data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Primary healthcare providers in our study recognised the challenges of treating refugees with CHB, including low health literacy, and the cost of providing and seeking care. However, when compared with hospital services, the benefits of primary care include community integration and location, rapport development, and the availability of interpreter services. Subsidising primary care provider training and other costs were recommended. CONCLUSIONS: Primary care may be better positioned than hospital services to treat refugees with CHB. These findings support funding and improving CHB management in primary care to meet the needs of refugees, which will lead to better health outcomes for this disadvantaged population.

title: A CHI3L1-containing diagnostic model for biopsy-confirmed significant fibrosis in chronic HBV infection: a retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Aim To evaluate the association between serum chitinase-3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) and biopsy-confirmed significant fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, and to explore CHI3L1-containing diagnostic models. Methods This retrospective study included 81 adults who underwent liver biopsy between January 2020 and December 2024. Significant fibrosis was defined as Scheuer stage S2-S4. Participants were allocated to training (n = 65) and hold-out validation (n = 16) cohorts before missing-value imputation. HBV DNA was log10-transformed. FibroScan, a serum model (prothrombin time, alkaline phosphatase, CHI3L1 and log10 HBV DNA), and a combined model were assessed. Results Fifty-six participants had significant fibrosis. Median CHI3L1 was numerically higher with significant fibrosis [31.73 (22.23–55.80) vs 27.41 (19.86–35.44) ng/mL; P = 0.105]. In the seven-variable model, CHI3L1 showed a positive adjusted association (odds ratio 1.061, 95% confidence interval 1.004–1.121; P = 0.036). Training/validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.783/0.808 for FibroScan, 0.856/0.750 for the serum model and 0.873/0.800 for the combined model. Conclusions CHI3L1 showed a positive adjusted association, but model ranking was inconsistent in the small validation cohort. These exploratory findings require rigorous internal validation and independent prospective multicenter validation before clinical use.

title: Impact of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors Control on Cardiovascular–Kidney–Metabolic Axis in Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: ABSTRACT Background The impact of cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) on the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) axis in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains poorly defined. Methods We conducted a prospective analysis enrolling patients with CHB who were on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs). CMRFs were defined as per established criteria; poorly‐controlled CMRFs were defined with specific cut‐offs measured across 5 years. Study outcomes include fibrosis progression (liver stiffness [LS] increase by ≥ 20%), liver‐related events (LREs), chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all‐cause mortality. Results A total of 714 NUC‐treated patients (median age: 61.0 [54.5–66.7] years; 69.6% male; 90.5% undetectable HBV DNA, median NUCs duration of 14.1 [11.3–16.5] years) were followed up for 9.7 (7.2–10.2) years. LREs occurred in 112 (15.7%) patients, with annual incidence rate of 1.62 events per 100 person‐years. All‐cause mortality was observed in 86 (12%) patients, including 47 (6.6%) liver‐related mortality. title: Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Ghana Between 2019 and 2026: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: 1.0 Introduction Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health challenge, contributing substantially to chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), with disproportionately high burdens reported in Southeast Asia and sub-Saharan Africa [1,2]. According to the World Health Organization, approximately 240 million people are living with chronic hepatitis B globally, with an estimated 0.9 million new infections occurring annually and 1.1 million deaths attributed primarily to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (primary liver cancer). This burden is unduly concentrated in the WHO Western Pacific and African Regions, which account for an estimated 102 million and 64 million chronic infections, respectively [3]. Within sub-Saharan Africa, HBsAg seroprevalence has remained comparatively high and geographically heterogeneous [4,5]. Ghana is consistently described as a country of major public health concern with respect to HBV, historically classified within the high-endemicity category, with prevalence estimates commonly exceeding 8% [6]. Accurate and current HBsAg seroprevalence data are essential for quantifying disease burden, tracking transmission patterns, and informing vaccination, screening, and treatment policies. This need is especially acute in high-endemicity settings such as Ghana, where progress toward the WHO's 2030 elimination targets depends on reliable, up-to-date epidemiological estimates [1,7]. Previous syntheses have established a substantial HBV burden in Ghana, but also reveal a shifting evidence base over time. A review covering 1995–2015 reported a pooled national HBsAg prevalence of 12.3%, though the underlying evidence was noted to be fragmented [6]. A subsequent systematic review restricted to 2015–2019 estimated adult prevalence at 8.36%, adolescent prevalence at 14.30%, and prevalence among children under five at 0.55%, highlighting marked variation by age group [8]. An umbrella review of viral hepatitis meta-analyses across sub-Saharan Africa further confirmed that this more recent estimate for Ghana was lower than earlier figures from 1995–2015, reinforcing evidence of a temporal decline in the national disease burden [9]. Although HBV transmission remains ongoing in Ghana, recent epidemiological data are fragmented across specific subpopulations, regions, and care settings [10–12]. To address this critical gap, the present systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes Ghanaian studies published between 2019 and 2026. By generating an updated national pooled estimate of HBsAg seroprevalence and characterizing variations across populations and settings, this study provides contemporary evidence to guide HBV control and elimination strategies in Ghana.

title: Hepatitis B vaccination coverage and factors associated with higher uptake among children aged 5–35 months in eight selected sub-Saharan African countries: a multilevel ordinal logistic regression analysis
abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) carries the world’s heaviest burden of chronic hepatitis B, most of which is acquired in early life; however, coverage remains short of what is needed to interrupt transmission. Most evidence treats childhood vaccination as a yes-or-no outcome and pools different antigens, hiding both the partial vaccination typical of a multi-dose schedule and the individual, household, and community influences that act together on uptake. We examined the factors associated with higher hepatitis B vaccination rates among children aged 5–35 months in eight selected SSA countries. We pooled the most recent Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) data (2016–2024) from the eight SSA countries whose surveys recorded all four hepatitis B touchpoints (birth dose and three pentavalent doses): 49,075 children aged 5–35 months (weighted n = 48,124) nested within 41,476 households and 5,580 communities. Hepatitis B vaccination was defined as an ordered outcome (not, partially or fully vaccinated) from the number of recorded doses. Guided by Andersen’s Behavioural Model of Health Services Use, we fitted three-level random-intercept ordinal logistic regression models (children within households within communities) with country fixed effects, reporting adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and intra-cluster correlation coefficients (ICC). Descriptive estimates accounted for the survey weights, strata and clusters; the proportional odds assumption was tested, and design-based, threshold-specific and country-stratified models were fitted as sensitivity analyses. Overall, 38.3% (95% CI 37.5–39.1) of children were fully vaccinated, 46.2% (45.4–46.9) partially vaccinated and 15.6% (14.9–16.2) not vaccinated, and only 49.7% (48.9–50.6) had a recorded birth dose. Full vaccination ranged from 3.4% in Burundi and 11.4% in Sierra Leone, where the birth dose was not part of the national schedule, to 89.7% in The Gambia; Nigeria had the largest share of unvaccinated children (35.3%). In the full model, facility-based delivery (aOR 2.83, 95% CI 2.66–3.02), maternal education (aOR 3.20, 95% CI 2.79–3.66 for higher versus none), exposure to media (aOR 1.29, 95% CI 1.22–1.36), maternal employment (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.20–1.34), older maternal age, older child age and greater household wealth (aOR 1.60, 95% CI 1.43–1.79 for richest versus poorest) were associated with a higher vaccination category, whereas rural residence (aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.70–0.86) and a preceding birth interval shorter than 24 months (aOR 0.86, 95% CI 0.79–0.94) were associated with a lower category. Health insurance coverage was not associated with vaccination once country was accounted for (aOR 0.98, 95% CI 0.89–1.07). The community level accounted for 32% of the residual variance and households for a further 3%, and the multilevel model fitted substantially better than the single-level model (LR χ2 = 5978.93, p < 0.001). In these eight countries most children were only partially vaccinated against hepatitis B and half had no recorded birth dose, with large differences between countries that mirror national birth-dose policy. Within countries, uptake was associated with facility delivery, maternal education, media exposure and household wealth, and it clustered strongly within communities. These cross-sectional associations suggest that introducing and delivering the birth dose through maternal and newborn care, reaching home births, and targeting less-advantaged mothers and lagging communities may help close the gap toward the 2030 elimination targets.

title: Pegylated interferon α-2b add-on to nucleos(t)ide analogues reduces hepatocellular carcinoma and decompensation in advanced fibrotic chronic hepatitis B
abstract: BACKGROUND The current therapeutic strategy of adding pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) is primarily aimed at achieving functional cure. However, its value in improving prognosis and the suitable candidates for this combination strategy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis remain to be further explored. AIM To evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy. A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores. RESULTS The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy. These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. CONCLUSION Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.

title: CRISPR diagnostics for maternal–infant HIV, hepatitis B, and syphilis care: clinical roles and translational gaps
abstract: This review asked which maternal–infant clinical decisions are plausible targets for CRISPR diagnostics, what evidence currently supports those roles, and what validation remains necessary. We conducted a structured narrative review of CRISPR diagnostics for HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV), and syphilis, evaluating complete specimen-to-result systems rather than isolated nuclease reactions. Across the studies identified, HIV early infant diagnosis (EID) had the strongest near-term clinical rationale but lacked validation of microvolume whole blood or dried blood spots, broad HIV-1 inclusivity, and integrated process controls. Maternal HBV had the broadest clinical-specimen evidence, but no identified study established IU/mL-traceable classification around a pregnancy prophylaxis decision boundary. Syphilis direct detection supported a narrower specimen- and stage-dependent adjunctive role and could not replace antenatal serology or exclude congenital infection when negative. Major cross-cutting gaps included specimen preparation, calibration, contamination containment, invalid-result detection, and multisite intended-use validation. These findings do not establish routine clinical readiness. As an evidence-informed development priority, a shared service platform with separately validated pathogen-specific assays appears more defensible in the near term than a universal single-tube triplex.

title: Resolved hepatitis B is associated with higher reactivation risk than chronic infection after chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.

title: Hepatitis B prevalence in the Levant: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Review title: Hepatitis B prevalence in the Levant: a systematic review and meta-analysis Type and method of review: Meta analysis Stage of review at time of this submission: Review ongoing — the protocol has been finalised and the peer-reviewed search prepared; formal screening not yet started. Review question: In General population and subgroups (blood donors, pregnant women, high-risk groups) in the Levant: Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Palestine, what is the effect of Hepatitis B virus infection (HBsAg positivity) compared with None on Pooled HBsAg seroprevalence, overall and by subgroup and country? Searches: The following sources will be searched: Europe PMC (PubMed, MEDLINE & preprints), PubMed / MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection. Additional records may be imported from other databases. No date or language restrictions are applied unless otherwise stated. The search strategy underwent peer review (PRESS) before execution. Condition or domain being studied: General population and subgroups (blood donors, pregnant women, high-risk groups) in the Levant: Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Palestine Participants / population: General population and subgroups (blood donors, pregnant women, high-risk groups) in the Levant: Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Palestine Intervention(s), exposure(s): Hepatitis B virus infection (HBsAg positivity) Comparator(s) / control: None Types of study to be included: Inclusion criteria: Populations in Lebanon, Syria, Jordan or Palestine; HBsAg tested by serological assay; Reports HBsAg prevalence or data allowing its calculation; Cross-sectional or cohort studies; Full-text article published in English. Exclusion criteria: Case-only series of HBV-positive patients; Populations outside the Levant (e.g., refugees elsewhere) without separable Levant data; Reviews, editorials, letters or conference abstracts; Overlapping cohorts (the largest or most recent report is kept) Main outcome(s): Pooled HBsAg seroprevalence, overall and by subgroup and country Data extraction (selection and coding): Two reviewers will independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts, blinded to each other’s decisions, and extract data in duplicate using a standardised, piloted form. Disagreements will be resolved by discussion or a third reviewer. Risk of bias (quality) assessment: The risk of bias of each included study will be assessed independently by two reviewers using a study-design-appropriate tool. Disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Risk of bias in the review itself will be appraised with ROBIS. Strategy for data synthesis: Results will be synthesised narratively. Where studies are sufficiently homogeneous, effect estimates will be pooled in a meta-analysis using a fixed- or random-effects model as indicated by heterogeneity (I2). The certainty of the evidence will be rated using GRADE.

title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. source_records.title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. title: Ten-Year Outcomes in Liver Transplantation for HBV/HDV Coinfection: A Romanian Single-Center Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV)/hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection is a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and remains a disproportionately frequent indication for liver transplantation (LT) in Romania, one of the highest-HDV-prevalence countries in Europe, yet patient-level outcome data from this high-burden Eastern European setting are lacking. We report the ten-year outcomes of LT for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis in a large single-centre Romanian cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 236 adults transplanted for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis at a single tertiary centre. Survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method and predictors were assessed by Cox regression. HBV, HDV and HCC recurrence, and anti-HBs kinetics under combined hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG)/nucleos(t)ide-analogue prophylaxis, were analysed. Results: Over a median follow-up of 8.1 years (maximum 14.4), overall survival was 89.8%, 82.8% and 79.5% at 1, 5 and 10 years; among 90-day survivors, conditional survival reached 86.9% at 10 years. Under an “on-demand” low-dose HBIG protocol combined with nucleos(t)ide analogues, HBV recurrence (HBsAg reappearance) occurred in 4.7% and HDV recurrence in 1.7% of patients, without graft dysfunction or death attributable to viral recurrence; anti-HBs titres stabilised at 120–140 IU/L beyond the first year, with approximately 60% of patients maintaining levels above 100 IU/L long-term. HBsAg reappearance occurred exclusively in HCC recipients (11/87 vs. 0/149, p < 0.001) and clustered in patients with tumour recurrence (9/17 vs. 2/70, p < 0.001), preceding the radiological diagnosis of recurrence in six of the nine patients concerned. Mortality was concentrated in the perioperative period (90-day mortality 8.5%), driven mainly by sepsis and surgical complications, and recurrent HCC was the most common recorded cause of late death. Neither the severity of liver disease at listing (MELD, ALBI) nor any viral variable was associated with survival; HCC as indication was associated with survival in univariable analysis and beyond-Milan tumour burden independently (HR 2.74, 95% CI 1.36–5.54). Conclusions: LT for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis achieves excellent long-term survival and very low viral recurrence under combined prophylaxis, even in this HDV-hyperendemic setting; beyond the perioperative period, viral factors were not associated with survival, whereas beyond-Milan tumour burden was associated with worse survival in one of the sensitivity analyses. In this HBV/HDV cohort, HBsAg reappearance after transplantation for HCC was associated with tumour recurrence and may be regarded as a warning sign prompting oncological reassessment; whether it represents a true early marker requires prospective validation.

title: Infection specific risk factors and ABO blood group associations among blood donors in northern and Bono East Ghana
abstract: Transfusion-transmissible infections (TTIs) remain a substantial public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa. Most surveillance reports describe overall burden among blood donors, but determinants of individual infections are less well characterised. We describe the burden of HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV) and syphilis among donors in northern and Bono East Ghana and identify donor characteristics associated with each infection, with exploratory analysis of ABO and Rhesus blood groups. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of routine records from 3,348 blood donors with complete data, collected between 2017 and 2022 at six secondary-level hospitals across northern and Bono East Ghana. Separate logistic regression models were fitted for each infection. Sparse-data analyses (HCV, co-infections, HIV) were treated as exploratory. Among 3,348 donors (91.2% male; mean age 28.9 years), 495 (14.78%) were positive for at least one TTI. Syphilis was the most common (8.18%), followed by HBV (5.05%), HCV (2.21%) and HIV (0.72%). First-time donation was independently associated with HBV (AOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.53–5.41). Regional differences dominated the syphilis model, with markedly higher odds in the Upper West and Oti areas. Blood group AB was associated with HBV (AOR 3.34, p = 0.005) but this did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and is hypothesis-generating. A first time-by-residence interaction was detected ( p = 0.004): first-time rural donors had the highest prevalence (22.5%) and repeat rural donors the lowest (1.0%). TTI burden among donors was high and strongly patterned by donor type and region. First-time and rural donors, and the Oti area, carry a disproportionate share of infections and are the logical focus for donor-conversion and screening efforts. ABO findings are exploratory and do not support blood-group-based risk stratification.

title: Impact of hepatitis delta virus infection on waiting list outcomes: A competing-risks analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND Liver transplantation is the gold standard for end-stage liver disease, but the shortage of donor organs results in extended waiting lists and considerable mortality before a graft becomes available. Model for end-stage liver disease (MELD)-based allocation has reduced waiting-list mortality and shortened waiting times across many national programs, but its predictive accuracy is not uniform. Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection promotes faster progression of fibrosis and leads to earlier decompensation. Whether HDV status provides independent prognostic information beyond the MELD score in predicting waiting-list outcomes remains insufficiently investigated. AIM To assess the impact of hepatitis delta infection on waiting-list outcomes through a competing-risks analysis. METHODS We conducted an ambispective national cohort study of adults listed for liver transplantation (1 January 2013-31 December 2025). The retrospective phase covered 2013-2017 and the prospective phase 2018-2025. Two separate etiologic analyses were performed, comparing HDV infection first with hepatitis B virus (HBV) monoinfection and then with non-delta viral infection, comprising HBV monoinfection, HBV/hepatitis C virus (HCV) coinfection, and HCV monoinfection. Death on the waiting list and transplantation were treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions (CIF) were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Multivariable cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were fitted for death and for transplantation. RESULTS Of 313 adults, 174 (55.6%) had delta infection. The delta group had a more advanced baseline profile. The 5-year CIF of waiting-list death did not differ between the delta and non-delta viral groups (45.9% vs 42.9%; Gray’s test, P = 0.696), whereas transplantation was more frequent in the delta group (43.1% vs 21.7%; P = 0.001). In cause-specific models for the viral cohort, HDV approximately doubled the hazard of both waiting-list death [cause-specific hazard ratio (csHR) = 2.12, 95%CI: 1.38-3.24, P CONCLUSION HDV increased the cause-specific hazard of waiting-list death, but this effect was attenuated by more frequent transplantation. HDV status may aid risk stratification in endemic settings, although current evidence is insufficient to justify a formal MELD exception.
