title: Interferon-Induced Protein 6 (IFI6): Biological Functions, Molecular Mechanisms and Pathological Roles in Human Diseases
abstract: Interferon (IFN)-induced protein 6 (IFI6) is an important member of the IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) family. It plays significant roles in anti-apoptosis, immune regulation, maintenance of mitochondrial homeostasis, antiviral defense, and tumor progression. At the molecular mechanism level, IFI6 inhibits mitochondrial membrane depolarization, cytochrome c release, and caspase activation. It also regulates the balance between B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2)/Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim), activates the Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathways, and upregulates the ferroptosis-related proteins solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby enhancing cell survival and proliferation through multiple pathways. In terms of immune regulation, IFI6 is associated with immune cells (such as T/B cells, etc.) and the tumor microenvironment. IFI6 regulates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, influencing respiratory chain assembly and metabolism. In terms of viral infection, IFI6 may inhibit the replication of multiple viruses (such as hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), SARS-CoV-2, etc.) by inhibiting flavivirus-induced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) invagination, interfering with retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathways, and inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase activity. In addition, IFI6 is highly expressed in autoimmune diseases and malignant tumors and is associated with proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In this review, we aim to highlight IFI6 as a potential key target in disease diagnosis and treatment.

title: Modulation of the FAK-Src Signalling Axis by Oncoviruses: Molecular Mechanisms, Functional Consequences, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Oncoviruses play a role in cellular transformation and cancer progression by manipulating host signalling pathways, such as the FAK-Src axis. Preclinical evidence suggests that viral proteins can modulate this axis through direct interactions, integrin signalling, tumour suppressor inactivation, transcriptional and kinase reprogramming, calcium/ROS signalling, regulation of phosphatases, and epigenetic modifications. Important examples include HPV E2 and E6/E7, EBV LMP1 and LMP2A, HBV HBx, HCV Core and E2, and KSHV proteins. FAK-Src disruption can activate pathways such as PI3K/AKT, Rho GTPase, AP-1, and NF-κB, thereby enhancing migration, invasion, survival, angiogenesis, and modulation of the immune response. In some infections, this axis may also be involved at different stages of the viral life cycle. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of FAK-Src regulation by oncoviruses and its functional and therapeutic implications. It also reviews FAK/Src targeting strategies, distinguishing experimental inhibitors, multitargeted agents, and compounds under clinical evaluation, emphasising the limited clinical evidence specific to each virus. Finally, pFAK and pSrc are reviewed as potential markers of pathway activation and pharmacodynamic interaction with the target; however, current evidence is insufficient for their use as valid diagnostic or predictive biomarkers. A better understanding of the virus-host-FAK/Src interaction could help develop mechanism-based therapeutic approaches and biomarker-based patient selection.

title: Novel Technologies and Clinical Breakthroughs: The Evolving Landscape of Gene Therapy in China.
abstract: Gene therapy offers a fundamental approach to treating genetic disorders, malignant tumors, and refractory chronic diseases by directly modifying or replacing defective genes at the molecular level. Driven by policy support, increased investment, and technological innovation, China has achieved remarkable progress in adenoviral and adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors, gene editing, genetically engineered immune cells, oncolytic microorganisms, and small nucleic acid drugs. This review provides a comprehensive narrative overview of the technical principles, product pipelines, and clinical advances in these fields. Notable achievements include the approval of AAV-based gene therapy products in China, the entry of multiple in vivo and ex vivo gene editing therapies into clinical trials, a leading number of CAR-T trials worldwide with expansion into solid tumors and autoimmune diseases, encouraging efficacy of oncolytic virotherapy in liver cancer and melanoma, and positive clinical data of small interfering RNA/antisense oligonucleotide drugs for chronic hepatitis B and hypercholesterolemia. However, challenges remain including suboptimal tissue specificity, off-target risks, limited cargo capacity, high production costs, and poor accessibility. Future directions should focus on tissue-selective vectors, precise editing tools, off-the-shelf cell products, scalable manufacturing, and improved regulatory frameworks. With abundant clinical resources and strong manufacturing capabilities, China is poised to play a significant role in the global gene therapy landscape.

title: Systems Pharmacology of Human Oncoviruses: Network-Based Drug Discovery for Virus-Driven Cancers.
abstract: Human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, MCPyV, KSHV, and HTLV-1, account for approximately 15%-20% of global human malignancies. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, viral oncoproteins systematically rewire host regulatory networks, rendering conventional single-target oncology paradigms vulnerable to rapid resistance and clinical failure. Systems pharmacology offers a transformative, network-centric framework that views virus-driven cancers as systemic perturbations of host protein-protein interaction networks. This review synthesises computational methodology, network topology, and drug discovery strategies across major human oncoviruses. We examine how graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (S AB ) uncover hidden network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing. Despite distinct genomic structures and tissue tropisms, oncogenic viruses converge on shared host interactome hubs, notably TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, to drive cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling. We evaluate repositioned synthetic pharmaceuticals (such as kinase inhibitors and host ion channel blockers) and multi-target bioactive formulations, detailing their mechanisms in targeting viral host dependencies. Finally, we address key translational bottlenecks, including disparities between in silico binding predictions and in vivo pharmacokinetics, extensive plasma protein binding, tumour penetration barriers, and viral latency reservoirs. Overcoming these hurdles will require integrating deep graph learning, single-cell spatial multi-omics, and patient-derived organoid models to accelerate the clinical realization of network-targeted therapies in viral oncology.

title: Clinical Risk Factors for Advanced Fibrosis in Pathology-Proven Steatotic Liver Disease: Emphasis on Nonelder Subjects.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) may lead to advanced liver diseases. We aimed to identify clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis in pathology-proven SLD patients in a hepatitis B virus (HBV) endemic population, with emphasis on nonelder subjects. METHODS: Adult SLD patients diagnosed via pathology at National Taiwan University Hospital between June 2009 and December 2023 were recruited. Advanced fibrosis was defined as F2 to F4 fibrosis. Patients were stratified by age (< 50 years defined as nonelder), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and HBV infection. Clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis and at-risk steatohepatitis were investigated, and the predictive performance of noninvasive scores was examined. RESULTS: Among 223 pathology-proven SLD patients, older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.04), alcohol consumption (OR: 5.77), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (OR: 2.13), chronic HBV infection (OR: 2.52), and obesity (OR: 2.64) were independent risk factors for advanced fibrosis. In the nonelder subgroup, older age (OR: 1.10) and obesity (OR: 3.75) were significant. In the MASLD subgroup, older age (OR: 1.04), hypertension (OR: 2.31), T2DM (OR: 3.07), and chronic HBV infection (OR: 3.59) remained significant. Obesity (OR: 4.14) was a significant risk factor for at-risk steatohepatitis in the nonelder subgroup. NAFLD fibrosis score had the highest AUROC (0.724) for advanced fibrosis in the entire cohort, while FIB-4 performed best in nonelder subjects. CONCLUSIONS: Older age, alcohol, T2DM, chronic HBV infection, and obesity were associated with advanced fibrosis. Risk factors and noninvasive score performance varied in nonelder subjects.

title: Comparative Burden and Attributable Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in China versus G20 Nations from 1990 to 2040: A Joinpoint Regression and Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling Study
abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a principal contributor to cancer-related deaths globally, presenting significant public health and economic challenges. This investigation presents a detailed examination of the spatial and temporal progression, associated risk factors, and projected trajectories of HCC burden in China and G20 nations spanning the period from 1990 to 2040. Leveraging data from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study, we applied descriptive statistical methods, Joinpoint regression analysis, Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) modeling, ARIMA forecasting techniques, and risk factor decomposition. Findings revealed that while the absolute count of HCC cases rose, largely attributable to demographic aging, the age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) exhibited a downward trend from 1990 to 2023. This reduction was more pronounced in China compared to the G20 average, despite China’s rates continuing to exceed the group mean. Notable inequalities were identified, with higher burdens observed among males, older populations, and G20 countries with lower socioeconomic status. A transition in the etiological profile was evident: the proportion of cases attributable to hepatitis B virus (HBV) declined, whereas the fraction linked to metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) rose significantly. Projections for 2040, generated through integrated BAPC-ARIMA models, anticipate a persistent decrease in age-standardized rates. Scenario modeling indicated that enhanced control of primary risk factors—including HBV, HCV, alcohol use, tobacco consumption, and MAFLD—could markedly hasten this decline. In summary, despite advancements, the HCC burden remains substantial, with a growing contribution from metabolic risks. These results highlight the necessity for precise, resource-adapted preventive measures, with particular emphasis on addressing MAFLD and existing inequalities, to effectively reduce the future impact of HCC.

title: Sociocultural Determinants of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prevention Behaviors Among Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Adults in the United States.
abstract: Background Prevention is critical to reduce hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) burden, however, sociocultural influences on engagement in HCC preventive behaviors among populations at elevated risk are rarely examined together. We sought to evaluate sociocultural factors associated with HCC preventive behaviors among Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) and Hispanic adults. Methods Pooled 2015-2024 NHIS data were used to identify NHB and Hispanic adults. HCC prevention behaviors included hepatitis B (HBV) vaccination, hepatitis C (HCV) testing, alcohol risk reduction, healthy weight, and physical activity. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated associations between sociocultural factors and prevention behaviors adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, healthcare access, and immigration factors. Results Among 74,162 adults (NHB: 44.7%, n=33,166; Hispanic: 55.3%, n=40,996), HBV vaccination was lower among individuals aged 45-64 compared with those aged 18-30 years old (aOR 0.38; 95%CI 0.34-0.42), whereas college graduates had higher vaccine uptake (aOR 2.01; 95%CI 1.70-2.38). Adults aged 31-44 years were more likely to get tested for HCV (aOR 1.88; 95%CI 1.57-2.26). Alcohol moderation was higher among women (aOR 2.01; 95%CI 1.81-2.22) and lower among Hispanic than NHB adults (aOR 0.53; 95%CI 0.46-0.60). Higher education attainment was associated with healthy weight (aOR 1.56; 95%CI 1.38-1.77). Immigration status modified racial/ethnic prevention patterns (interaction p=0.009); long-term foreign-born noncitizen Black adults had higher vaccination rates (aOR 3.50; 95%CI 1.37-8.94). Discussion Engagement in HCC prevention behaviors among NHB and Hispanic adults was strongly affected by age, education, insurance coverage, healthcare access, and immigration context, highlighting structural influences on prevention opportunities. Equity-focused strategies expanding vaccination, screening, and lifestyle interventions are required.

title: Surgical resection combined with TACE for primary clear cell carcinoma of the liver: a case report and literature review
abstract: Background Primary clear cell carcinoma of the liver (PCCCL) is an uncommon hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) subtype that resembles extrahepatic clear cell tumors, posing diagnostic challenges. Case presentation A 74-year-old woman with hepatitis B–related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class A) presented with acute abdominal pain and vomiting. Imaging revealed a hypervascular hepatic lesion with intralesional fat, while serum AFP was normal and CA125 mildly elevated. Laparoscopic partial hepatectomy was performed. Histology confirmed PCCCL, and immunohistochemistry supported hepatic origin while excluding metastatic renal carcinoma. The patient subsequently received two sessions of postoperative TACE as an individualized treatment and remained free of recurrence or metastasis during surveillance from 2022 to 2025. Conclusion PCCCL is rare and difficult to distinguish from conventional HCC or metastatic clear cell carcinoma. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry is essential for diagnosis. Surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment. Although this patient remained recurrence-free after postoperative TACE, the role of TACE cannot be determined based on a single case, and studies with larger sample sizes are still needed.

title: Antiangiogenic Class and Trial Population Are Confounded in First- Line Immunotherapy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Nine Randomised Trials
abstract: Abstract Background First-line therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) combines an immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) with one of two antiangiogenic backbones: an anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody or a VEGFR-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). No head-to-head trial exists, and successive network meta-analyses have ranked the two classes and reported class-level probabilities as estimates of a drug-class property. Objective To estimate the class comparison and, separately, to test whether a class effect is identifiable from the aggregate trial data on which such rankings are based. Methods Nine randomised trials (5,333 patients) were synthesised in a Bayesian random-effects network anchored on sorafenib. Because each treatment appears in a single trial, between-study heterogeneity is not identifiable from the data; it was therefore specified using the external empirical predictive distributions of Turner et al., and every efficacy estimate reported here is conditional on that externally sourced prior. Outcomes were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response (ORR) and grade ≥3 adverse events. Five effect modifiers were pre-specified; their joint distribution across trials was examined before interpreting any class-level estimate. Results Three regimens improved OS over sorafenib: sintilimab plus bevacizumab (HR 0.57, 95% credible interval 0.35–0.92), finotonlimab plus bevacizumab (0.60, 0.37–0.99) and camrelizumab plus rivoceranib (0.64, 0.41–0.99). The posterior probability favouring the anti-VEGF-antibody class was 75.0% for OS, 74.8% for ORR and 45.3% for PFS. These estimates are not interpretable as class effects. Treatment class, hepatitis B virus prevalence, macrovascular invasion and China-only enrolment were mutually collinear across trials (pairwise r = 0.81–0.91; HBV–China r = 0.87), so a survival advantage attributed to drug class is equally consistent with one attributable to the populations in which each class was tested. title: Editorial: Liver diseases – from pathophysiology to new treatment options
abstract: Liver diseases are a major global health challenge, spanning viral, autoimmune, cholestatic, metabolic, and alcohol-associated diseases, with progression to cirrhosis, decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Advances in molecular biology, genetics, immunology, and systems biology are refining our understanding of disease progression and informing new diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies. This Frontiers in Immunology Research Topic brought together basic, translational, and clinical studies focused on inflammation, metabolic and immune dysregulation, fibrogenesis, biomarkers, non-invasive approaches, and emerging therapies. Collectively, these studies highlight both shared biological pathways and disease-specific mechanisms relevant to precision diagnosis and treatment.Viral hepatitis remains a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality, with more than 300 million people worldwide living with chronic hepatitis B (HBV) or hepatitis C (HCV) infection [1][2][3][4]. Despite major advances in HBV vaccination, long-term antiviral suppression, and highly effective curative therapy for HCV, substantial gaps in diagnosis, linkage to care, and treatment coverage persist globally.HBV infection follows a complex, dynamic natural history characterized by overlapping clinical phases shaped by host immune response, viral replication, and age at infection [5].HBV evasion strategies. They summarized how pattern-recognition receptors sense HBVderived DNA and RNA, including pregenomic RNA, as well as viral proteins, with particular emphasis on Toll-like receptors and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like pathways. The authors further discussed how HBV interferes with these sensing mechanisms to establish persistent infection. By delineating the interplay between viral components and host innate immunity, this review highlights pattern-recognition receptor pathways as potential targets for future immunomodulatory approaches [6].Immune dysfunction, namely immune paralysis, characterized by impaired innate immune responses, compromised antimicrobial defense, and increased susceptibility to secondary infections, was the focus of Xiaoqin Liu et al.'s study of patients with HBV-related acuteon-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). The authors identified Methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 2 (MBD2) as significantly upregulated in HBV-ACLF monocytes, with expression levels correlating with disease severity, systemic inflammation, and clinical outcome.Mechanistic studies showed that loss of MBD2 increased chromatin accessibility and transcription of genes involved in antigen presentation and pro-inflammatory responses, including pathways related to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II synthesis.These findings suggest that MBD2 epigenetically represses HLA-DR expression in monocytes, leading to impaired antigen presentation and immune paralysis. The authors proposed MBD2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for restoring immune competence in ACLF. [7] Continuing with HBV-oriented immune responses, Fangfang Li et al. contributed a manuscript aimed at identifying characteristic hub genes in the immune-active phase of chronic hepatitis B, defined by positive serum HBsAg, elevated alanine transaminase (ALT) levels, and detectable HBV DNA. By integrating transcriptomic analyses, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine-learning approaches, the authors identified four candidate hub genes-CCR5, IL10RA, KCNA3, and SLC24A4associated with the immune-active phase. Among these, SLC24A4 emerged as a particularly relevant immune-regulatory candidate. In silico knockout analyses suggested that SLC24A4 may act as a negative regulator of monocyte activation, highlighting SLC24A4 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for immune-modulatory strategies in chronic HBV infection [8].Progressive development of liver fibrosis, which can eventually lead to cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma, is a key determinant of long-term prognosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B [9].To unravel this process, Jiahao Wu et al. investigated the role of Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) signaling in HBV-related fibrogenic progression. Using an integrated bioinformatics approach, the authors identified CCND1 and IL7R as key JAK-STAT pathway-associated genes in HBV-related fibrosis. Functional analyses further indicated that CCND1 and IL7R are involved in immune regulatory and profibrotic pathways and are closely associated with M1 macrophages and other immune cell subsets, thereby identifying CCND1 and IL7R as potential biomarkers and molecular targets in HBV-associated liver fibrosis [10].Current treatment of HBV infection relies primarily on potent nucleos(t)ide analogs and, in selected patients, pegylated interferon-α (Peg-IFN-α); however, achieving functional cure, defined as sustained HBsAg loss, remains uncommon, underscoring the need for reliable predictors of treatment response and strategies that optimize efficacy while minimizing treatment-related toxicity [11,12] Two contributions to this Research Topic specifically addressed these issues in relation to Peg-IFN-α. studied 91 HBV-infected individuals to test whether early ontreatment expression of ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1 (ENPP1) and interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 2 (IFIT2) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells could serve as biomarkers to predict hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance and therapeutic responses. Both ENPP1 and IFIT2 mRNA levels increased in patients with virological and serological responses; their expression levels at weeks 12 and 24 positively correlated with HBsAg reduction, and their early induction at week 12 was associated with subsequent HBsAg decline. Furthermore, combining ENPP1 and IFIT2 improved predictive performance, supporting their potential utility as early biomarkers of Peg-IFN-α response [13].Along these lines, Liya Zhu et al. reviewed the mechanisms and management of Peg-IFNα toxicity in chronic HBV infection. The authors describe the most common and serious adverse effects, explain the pathophysiological mechanisms behind each, and, in the final section, discuss predictive biomarkers, risk prediction, and personalized management. The review therefore provides a clinically oriented framework for anticipating, monitoring, and managing Peg-IFN-α-associated toxicity, with particular emphasis on individualized risk assessment [14].Xingtao Jin et al. provided a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the evolving field of immunotherapy for chronic HBV infection. They discussed the growing interest in immune-based approaches to an HBV cure. China and the United States emerged as the leading contributors. At the same time, keyword and citation analyses revealed growing interest in the persistence of viral reservoirs, profound immune dysfunction and exhaustion, and mechanisms linking chronic HBV infection to hepatocellular carcinoma. Notably, the literature landscape indicates a clear shift toward combination strategies that integrate potent viral suppression with immune modulation [15].Despite the highly effective direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, HCV remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality [2]. Although DAA treatment has led to successful HCV eradication in more than 95% of patients, regardless of comorbidities [16], the presence of cirrhosis and/or portal hypertension poses a significant clinical challenge.In their published study, Ruben Martin-Escolano et al. investigated the immunological determinants of persistent portal hypertension after HCV cure in patients with advanced cirrhosis, with particular emphasis on the impact of HIV coinfection. In this prospective study of 41 patients, baseline immune profiles were associated with changes in the hepatic venous pressure gradient over 48 weeks. In patients without HIV, impaired portal pressure regression was linked to systemic inflammation and broad CD4+ T-cell activation. In contrast, HIV-coinfected patients exhibited a distinct profile marked by endothelial dysfunction and activation of effector-memory and TemRA CD4+ T cells. These findings suggest that HIV reshapes the immunological mechanisms governing hepatic recovery after HCV eradication and may help identify pathways that contribute to residual portal hypertension despite virological cure [17].Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs) encompass a heterogeneous group of chronic inflammatory disorders, including autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), and primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), with a steadily rising worldwide prevalence [18]. Despite substantial advances in understanding their immunopathogenesis, the mechanisms that drive disease initiation, progression, and phenotypic heterogeneity remain incompletely understood [19][20][21]. Zefeng Zhang's review focused on the complex pathogenesis of these diseases, namely the AIH-PBC and AIH-PSC variants. The author described distinct immune architectures characterized by T-cell dysfunction, pro-inflammatory macrophage niches, B-cell activation, tertiary lymphoid structures, and senescent cholangiocytes. As a result, persistent crosstalk among adaptive immune cells, the biliary epithelium, bile acid signaling, and inflammatory pathways may sustain liver injury despite conventional immunosuppression. The review also highlights emerging precision approaches, including JAK inhibition and B-cell-depleting therapies, for difficult-to-treat disease [22].To better understand AILD pathogenesis, Wenjuan Wang et al. examined the significance of ductopenia in PBC. In a study of 518 patients with biopsy-proven PBC, ductopenia was common, affecting 56.76% of patients, including 24.83% with early-stage disease. In multivariable logistic regression, serum ANA ≥1:1000, elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase and total bilirubin, and low serum albumin emerged as biomarkers for ductopenia in patients with early-stage PBC. During follow-up, patients with ductopenia had a higher prevalence of liver-related adverse events, underscoring the significance of ductopenia in disease progression. [23] PBC has recently attracted significant interest due to the rapid expansion of second-line treatments, including the two approved peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) agonists, elafibranor and seladelpar, as well as several additional agents in clinical development [24].Against the rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape, Angelara et al. reviewed current and emerging treatment options for PBC. The authors emphasize that a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve an adequate biochemical response to first-line ursodeoxycholic acid and discuss the efficacy, safety, and positioning of recently introduced PPAR agonists.They also review emerging agents targeting FXR, FGF19/FGFR4, NOX1/4, immune pathways, and bile acid transport, illustrating the ongoing shift toward more individualized, mechanism-based treatment strategies [25].Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is another autoimmune disease that commonly affects the biliary tract but usually spares the liver [26]. reported a rare case of seronegative, IgG4-related hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor (IgG4-HIPT) in a 60-year-old man with multifocal hepatic lesions, mild inflammatory symptoms, and normal serum IgG4 levels. Histopathological analysis showed dense IgG4-positive lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative phlebitis, establishing the diagnosis of IgG4-HIPT, which responded well to corticosteroids. The authors also discuss the immunopathogenesis, significance, and differential diagnosis of this rare entity [27]. Beyond its rarity, the case highlights the potential dissociation between circulating biomarkers and tissue-level immune activity. It underscores the importance of histological assessment in the differential diagnosis of atypical hepatic lesions.Metabolic dysfunction and alcohol exposure are increasingly important drivers of chronic liver disease and share key mechanisms with other forms of liver injury, such as oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysregulation, and hepatocellular damage [28,29].MASLD is a leading cause of chronic liver disease, encompassing steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and HCC, and is closely associated with cardiovascular and metabolic disease [29]. Contributions to this Research Topic span clinical and metabolic markers, immune mechanisms, and experimental therapies.particularly those with clinically diagnosed non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), in a large case-control cohort from Qatar. Hematological abnormalities, particularly thrombocytopenia, were more prevalent among patients with NASH, and higher fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index values were independently associated with anemia and abnormal platelet counts. The progressive increase in platelet abnormalities across higher FIB-4 risk categories further supports the potential value of readily available hematological parameters for identifying patients at increased risk of advanced fibrosis [30]. Alcohol remains a major cause of chronic hepatocellular injury [35]. However, MASLD and ALD have distinct initiating factors; both share mechanisms of oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysregulation, metabolic alterations, and progressive hepatocellular damage [36].Zhou et al. used an integrated multi-omics strategy to distinguish potential causal mediators of ALD from merely associated biomarkers. Mendelian randomization, followed by genetic, single-cell transcriptomic, and experimental analyses, identified four compelling proteins: triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-like 2 (TREML2) and matrix metallopeptidase 12 (MMP12), which were associated with increased ALD risk, and phospholipase A2 receptor 1 (PLA2R1) and MYC-associated factor X (MAX), which appeared protective. The localization of risk-associated proteins predominantly to hepatic myeloid cells further supports the importance of inflammation and matrix remodeling in ALD and identifies potential targets for future therapeutic investigation [37].Chronic liver diseases of diverse etiologies converge on inflammation, hepatic stellate cell activation, and extracellular matrix accumulation, making fibrosis a central process that links disease-specific injury to advanced chronic liver disease [38].Lu et al. reviewed how multi-omics technologies are reshaping our understanding of hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis across etiologies, including viral hepatitis, ALD, and MASLD. Integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data highlights common mechanisms, such as hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix deposition, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and metabolic alterations. These approaches may uncover molecular pathways, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets that conventional methods do not readily identify. At the same time, cross-species comparisons underscore both the translational value and the limitations of experimental models [39].Persistent fibrogenesis culminates in cirrhosis, marked by architectural distortion and major vascular, metabolic, and immune dysfunction [40]. Contributions to this Research Topic address both the molecular diagnosis of rare inherited diseases and the changing epidemiology of cirrhosis at the population level. The transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis represents a major turning point in the natural history of chronic liver disease [43]. The development of ascites, variceal bleeding, or hepatic encephalopathy reflects complex interactions among portal hypertension, systemic inflammation, circulatory dysfunction, and declining hepatic reserve [44]. In a subset of patients, acute precipitating events may further destabilize this balance, leading to acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a syndrome characterized by severe systemic inflammation, immune dysfunction, organ failure, and high short-term mortality [45]. HCC is another major consequence of chronic liver disease, with cirrhosis remaining the principal predisposing condition [47]. Prognosis and treatment depend on tumor burden, liver function, portal hypertension, and patient factors, while immune-based therapies increasingly link tumor biology to the immune environment in chronic liver disease [48].unresectable HCC receiving first-line immunotherapy. In a cohort of 100 patients, several baseline characteristics were associated with overall survival (OS), including albuminbilirubin (ALBI) grade, Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage, macrovascular invasion, up-to-7 criteria, and lymphocyte infiltration. The investigators incorporated the strongest independent prognostic parameters into the ALIVE-IO score, designed to estimate 1-year OS, and internally validated it using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and 10-fold cross-validation. Patients could then be stratified into distinct risk groups with differences in treatment response and survival. Although external validation remains necessary, this study provides a clinically oriented framework for integrating tumor burden, liver function, and host immune characteristics into prognostication [49].The contributions to this Research Topic also extend beyond the conventional continuum from chronic liver injury to cirrhosis and its complications. Increasing attention is being directed toward the interactions among the intestinal microbiome, intestinal barrier, immune system, and liver. Disruption of this gut-liver axis may influence hepatic inflammation and immune responses across multiple liver diseases and contribute to infectious complications, adding another dimension to the complex interplay between hepatic and extrahepatic systems [50].Bai et al. examined the emerging role of the gut-liver axis in invasive liver abscess.Integrating microbiomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic evidence, the authors describe how intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial dysbiosis may facilitate bacterial translocation and alter bile acid and short-chain fatty acid metabolism. These processes may promote hepatic immune dysregulation and inflammation and interact with bacterial virulence mechanisms. Their proposed bacterium-inflammation-virulence framework illustrates how host-microbial interactions may contribute to liver disease and highlights the microbiota and intestinal barrier as potential therapeutic targets [51].Taken together, this Research Topic demonstrates that immune dysregulation links disease initiation, progression, and therapeutic response across viral, autoimmune, cholestatic, metabolic, and alcohol-associated liver diseases. Despite distinct etiologies, viral hepatitis, autoimmune and cholestatic disorders, MASLD, and ALD converge on inflammation, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, cellular injury, and fibrogenesis. Persistent injury can lead to cirrhosis, portal hypertension, decompensation, ACLF, and hepatocarcinogenesis.Several contributions go beyond mechanistic descriptions to identify candidate biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and approaches to treatment personalization. Integrating molecular and immunological insights with clinical phenotyping will be essential to translating these advances into improved outcomes.

title: Hepatic Cysts in Korea: Prevalence, Incidence, and Risk Factors Based on a 5.8-Year Follow-up Health Screening Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic cysts are fluid-filled liver lesions that are mostly asymptomatic, but fewer than 15% of patients present clinically significant symptoms. Reported prevalence ranges from 2.5% to 71%, yet prior studies have been limited by small populations and incomplete assessment of risk factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, incidence, and risk factors using data from a large health screening cohort in Korea. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 78,676 participants in the Health and Prevention Enhancement cohort who underwent abdominal ultrasound at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center from 2003 and 2014. Hepatic cysts were identified using a validated rule-based text-mining algorithm applied to ultrasound reports. Prevalence was estimated from baseline data. Incidence was assessed in 41,179 participants initially negative for hepatic cysts. Risk factors were determined through Cox proportional hazards modeling. RESULTS: The prevalence of hepatic cysts at baseline was 8.54% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 8.34-8.73). The incidence was 23.4 per 1,000 person-years at risk (95% CI, 22.8-24.0). Cox regression identified hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBs-Ag) positivity (hazard ratio [HR], 1.20; 95% CI, 1.00-1.45) and renal cyst presence (HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.31-1.64) as independent risk factors, whereas diabetes mellitus (HR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.54-0.77) and high physical activity (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.81-0.97) appeared protective. CONCLUSION: This study provides the prevalence of 8.54%, incidence, and risk factors of hepatic cysts. Renal cyst presence and HBs-Ag positivity are significant risk factors, whereas high physical activity and diabetic status are protective.

source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic cysts are fluid-filled liver lesions that are mostly asymptomatic, but fewer than 15% of patients present clinically significant symptoms. Reported prevalence ranges from 2.5% to 71%, yet prior studies have been limited by small populations and incomplete assessment of risk factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, incidence, and risk factors using data from a large health screening cohort in Korea. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 78,676 participants in the Health and Prevention Enhancement cohort who underwent abdominal ultrasound at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center from 2003 and 2014. Hepatic cysts were identified using a validated rule-based text-mining algorithm applied to ultrasound reports. Prevalence was estimated from baseline data. Incidence was assessed in 41,179 participants initially negative for hepatic cysts. Risk factors were determined through Cox proportional hazards modeling. RESULTS: The prevalence of hepatic cysts at baseline was 8.54% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 8.34-8.73). The incidence was 23.4 per 1,000 person-years at risk (95% CI, 22.8-24.0). CONCLUSION: This study provides the prevalence of 8.54%, incidence, and risk factors of hepatic cysts. Renal cyst presence and HBs-Ag positivity are significant risk factors, whereas high physical activity and diabetic status are protective.

title: HVSnp: A manually curated database of human SNPS associated with viral infections.
abstract: Abstract We developed the “HVSnp: Human Viruses SNP-related database, a curated database”. HVSnp is exclusive to the human SNPs studied and related to viral diseases, with manually mined and curated information from public SNP databases and scientific articles. We used MySQL (version 8.0) due to the easy management and the Looker Studio online availability. Among the output information, we have SNP identification, reference, alternative, and risk alleles, chromosome, gene, and gene function, summary, among others. In total, HVSnp contains eighteen viral diseases and 2020 records: Adenovirus (17 SNPs), Chikungunya (7), COVID-19 (314), Cytomegalovirus (54), Dengue (62), Epstein-Barr (54), Hepatitis A (3), Hepatitis B (380), Hepatitis C (166), Herpes (8), Human immunodeficiency virus (479), Papillomavirus (87), Influenza (74), Measles (68), Respiratory syncytial virus (50), Sars-CoV (80), West Nile (68), and Zika (49). As one SNP can be associated with more than one virus, the number of unique SNPs is 1691 and 651 genes. HVSnp has supplementary information obtained in articles for the summary elaboration, which contains the most significant results described in the literature about a possible relationship between SNPs and viruses. The database is available at URL: https://lookerstudio.google.com/s/pGUC7m538gQ.

title: Protecting_the_protectors: _occupational_health_and_safety_of_h ealth_workers_in_Sierra_Leone_–_a_systems_analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Health workers in Sierra Leone face significant occupational hazards, yet comprehensive data on their protection remains limited. This paper analyzes the current state of occupational health and safety (OHS) for health workers in Sierra Leone, identifies systemic gaps, and proposes evidence-based interventions. Methods The researcher conducted a mixed-methods situational analysis across 54 healthcare facilities in five provinces, involving surveys with 60 health workers, key informant interviews with policymakers and implementing partners, and document review. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and observation checklists. Results Only 44.4% of facilities had designated OHS responsible personnel. Infection prevention and control programmes existed in most facilities, but hand hygiene compliance was low (32% in tertiary settings). Needlestick injury prevalence ranged from 60–66% across studies, with only 40–45% reporting incidents. Personal protective equipment supply was inconsistent, and only one facility had a compensation scheme. Immunization coverage for hepatitis B was inadequate, particularly for cleaning staff. Nearly 50% of peripheral health unit staff work without salaries, compounding OHS vulnerabilities. Conclusion Sierra Leone's health workers face substantial occupational risks amidst a fragile health system. Strengthening OHS requires policy reform, sustained investment in protective measures, health workforce stabilization, and robust reporting systems. The mpox outbreak demonstrates the urgent need for comprehensive health worker protection.

title: The Role of Viral Pathogens in the Promotion of Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition and Neoplastic Cell Invasion
abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a multistep process in which stationary, polarized epithelial cells lose cell-to-cell adhesion and acquire a mesenchymal phenotype with migratory and invasive properties. Migrating EMT cells express both epithelial and mesenchymal markers, an intermediate hybrid state that allows them to retain some epithelial traits for survival while gaining mobility. After migration and metastasis to a secondary tumor site, EMT cells revert to an epithelial-like state via a mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) to establish new tumors. Cells undergoing EMT may also acquire cancer stem cell properties, leading to chemotherapy resistance and cancer recurrence. Accumulating evidence suggests that both oncogenic and non-oncogenic viruses can induce EMT. Among the oncogenic viruses, EMT has been reported in neoplastic cells infected with human papillomavirus, hepatitis B and C viruses, Epstein–Barr virus, and Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus. Non-oncogenic viruses, including human cytomegalovirus and human immunodeficiency virus, can also induce EMT in neoplastic cells. Furthermore, coinfection of neoplastic cells with two or more oncogenic viruses or oncogenic and non-oncogenic viruses may lead to synergistic and/or additive effects with respect to EMT induction. This review presents our current understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying virus-induced EMT and the role of this transition in promoting neoplastic disease.

title: Socio-Ecological Dimensions of Drug Abuse: Community Knowledge, Experiences, and Responses in Makwanpur District
abstract: This research aims to examine the knowledge, experiences, and responses regarding the effects of drug abuse on society in the Makwanpur district, through results generated from a cross-sectional survey conducted among 220 residents from Hetauda ward No. It comprises of 6032 total population of which 2,930 people were male and 3,102 people wereemale. (National Population and, 2078). A simple random technique was used for field study. Data was analyzed by using both inferential statistics and descriptive method. The findings from this study revealed that cannabis washe most recognized drug, known by 42.72% of respondents. This is followed by opiates. 36.8% of respondents on survey had general understanding of drugs. Despite this awareness, there was a concerning lack of understanding about synthetic drugs. Most respondents (91.8%) were aware of the high risk of diseases like HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B/C associated with drug use. This research indicated peer influence (82.3%) started due to peer influence as the most significant factor influencing initial drug use, while addiction is mainly associated with a perceived lack of personal will power (54.4%). Majority of respondents acknowledged the growing trend of drug abuse among males (92.7%) aged 15-30 years (90.5%), with significant negative consequences on various social, economic, health, and educational aspects of the society. Increased accidents (40%), higher healthcare costs (33.6%), and diminished educational outcomes (57.3%) were among the major impacts noted by the respondents. The study also highlights that it is difficult for law enforcement efforts in controlling cannabis cultivation because of high profits associated with this cash crop. The result from this study suggests requirements enhancing public awareness, creating employment opportunities for youth, promoting alternative farming, and improving border controls to combat drug trafficking. This study illustrates that there is an urgent need for coordinated efforts among various relevant stakeholders to alleviate the adverse effects of drug abuse in Makwanpur district.

source_records.title: Socio-Ecological Dimensions of Drug Abuse: Community Knowledge, Experiences, and Responses in Makwanpur District
source_records.abstract: This research aims to examine the knowledge, experiences, and responses regarding the effects of drug abuse on society in the Makwanpur district, through results generated from a cross-sectional survey conducted among 220 residents from Hetauda ward No. It comprises of 6032 total population of which 2,930 people were male and 3,102 people wereemale. (National Population and, 2078). A simple random technique was used for field study. Data was analyzed by using both inferential statistics and descriptive method. The findings from this study revealed that cannabis washe most recognized drug, known by 42.72% of respondents. This is followed by opiates. 36.8% of respondents on survey had general understanding of drugs. Despite this awareness, there was a concerning lack of understanding about synthetic drugs. Most respondents (91.8%) were aware of the high risk of diseases like HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B/C associated with drug use. This research indicated peer influence (82.3%) started due to peer influence as the most significant factor influencing initial drug use, while addiction is mainly associated with a perceived lack of personal will power (54.4%). Majority of respondents acknowledged the growing trend of drug abuse among males (92.7%) aged 15-30 years (90.5%), with significant negative consequences on various social, economic, health, and educational aspects of the society. Increased accidents (40%), higher healthcare costs (33.6%), and diminished educational outcomes (57.3%) were among the major impacts noted by the respondents. The study also highlights that it is difficult for law enforcement efforts in controlling cannabis cultivation because of high profits associated with this cash crop. The result from this study suggests requirements enhancing public awareness, creating employment opportunities for youth, promoting alternative farming, and improving border controls to combat drug trafficking. This study illustrates that there is an urgent need for coordinated efforts among various relevant stakeholders to alleviate the adverse effects of drug abuse in Makwanpur district.

title: Abstract B153: Hepatocellular carcinoma screening awareness, testing, and vaccination among Southeast Asian adults in Minnesota: Implications from social isolation, loneliness, connections, and trust
abstract: Abstract Background: Southeast Asian American adults experience a higher risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), driven in part by hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and barriers to prevention. Literature suggests that social capital (e.g., interpersonal relationships, community connection, trust) enhances cancer prevention, but its role in HCC-related prevention among Southeast Asians remains understudied. This study examined the association between social capital and HCC-specific prevention among Southeast Asian adults in Minnesota. Methods: Data was collected in three urban centers in Minnesota through community-engaged survey of Southeast Asian adults (age 18 or older). The sample (n=501) consisted of individuals from various countries of origin (e.g., Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, other). Outcomes were (1) HCC screening awareness, (2) hepatitis B testing, and (3) hepatitis B vaccination. Predictors were social capital measures: (1) social isolation/loneliness (2) social connections, and (3) trusted source of cancer-related information. Covariates were age, gender, relationship status, education, and insurance. In modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors models, we estimated adjusted associations between social capital and each outcome. Analysis was conducted in SAS Studio 3.82. Results: First, social isolation/loneliness was not significantly associated with three outcomes. Compared to adults aged 18-29, those aged 50-69 reported higher screening awareness (PR=2.21; 95% CI=1.46, 3.31) and HBV testing (PR=1.58; 95% CI=1.08, 2.32). Insured (PR=2.09; 95% CI=1.03, 4.23), women (PR=1.27; 95% CI=1.02, 1.57), and more educated (PR=2.10; 95% CI=1.40, 3.14) reported higher prevalence of HBV vaccination. Second, social connectedness was also not significantly associated with three outcomes. Compared to adults aged 18-29, those aged 50-69 reported higher screening awareness (PR=2.20, 95% CI=1.47, 3.29) and HBV testing (PR=1.64; 95% CI=1.11, 2.40). Insured (PR=2.16; 95% CI=1.07, 4.37), women (PR=1.28; 95% CI=1.03, 1.58), and more educated (PR=2.07; 95% CI=1.39, 3.09) participants reported higher prevalence of HBV vaccination. Third, those who trusted doctors and family/friends for cancer-related information reported higher prevalence of screening awareness; government agency (e.g., National Cancer Institute) and charitable organization for higher prevalence of HBV testing; and family/friends, charitable organization, religious organization, and academic researchers reported higher prevalence of HBV vaccination. Conclusion: Contrary to literature linking social capital to cancer screening, social isolation/loneliness and connections were not associated with HCC prevention in this study. HCC prevention may be more closely tied to health care access, socioeconomic factors, and trusted sources of information, rather than general social capital. Potential interventions targeting high-risk population to improve HCC-specific prevention will need to leverage trusted community and tailor to the population. Citation Format: Eunice Y. title: Trends in Hepatitis D Virus Prevalence Among HBsAg-Positive Individuals With and Without HIV in Italy: A Converging Epidemiology.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection has historically been more prevalent among people with HIV (PWH) due to shared transmission routes. Whether HIV status still identifies a subgroup at higher risk of HDV in contemporary settings remains unclear. METHODS: We performed two cross-sectional analyses assessing anti-HDV prevalence among HBsAg-positive PWH enrolled in the ICONA cohort in 2009-2012 and 2019-2023, compared with HIV-negative individuals from the MASTER and PITER cohorts. RESULTS: Anti-HDV prevalence among PWH declined from 19.1% to 12.5%, converging with that observed in HIV-negative individuals (12.7%). Injection drug use markedly decreased over time among PWH and remained the strongest determinant of HDV infection. In multivariable analyses, HDV seropositivity was associated with age, injection drug use, and birth outside Italy, but not with HIV infection in the contemporary period. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that HIV infection is no longer independently associated with HDV infection in this setting and support universal HDV screening strategies.
authors: PITER, MASTER and ICONA Study Groups
journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

Methods We performed two cross-sectional analyses assessing anti-HDV prevalence among HBsAg-positive PWH enrolled in the ICONA cohort in 2009-2012 and 2019-2023, compared with HIV-negative individuals from the MASTER and PITER cohorts. Results Anti-HDV prevalence among PWH declined from 19.1% to 12.5%, converging with that observed in HIV-negative individuals (12.7%). Injection drug use markedly decreased over time among PWH and remained the strongest determinant of HDV infection. In multivariable analyses, HDV seropositivity was associated with age, injection drug use, and birth outside Italy, but not with HIV infection in the contemporary period. Conclusion These findings indicate that HIV infection is no longer independently associated with HDV infection in this setting and support universal HDV screening strategies.

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in individuals without HBV or HCV infection in the MASLD era
abstract: Abstract Current surveillance guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) primarily target individuals with liver cirrhosis or viral hepatitis. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-based model to predict HCC risk in individuals without viral hepatitis. Using the South Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we analyzed 7,961,075 individuals aged 20–79 years who underwent health screening in 2017 and were followed through 2023. Twelve AI models were compared. The best-performing model was retrained and evaluated in an unmatched validation cohort reflecting the original HCC prevalence and an independent non-selected validation cohort. Multi-Head Attention with Deep Neural Network (MHA_DNN) achieved the highest performance (AUC 0.9385, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.9312–0.9455 In the unmatched validation cohort, the model demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUROC 0.9450; AUPRC 0.0503), improved calibration after logistic recalibration, and superior clinical utility. Performance remained consistent in the independent non-selected validation cohort (AUROC 0.8848; AUPRC 0.0293). SHAP analysis identified fatty liver index (FLI) and triglycerides (TG) as the most influential predictors. TG increased HCC risk in individuals with FLI < 60 but showed the opposite association in those with FLI ≥ 60. MHA_DNN provides robust population-level prediction of HCC in individuals without viral hepatitis and supports personalized surveillance based on metabolic risk factors.

title: Diagnostic value of PNI and MLR in cirrhotic patients with negative HBV DNA and positive HBV RNA:A nomogram--based evaluation model
abstract: Introduction To investigate the diagnostic significance of the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) and the Monocyte-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (MLR) for the development of cirrhosis in patients with HBV DNA-negative, HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B, and to evaluate their clinical application value. Methods A total of 87 patients with HBV DNA-negative, HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B who developed cirrhosis and were admitted to the patients from the Second People's Hospital of Fuyang City between March 2024 and March 2025 were enrolled as the observation group. Additionally, 96 patients with HBV DNA-negative and HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B during the same period were selected as the control group. Liver function, AFP levels, and five-part differential blood counts were measured in both groups. The PNI and MLR were calculated and compared between the two groups. ROC curves were plotted to analyze the sensitivity and specificity of PNI and MLR in diagnosing cirrhosis in patients with HBV DNA-negative, HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B, and their correlations were assessed. Furthermore, a nomogram model was established to evaluate the predictive ability of these two indicators for concomitant cirrhosis in this patient population, and the model was validated using a diagnostic calibration curve. Results In No statistically significant differences were observed between the observation and control groups in terms of age, sex, ALT, ALP, or AFP levels ( P > 0.05). Compared with the control group, patients in the observation group showed significantly lower levels of inflammatory markers (white blood cell, lymphocyte, and monocyte counts), nutritional markers (TP, ALB, PA), and PNI, while levels of AST, GGT and MLR were significantly higher ( P < 0.05). A significant negative correlation was observed between PNI and MLR levels in the observation group ( r = −0.484, P < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed that the areas under the curve of PNI and MLR for diagnosing cirrhosis in patients with HBV DNA-negative, HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B were 0.821 and 0.743, with sensitivities of 0.958 and 0.854, respectively ( P < 0.001). The additional analyses convincingly demonstrate that PNI and MLR offer incremental clinical value beyond the widely used FIB-4 and APRI scores. Logistic regression analysis indicated that PNI overexpression was a protective factor for cirrhosis in this patient population. The calibration curve demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis suggested a positive net benefit for the clinical application of this model. Conclusion The Prognostic Nutritional Index and the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio can serve as sensitive and effective biomarkers for the diagnosis of cirrhosis in patients with HBV DNA-negative, HBV RNA-positive hepatitis B. The established nomogram model provides a reference for the clinical diagnosis of cirrhosis in this patient population.

title: MDL-001: An Oral, Direct-Acting Broad-Spectrum Antiviral for Influenza-like Illness (ILI) and Chronic Hepatitis In Vivo
abstract: Background/Objectives: Endemic viral respiratory illnesses caused by influenza, RSV, and coronaviruses impose a global disease burden of hundreds of millions of infections and hundreds of thousands of deaths annually. Chronic hepatitis B and C infections persist in 254 million and 58 million people worldwide, respectively. No approved therapy addresses these viruses simultaneously. MDL-001 is an oral, direct-acting, broad-spectrum antiviral targeting the Thumb-1 allosteric site of viral polymerases. Methods: Here, we evaluated the antiviral activity of MDL-001 in vitro in influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D. We next evaluated MDL-001 antiviral activity in vivo in H1N1, SARS-CoV-2, HCV, and HBV. MDL-001’s in vivo efficacy was compared head-to-head versus standards of care including oseltamivir, remdesivir, sofosbuvir, and tenofovir alafenamide, or through the literature comparison with nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Lastly, we evaluated the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, tolerability, and safety profile of MDL-001. Results: Here, we report that MDL-001 inhibits influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D viruses with nanomolar EC90 potency in vitro. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent in vivo efficacy to oseltamivir against mouse-lethal influenza A virus infection, reducing lung viral load by 2.6 log10 and preventing weight loss and mortality. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent symptom reduction to subcutaneous remdesivir after SARS-CoV-2 infection. MDL-001 reduced SARS-CoV-2 lung viral titers by 2.9 log10, superior to the literature-reported 1.4 log10 and 1.0 log10 reductions for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir, respectively. MDL-001 reduced HCV viremia by 3.3 log10, equivalent to sofosbuvir. Oral MDL-001 reduced plasma HBV surface antigen by 2.5 log10, superior to tenofovir alafenamide from Day 8 through Day 21. MDL-001 demonstrated an in vitro EC50 of 79.4 nM against infection with RSV strain A2, which is a 416-fold improvement over literature-reported ribavirin. Oral pharmacokinetics studies demonstrate that MDL-001 is rapidly absorbed and partitioned into lung (Kp = 39–52) and liver (Kp = 71–104) tissues. MDL-001 produced no treatment-related tolerability adverse events across 376 animals and showed no hERG, Ames genotoxicity, or micronucleus safety issues. Conclusions: These findings support MDL-001 as a broad-spectrum, direct-acting non-nucleoside antiviral clinical candidate.

title: Changes in cardiometabolic biomarkers 1 year after direct acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C virus co-infection among people with HIV.
abstract: Objectives Among people with HIV with hepatitis C virus (HCV) co-infection, we examined differences in haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk score at 12-months following direct acting antiviral (DAA) initiation, comparing people with HIV who initiated DAA with those who did not to explore the utility of DAAs beyond HCV elimination. Methods Utilizing a nested exposure-matched study of people with HIV age ≥ 18 years, on antiretroviral therapy from the NA-ACCORD and the Mass General Brigham HIV cohorts between 01/1/2014 and 12/31/2022, people with HIV with HCV co-infection were identified by detectable plasma HCV RNA. People with HIV who initiated DAA were matched 1:1 with people with HIV who did not initiate DAA. Multivariable linear regression models estimated HbA1c (N = 2374), TC (N = 3418) and ASCVD risk score (N = 488) at 12-months comparing people with HIV who initiated DAAs versus did not. Results We identified no significant difference in the mean HbA1c at 12-months comparing DAA initiators to DAA non-initiators (β: 0.00%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.09% to 0.08%). The mean TC at 12-months was 13 mg/dL (95% CI 11-16 mg/dL) higher in DAA initiators and largely due to increases in LDL. There was no significant difference in the mean ASCVD risk score at 12-months when comparing DAA initiators with those who did not initiate DAAs (β: 1.10, 95% CI -0.09 to 2.20). Conclusion People with HIV with HCV who initiated DAA demonstrated no statistically significant difference in HbA1c or ASCVD risk score at 12-months compared to HIV/HCV co-infected persons who did no initiate DAA. However, TC and LDL levels increased 12 months following DAA treatment.

title: INFECTIOUS MORBIDITY OF THE POPULATION OF UKRAINE IN 2016–2025 IN THE CONTEXT OF EUROPEAN TRENDS
abstract: Infectious diseases remain an important public health problem despite progress in the prevention and control of individual infections. Changes in the epidemiological situation in Ukraine are occurring against the background of global and European trends, which necessitates systematic monitoring and effective forecasting. Identifying current trends in Ukraine and the European Region is important in the context of global challenges and migration processes.Aim. To identify the main trends in infectious morbidity among the population of Ukraine in 2016–2025 and to conduct a comparative assessment with European trends in order to substantiate prevention priorities.Materials and methods. The study used data from official statistical reports of the Public Health Center of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine for 2016–2025, national regulatory and legal documents in the field of epidemiological surveillance, as well as analytical and statistical materials from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Information and analytical, statistical, and epidemiological methods, time-series analysis, and comparative analysis were applied.Results. It was established that Ukraine has an updated regulatory and legal framework aimed at improving epidemiological surveillance and strengthening the control of infectious diseases. During 2016–2025, a decrease in the incidence of socially significant infectious diseases was observed, including a 47.0% reduction in HIV infection, a 71.6% reduction in AIDS, and a 30.5% reduction in tuberculosis. The incidence of acute viral hepatitis A, B, and C decreased by 62.9%, 64.7%, and 26.2%, respectively, whereas the incidence of chronic viral hepatitis B and C increased by 3.3% and 29.6%, respectively. Among other infections, the largest decreases were observed for rubella (−95.7%), pediculosis and phthiriasis (−86.4%), gonococcal infection (−91.5%), and pertussis (−62.6%). At the same time, measles incidence increased 15.3-fold, Lyme disease incidence increased 2.6-fold, and tetanus incidence increased by 20.0%. Regional analysis revealed substantial disparities in the incidence of HIV infection and tuberculosis. The highest rates were observed in Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions, while the lowest rates were recorded in western regions, with differences reaching 9- to 12-fold. These trends correspond to challenges faced by the WHO European Region, where a substantial burden of tuberculosis and HIV infection persists and measles outbreaks continue to occur amid declining routine immunization coverage.Conclusions. Thus, analysis of the ten-year dynamics demonstrates multidirectional changes in infectious morbidity in Ukraine. Alongside a sustained decrease in the incidence of a number of socially significant and vaccine-preventable infections, an increase was observed in the incidence of certain diseases, particularly measles, Lyme disease, and chronic viral hepatitis. This highlights the need for a differentiated approach to assessing the epidemiological situation and for further improvement of epidemiological surveillance, prevention, early detection, and control of infectious diseases, as well as effective outbreak forecasting.

To identify the main trends in infectious morbidity among the population of Ukraine in 2016–2025 and to conduct a comparative assessment with European trends in order to substantiate prevention priorities.Materials and methods. The study used data from official statistical reports of the Public Health Center of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine for 2016–2025, national regulatory and legal documents in the field of epidemiological surveillance, as well as analytical and statistical materials from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Information and analytical, statistical, and epidemiological methods, time-series analysis, and comparative analysis were applied.Results. It was established that Ukraine has an updated regulatory and legal framework aimed at improving epidemiological surveillance and strengthening the control of infectious diseases. During 2016–2025, a decrease in the incidence of socially significant infectious diseases was observed, including a 47.0% reduction in HIV infection, a 71.6% reduction in AIDS, and a 30.5% reduction in tuberculosis. The incidence of acute viral hepatitis A, B, and C decreased by 62.9%, 64.7%, and 26.2%, respectively, whereas the incidence of chronic viral hepatitis B and C increased by 3.3% and 29.6%, respectively. Among other infections, the largest decreases were observed for rubella (−95.7%), pediculosis and phthiriasis (−86.4%), gonococcal infection (−91.5%), and pertussis (−62.6%). At the same time, measles incidence increased 15.3-fold, Lyme disease incidence increased 2.6-fold, and tetanus incidence increased by 20.0%. Regional analysis revealed substantial disparities in the incidence of HIV infection and tuberculosis. The highest rates were observed in Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions, while the lowest rates were recorded in western regions, with differences reaching 9- to 12-fold. These trends correspond to challenges faced by the WHO European Region, where a substantial burden of tuberculosis and HIV infection persists and measles outbreaks continue to occur amid declining routine immunization coverage.Conclusions. Thus, analysis of the ten-year dynamics demonstrates multidirectional changes in infectious morbidity in Ukraine. Alongside a sustained decrease in the incidence of a number of socially significant and vaccine-preventable infections, an increase was observed in the incidence of certain diseases, particularly measles, Lyme disease, and chronic viral hepatitis. This highlights the need for a differentiated approach to assessing the epidemiological situation and for further improvement of epidemiological surveillance, prevention, early detection, and control of infectious diseases, as well as effective outbreak forecasting.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Direct-Acting Antivirals in Mexican Patients with Chronic Hepatitis C: A Multicenter Study by Cirrhosis Status
abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major global health burden, potentially leading to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) have improved treatment outcomes, achieving high sustained virologic response (SVR) rates. However, real-world evidence from Mexico remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate DAA effectiveness in Mexican patients with chronic HCV infection and compare outcomes according to cirrhosis status. A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted across five public healthcare institutions in Mexico. We included 253 patients who received DAA therapy. The primary outcome was SVR, defined as undetectable HCV RNA after treatment. Clinical, demographic, and treatment-related variables were analyzed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Overall, SVR was achieved in 94.5% of patients. Among those with cirrhosis (54.1%), the SVR rate was 95.6%, compared with 93.1% among those without cirrhosis (p = 0.536). Patients with cirrhosis were older and had longer treatment durations, while baseline viral load and genotype distribution were comparable. Treatment completion was high (94.1%), with low discontinuation rates and no significant differences by cirrhosis status. DAAs were highly effective in Mexican patients with chronic HCV infection, regardless of cirrhosis status. Expanding access to diagnosis and treatment is essential to reduce disease burden and achieve hepatitis C elimination goals.

title: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein enhances HBV replication via autophagy and aggravates inflammation in CHB patients with liver dysfunction
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the effects of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein (S protein) on hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication and immune function in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), aiming to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of S protein–HBV interaction. Through in vitro cell experiments and clinical sample analyses, S protein expression was induced in HepG2.2.15 cells, leading to enhanced HBV replication; this effect was reduced by autophagy inhibitors, confirming the critical mediating role of autophagy. Furthermore, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from CHB patients were co-cultured with the S protein, resulting in increased inflammatory responses in T cells and monocytes, particularly in patients with concurrent abnormal liver function and lipid metabolism disorders. In summary, the S protein promotes HBV replication by activating autophagy and exacerbates immune inflammation in CHB patients. Autophagy inhibitors block its effect on HBV replication, suggesting autophagy as a key regulatory target. The immune-activating effects of the S protein are more pronounced in patients with liver dysfunction and metabolic abnormalities. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into the interplay between the S protein and autophagy in HBV infection. IMPORTANCE This study reveals that the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein promotes hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication by activating the autophagy pathway and elucidates its role in exacerbating immune inflammation in patients with chronic hepatitis B, particularly showing more pronounced responses in patients with liver dysfunction and lipid metabolism disorders. These findings provide critical molecular insights into the viral interaction and immunopathological mechanisms during SARS-CoV-2 and HBV co-infection. They also improve our understanding of the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 and HBV in the context of co-infection and provide a basis for future studies.

title: The aMAP Score Effectively Stratifies Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk in the Steatotic Liver Disease Population
abstract: ABSTRACT Background & Aims Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is an increasingly important cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet validated risk stratification tools remain limited. We aim to evaluate the aMAP score, initially developed for HCC risk prediction mainly in viral hepatitis across international cohorts, in the SLD population. Methods 156 406 SLD participants were included from the UK Biobank (UKB) and 3166 SLD patients with virally suppressed chronic hepatitis B from a Chinese cohort. title: Crowder-specific modulation of hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease activity and local structural dynamics.
abstract: Macromolecular crowding modulates enzyme behavior in crowder- and protein-specific ways, yet its impact on viral proteases, which are often key therapeutic targets, remains unclear. Here, we investigated the hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease under increasing concentrations of polyethylene glycols (PEGs), ficoll, dextran, and lysozyme using fluorescence-based assays to examine enzyme kinetics, local Trp environments, thermal stability, and rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe in the surrounding medium. PEGs reduced catalytic activity while leaving substrate binding either unaffected or slightly enhanced. These effects were accompanied by a moderate tryptophan fluorescence spectral narrowing, consistent with reduced heterogeneity in local conformational environments. In contrast, ficoll enhanced catalytic efficiency despite stronger fluorescence quenching, indicating local structural changes that favored catalysis. Dextran and lysozyme inhibited protease activity through distinct kinetic patterns, likely reflecting differences in their size, shape, and chemical properties. Thermal analysis revealed crowder-specific local structural changes in NS3/4A without global unfolding up to 65°C, with differences in local stability and flexibility corroborating the observed kinetic effects. Changes in the rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe further indicated that generalized restriction of molecular motion alone could not explain the effects of crowding on NS3/4A. These findings demonstrate that macromolecular crowding modulates NS3/4A catalysis through crowder-specific effects on local structure.

title: Timing of Earliest Documented Positive Hepatitis C Laboratory Result Relative to Delivery Among Pregnant Persons With Active Infection in West Virginia, 2022-2023.
abstract: Direct-acting antiviral therapy can cure hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection; however, because treatment is not recommended during pregnancy, preconception treatment remains the primary strategy to prevent perinatal HCV exposure. West Virginia birth records from 2022 to 2023 were linked with statewide HCV laboratory surveillance data. This linked dataset was used to identify births to persons with active HCV infection and characterize the timing of the earliest documented positive HCV laboratory result relative to delivery. A total of 426 deliveries resulting in 433 HCV-exposed live-born infants were identified. Most pregnant persons were aged 25-34 years, White and insured by Medicaid. Overall, 38.5% had their earliest documented positive HCV laboratory result more than 5 years prior to delivery, 36.9% had their first documented positive test 1-5 years prior to delivery and 24.6% had their first documented positive test within 1 year before delivery and up to 2 weeks postpartum. These findings indicate that many pregnant persons with active HCV infection had documented longstanding infection prior to pregnancy, highlighting opportunities to strengthen linkage to care and access to curative treatment before pregnancy.
