title: Direct-Acting Antiviral Therapy in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma Receiving Non-Curative Treatment: High Sustained Virological Response Rates and Preservation of Liver Functional Reserve.
abstract: Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) cure most chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, but their impact on liver functional reserve in patients with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly after non-curative HCC treatment, remains unclear. We evaluated antiviral efficacy and liver functional reserve after DAA therapy according to HCC history and timing of DAA initiation. In this retrospective single-center cohort, 716 patients initiated DAA therapy, and 690 with evaluable sustained virological response at 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12) were analysed. Patients were classified as no HCC, curative-treated HCC, or non-curative-treated HCC according to the most recent HCC treatment before DAA initiation. Liver functional reserve was assessed using the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score, modified ALBI grade, and Child-Pugh class. In the non-curative-treated HCC group, early (≤ 3 months) versus delayed (> 3 months) DAA initiation after the most recent HCC treatment was compared. Overall SVR12 was 96.1%, with similarly high rates across groups regardless of HCC history. The median ALBI score improved from -2.35 to -2.58 at SVR12 in the curative-treated HCC group (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged in the non-curative-treated HCC group (-2.36 to -2.38). Among 64 patients with a history of HCC, 43 (67.2%) developed recurrence; in these patients, the ALBI score improved from -2.31 at DAA initiation to -2.57 at recurrence (p < 0.001), and more than 90% remained Child-Pugh class A. Early and delayed DAA initiation showed similarly high SVR12 rates and comparable liver functional reserve. DAAs achieved high SVR12 rates and maintained liver functional reserve in patients with HCV, including those with a history of HCC after non-curative treatment.

title: Case Report: Rapidly fatal hepatic portal venous gas following transarterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatic portal venous gas (HPVG) is an uncommon radiological sign whose clinical importance depends on the underlying disorder and the patient’s physiological state. Only two cases of HPVG following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) have been reported. We describe a rapidly fatal episode in a 71-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and biopsy-confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma. Selective TACE involved lobaplatin infusion, followed by 10 mL of an iodized oil-raltitrexed emulsion and 1 mL of epirubicin-loaded drug-eluting microspheres. Constipation and abdominal distension developed approximately 21 h after TACE. Severe abdominal pain and vomiting followed at 37 h. Emergency CT at approximately 38 h showed peripheral branching HPVG, bowel dilatation, and intraluminal fluid. At approximately 39 h, the patient developed impaired consciousness, hypotension, and bradycardia. He died despite resuscitative treatment approximately 40 h after TACE. Lactate, a repeat leukocyte count, blood cultures, and other microbiological samples were not obtained after the acute deterioration. Sepsis therefore remained an unconfirmed possible mechanism. The combined embolization regimen represents a procedural exposure, not a proven cause. Progressive abdominal symptoms after TACE should prompt urgent evaluation for bowel injury, infection, biliary complications, and circulatory deterioration.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of HCV Screening in Emergency Departments Using DETECT Hep C Trial Results.
abstract: Importance Nontargeted hepatitis C virus (HCV) screening in emergency departments (EDs) has been demonstrated to identify more patients with HCV than targeted screening. Cost-effectiveness is key to strategy selection; however, the cost-effectiveness of these strategies in EDs remains unknown. Objective To compare clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness of 2 novel ED-based HCV screening strategies with no ED HCV screening. Design, setting, and participants In this economic evaluation study, a cohort of individuals presenting to the ED in the US was simulated with data from the Determining Effective Testing in Emergency Departments and Care Coordination on Treatment Outcomes for Hepatitis C Screening (DETECT Hep C) trial using the Hepatitis C Cost-Effectiveness (HEP-CE) model from a health sector perspective. Using data from EDs at Denver Health Medical Center, Johns Hopkins Hospital, and the University of Mississippi Medical Center, 3 strategies were simulated over a lifetime horizon, including (1) no ED HCV screening, (2) targeted HCV screening, and (3) nontargeted HCV screening. Data were collected from November 2019 to August 2022 and analyzed from December 2021 to July 2026. Exposure HCV screening in the ED. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcomes were remaining life expectancy, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), and costs (2024 US dollars). An annual discount rate of 3% was applied to future costs and benefits when calculating ICERs. An ICER of less than $100 000 per QALY gained was considered cost-effective. Results A simulated cohort with a total of 500 million individuals (mean [SD] age, 46.3 [17.2] years; 264.4 million male [52.88%]) were included in this analysis. title: Cognitive–Affective Dimension After Virological Cure of Hepatitis C Virus Infection: WBSI Dynamics, Liver Status, and the Role of Comorbidities
abstract: Introduction: Virological cure in chronic infection with hepatitis C virus (HCV) is followed by important clinical and biological benefits, including psychological ones. The White Bear Suppression Inventory (WBSI) assesses the tendency to suppress intrusive thoughts and was used in this study as a tool to provide a cognitive–affective assessment of patients with chronic HCV infection—both at the start of antiviral therapy and five years after achieving virological cure. Objective: This study aimed to characterize patients with HCV infection who received antiviral therapy and completed the WBSI, to assess longitudinal changes in WBSI scores, and to identify clinical, biological, and comorbidity-related factors associated with these changes. Methods: The study employed an ambispective observational longitudinal cohort study design conducted on a sample of 386 patients, of whom 81 completed the WBSI both at baseline and at follow-up. Results: The WBSI subsample did not differ significantly from the remainder of the cohort in terms of age, cytolysis markers, bilirubin, albumin, platelet count, or major comorbidities. The WBSI score decreased significantly from baseline to follow-up, from 61.36 to 54.16, with a mean difference of 7.20 points (t = 6.32; p < 0.001). The correlation between the baseline and follow-up scores was very strong (r = 0.899; p < 0.001), indicating substantial interindividual stability. ΔWBSI was weakly but significantly correlated with the change in total bilirubin (r = 0.254; p = 0.022), with no significant correlations with the other biological markers. In the multivariable model, cardiovascular comorbidities (B = −8.469; p < 0.001) and metabolic comorbidities (B = −9.869; p = 0.002) were independent negative predictors of WBSI scoring, whereas fibrosis evolution, age, sex, and baseline total bilirubin had no significant influence. Conclusions: Improvements in WBSI scores observed only in specific patient subgroups, one year after achieving HCV virological cure, underscore the need to integrate psychological assessment into long-term monitoring, particularly for patients with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities.

title: Implementation and Assessment of an Electronic Health Record Alert Preventing Misleading Serology Test Results in Patients Recently Treated with Intravenous Immunoglobulin
abstract: To the Editor: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is concentrated immunoglobulin from human donors. It is FDA-approved for a large number of conditions, including primary immunodeficiency disease, immune thrombocytopenic purpura, dermatomyositis, and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (1). The literature has shown that patients with exposure to IVIG can demonstrate false positivity in various serology tests (2–5). We have previously published findings supporting a false positivity rate of 1.4% in serum protein electrophoresis tests with recent IVIG usage (5). As a result, at The Johns Hopkins Hospital, we implemented an OurPractice Advisory (OPA) in the Epic electronic health record to alert clinicians when ordering selected serum tests where evidence has supported that results could be compromised by recent IVIG exposure (2–5). The alert triggers when a test is ordered in a patient who was treated with IVIG within 30 days (in concordance with the average half-life of IVIG preparations), and the alert provides background information and offers options for test acknowledgment/continuation or for cancellation. The tests included in the alert, based on a literature review, are direct antiglobulin tests, Treponema palladium antibodies, hepatitis B surface and core antibodies, and serum protein electrophoresis tests, although it is acknowledged that this list is not exhaustive. Approximately 1 year postimplementation, we analyzed the number of alert triggers and test cancellations (aka “remove orders”). Twenty-nine of 332 tests were canceled, giving a cancellation rate at the time of alert of 8.7%. We further investigated the 50 most recent alert triggers through a manual review, which showed a cancellation rate of 26% (13/50 tests) (Fig. Investigation into the differences in these results revealed that if clinicians canceled the test order through alternative means during the alert process (such as terminating the entire prompt, navigating out of Epic, etc.) without hitting the “remove order” button on the alert prompt, the order would be removed and traceable during manual review; however, the electronic health record system would not identify this as a test cancellation. Further investigation of the 37/50 ordered tests found that 8 tests were subsequently canceled post-OPA but prior to laboratory analysis, leading to a cancellation rate of 21/50 (42%). IVIG alert analysis. Bar graph depicts tests canceled at the alert (orange) vs ordered (gray) after longitudinal review of approximately 1 year in duration (n = 332). An in-depth review of the last 50 alerts assessed tests canceled after the alert was triggered (post-alert). A breakdown of the ordered tests (29 total) revealed a false positivity rate of 10% (3/29). Of the 29 tests that were completed, 8 tests produced negative results, and 21 produced positive findings (Fig. Due to the interfering nature of recent IVIG exposure, the validity of these positive results was investigated by reviewing the medical history, clinical context, patient workup, and other laboratory findings and conclusions from the managing clinical team. Any completed tests not meeting these criteria were labeled as clinically discordant, potentially due to IVIG-related serologic interference, with 3/29 (10%) completed tests identified. The specifics are as follows: Direct antiglobulin testing to clarify the etiology of hemolytic anemia. The direct antiglobulin test was positive for IgG and negative for C3, and IVIG-induced hemolysis was suspected given the clinical context/recent exposure and subsequent eluate showing anti-A antibodies in a patient with blood type A positive. A suspected false-positive hepatitis B core antibody test (IgG and IgM) in a patient who was negative for hepatitis B surface antigen and positive for surface antibody. The patient was previously vaccinated and had prior hepatitis B core IgM testing 15 days prior (and before IVIG), which was negative. A suspected false-positive hepatitis B core antibody test (IgG and IgM) in a patient who was previously vaccinated and had positive hepatitis B surface antibody and negative antigen. There was no follow-up with the primary team for interpretation of these findings. Together, these data support the findings that recent IVIG usage affects certain serum tests, leading to clinically discordant results and a finding that an electronic health record alert is an effective method to reduce the number of orders for which results could be compromised (a test cancellation rate of up to 41% in the most recent 50 tests). Additionally, our analysis also highlighted another benefit of the OPA, which raises awareness of the potential interference leading to a substantial proportion of late test cancellations (16%) after the initial alert. We suspect that after awareness of the issue and discussion by the clinical team, the risks of clinical decisions being made from potentially compromised serology results prompted test cancellation. This analysis supports the finding that an alert influences decisions at the time of the alert, affects downstream clinical decisions, and raises awareness within the clinical team. This underscores the importance of evaluating the impact of an alert both at the initial alert stage and afterward to accurately determine its efficacy. title: Host receptor networking and molecular mechanisms of innate immune evasion in hepatitis E virus pathogenesis
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV), the causative agent of hepatitis E, is a major global health concern, with seroprevalence estimates suggesting that approximately 939 million people worldwide have been exposed to the virus. Although historically regarded as a predominantly self-limiting cause of acute hepatitis, HEV is now recognized as a clinically diverse pathogen capable of causing acute liver failure, chronic hepatitis in immunocompromised individuals, and neurological, renal, hematological, and other extrahepatic manifestations. This review integrates current understanding of HEV cell entry, tissue and host tropism, innate immune recognition, and viral immune evasion. HEV exists in two particle forms: non-enveloped (nHEV) and quasi-enveloped (eHEV). Both use distinct but partially convergent entry pathways involving attachment factors, entry cofactors, endosomal trafficking machinery, and lysosomal processing rather than a single canonical receptor. We evaluate the evidence supporting established and candidate host factors and propose a dual-module heuristic to organize current receptor evidence while emphasizing that this framework remains provisional and requires validation in physiologically relevant models. We further examine how viral genetic determinants, receptor engagement, post-entry replication compatibility, and host antiviral responses collectively shape tissue tropism and cross-species transmission. Innate recognition involves RIG-I and MDA5 signaling through MAVS–TBK1–IRF3, alongside TLR pathways converging on IRF3 and NF-κB, driving type I and III interferon responses. HEV, however, counteracts these defenses at multiple levels. Functional regions within ORF1 interfere with pathogen sensing and interferon signaling; ORF2 contributes to immune evasion through a secreted glycosylated decoy isoform and modulation of NF-κB signaling; and ORF3 exerts context-dependent immunomodulatory effects while facilitating quasi-enveloped virion egress through the ESCRT pathway. Together, these mechanisms support a model in which HEV induces a sustained but incompletely effective antiviral response that may permit viral persistence, particularly under immunosuppression. Integrating entry biology with tropism, zoonotic determinants, and innate immune evasion highlights key unresolved mechanisms and provides a framework for developing improved experimental models, antiviral strategies, and diagnostic approaches for hepatitis E.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of Dolutegravir/Rilpivirine in Japanese People Living with HIV: Final Report of 6-Year Post-marketing Surveillance Study
abstract: Previous phase 3 studies demonstrated that a two-drug combination of dolutegravir (DTG) and rilpivirine (RPV) was non-inferior to three-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) with stable plasma HIV-1 RNA. In Japan, DTG/RPV was approved in 2018 for maintenance of HIV-1 suppression, but evidence on its long-term safety and effectiveness is limited. In this post-marketing surveillance, data on the real-world clinical use of DTG/RPV were obtained through the HIV-Related Drug Cooperative Survey, a national joint post-marketing program overseen by manufacturers of HIV medications in Japan. The data collection period was from November 26, 2018 to November 26, 2024. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and potential risk factors associated with their incidence were examined. Effectiveness was evaluated by longitudinal changes in plasma HIV RNA levels and peripheral CD4+ T cell counts. Forty-four participants were registered, of whom 43 were assessed for safety and 41 for effectiveness. Safety analyses included 39 men and 4 women, with a mean age of 53.3 years. All participants switched from other ART regimens. DTG/RPV treatment exceeded 2 years in 76.74% of participants. Four ADRs, all non-serious, occurred in three participants (6.98%): weight increased (n = 1), hypertension (n = 1), hyperuricemia (n = 1), and condition aggravated (n = 1, aggravated hyperuricemia in the participant with hyperuricemia). The incidence of ADRs differed by the following participant characteristics: treatment duration, hepatic disorder, and renal disorder. Plasma HIV RNA levels remained < 50 copies/mL for 3 years after switching to DTG/RPV in most participants. The mean (standard deviation) peripheral CD4+ T cell count was 563.3 (207.2) cells/mm3, which remained stable throughout 3 years. This 6-year post-marketing surveillance confirms the long-term safety and effectiveness of DTG/RPV in people living with HIV in Japan who were virologically suppressed and switched to this two-drug regimen. Previous clinical studies demonstrated that a two-drug combination of dolutegravir and rilpivirine was non-inferior to three-drug antiretroviral therapy regimens in people living with HIV (PLHIV) whose plasma HIV RNA levels were under control. Data on the long-term safety and effectiveness of dolutegravir/rilpivirine in Japan are limited. In this 6-year post-marketing surveillance (November 2018 to November 2024), we collected data on the clinical use of dolutegravir/rilpivirine through a national joint post-marketing program overseen by manufacturers of HIV medications in Japan. We assessed the safety of dolutegravir/rilpivirine by the occurrence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs), and its effectiveness by changes over time in plasma HIV RNA levels and peripheral CD4+ T cell counts after switching from prior antiretroviral therapy regimens to dolutegravir/rilpivirine. Of 43 participants assessed for safety, 42 were Japanese (97.67%), 39 were men (90.70%), and the mean age was 53.3 years. All participants switched from other antiretroviral therapy regimens. Four non-serious ADRs (weight gain, hypertension, hyperuricemia, and aggravated condition) occurred in three participants (6.98%). None of the participants had events related to hepatitis B virus infection or reactivation. Among 41 participants assessed for effectiveness, most participants maintained suppressed HIV RNA levels and stable CD4+ T cell counts for 3 years after switching to dolutegravir/rilpivirine. Our findings suggest that dolutegravir/rilpivirine is a safe and effective two-drug combination for PLHIV in Japan whose plasma HIV RNA levels are under control and who consider switching treatment.

Forty-four participants were registered, of whom 43 were assessed for safety and 41 for effectiveness. Safety analyses included 39 men and 4 women, with a mean age of 53.3 years. In this 6-year post-marketing surveillance (November 2018 to November 2024), we collected data on the clinical use of dolutegravir/rilpivirine through a national joint post-marketing program overseen by manufacturers of HIV medications in Japan. We assessed the safety of dolutegravir/rilpivirine by the occurrence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs), and its effectiveness by changes over time in plasma HIV RNA levels and peripheral CD4+ T cell counts after switching from prior antiretroviral therapy regimens to dolutegravir/rilpivirine. Of 43 participants assessed for safety, 42 were Japanese (97.67%), 39 were men (90.70%), and the mean age was 53.3 years. All participants switched from other antiretroviral therapy regimens. None of the participants had events related to hepatitis B virus infection or reactivation. Among 41 participants assessed for effectiveness, most participants maintained suppressed HIV RNA levels and stable CD4+ T cell counts for 3 years after switching to dolutegravir/rilpivirine. Our findings suggest that dolutegravir/rilpivirine is a safe and effective two-drug combination for PLHIV in Japan whose plasma HIV RNA levels are under control and who consider switching treatment.

title: Sustained Virological Response of Hepatitis C with Immunotherapy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: a case report
abstract: Introduction: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is a blood borne virus that will progress to a chronic state in 55-85% of cases. Though direct acting antivirals (DAA) offers an effective cure, HCV remains underdiagnosed and the development of complications of cirrhosis including HCC may be the only clinical clue prompting diagnosis. Achieving sustained virological response (SVR) with direct acting antivirals (DAA) is a therapeutic imperative even in advanced HCC to prevent decompensation and to reduce tumor recurrence. However, drug interactions, suboptimal response in HCC, and risk of provoking decompensation in cirrhosis are important considerations in initiating treatment. We present the novel case of SVR with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in a treatment naïve host. M is a 53-year-old male with alcohol use disorder, and remote intravenous drug use, presented with severe abdominal pain, acute anemia (hemoglobin 7.6g/dL), hypotension (systolic BP 94mmHg). CT imaging revealed cirrhotic morphology and an 8cm liver lesion with tumor thrombosis and hemoperitoneum consistent tumor rupture. His Childs Pugh Score was B-9. Liver biopsy confirmed mixed biphenotypic HCC/Cholangiocarcinoma. Etiological screen returned positive for HCV (antibody positive, RNA 20,500 IU/mL, genotype I). Treatment was deferred due to ‘advanced malignancy’. He started systemic therapy as tremelimumab and durvalumab, achieving significant tumor response. His HCV titer climbed to 895,000 IU/mL 5 months after starting treatment before declining and remaining persistently undetectable even after completion of immunotherapy. Subsequent disease progression was managed with TACE and SBRT. Systemic therapy was complicated by grade II ICI-hepatitis responsive to prednisone. Discussion: This case shows immune checkpoint inhibition can reverse immune tolerance of chronic HCV and can achieve SVR without DAAs. ICI is the backbone of systemic therapy for HCC and enhance anti-tumor immunity by promoting T-cell regulatory cell depletion and reversal of T-cell exhaustion. Only one other case of HCV clearance with ICI is published but this is the first in the absence of DAA therapy. This finding suggests that ICI may restore anti-viral immunity in chronic infections and has implications for treatment decisions for HCV.

title: Virus-specific T cells and neutralizing antibodies are independent correlates of long-term protective immunity against hepatitis C virus
abstract: ABSTRACT Virus-specific T cells and broadly neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) are associated with spontaneous clearance of acute primary hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and reinfection. Following spontaneous clearance, HCV-specific memory T cells are long-lived, but NAbs are less durable. How these two arms contribute to long-term protective immunity upon re-exposure is unknown. Herein, we compared the magnitude and breadth of memory HCV-specific T cells and NAbs in a cohort of HCV-spontaneously resolved people who inject drugs with high-risk exposure to the virus but who remained free of observed reinfections (FOR, n = 34) or who got reinfected ( n = 22). Among FOR, 73.5% ( n = 25) exhibited high frequencies of gamma interferon (IFN-γ)-producing T cells, while 23.5% ( n = 8) showed high neutralization breadth (>25% neutralization of HCV pseudoparticles [HCVpp]) and/or potency (geometric mean neutralization >50% against seven HCVpp). Notably, some subjects had detectable NAbs several years after clearance. Multivariate random forest analysis demonstrated that the frequency of IFN-γ-producing T cells and the NAb response against only one difficult-to-neutralize HCVpp (1b58) were significant predictors of protection against reinfection ( P IMPORTANCE Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a blood-borne virus that disproportionately affects people who inject drugs. Most HCV infections become persistent, leading to liver fibrosis and cancer. Although effective antiviral therapies are available, around 50 million people remain persistently infected with HCV and can transmit the virus. Currently, there is no available vaccine to control the spread of HCV. However, around one in four people infected can naturally clear the virus, becoming partially protected upon re-exposure, suggesting it is possible to develop a vaccine that induces similar protection. In this study, we investigated the contribution of T cells and neutralizing antibodies to protection against observed reinfection in a cohort of people who inject drugs and have naturally cleared HCV, yet remain at high-risk exposure. Our findings suggest that strong T cell responses and neutralizing antibodies targeting hard-to-neutralize isolates could predict protective immunity upon reinfection.

title: Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

title: The birth of the European Liver transplant registry
abstract: This personal account, written on the occasion of the fortieth anniversary of the European Liver Transplant Registry (ELTR), traces the origins of the Registry from the earliest days of liver transplantation in Europe to its present scale. Beginning with a handful of pioneering centres in the 1970s and the scepticism that surrounded the procedure, the narrative follows the events of 1983 that transformed the field, the creation of an informal registry at Paul Brousse, and its extension to a European network following a founding meeting in Hannover in October 1985. It describes the early design choices that shaped the Registry, the methodological debates that defined its core definitions, and the scientific contributions that followed, including landmark findings on patient survival and on hepatitis B recurrence after transplantation, as well as the 1993 Paris Consensus Conference on indications for liver transplantation. The account closes with the Registry’s transition to new stewardship and its present scope, spanning more than 200,000 transplants recorded across 32 countries. The history illustrates how informal, trust-based collaboration among a small number of European surgeons gave rise to one of the longest-running transplant registries in the world.

title: Transcriptome Analysis of Hepatitis C Virus-Infected Hepatoma Cells Following Stringent Removal of Genomic DNA
abstract: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is a positive strand RNA virus that infects hepatocytes and reprograms cellular gene expression, contributing to chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma. HCV replicates slowly and induces limited changes in the cellular transcriptome. Here, we improved analysis of low-abundance transcripts, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), in the context of HCV replication. We stringently removed genomic DNA from total RNA from Huh-7 hepatoma cell lines by a combination of TRIzol, acidic phenol, silica matrix columns and recombinant DNase I. RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and targeted validation were used to characterize Lnc-ITM2C-1 splice variants and expression of its neighboring gene, G protein-coupled receptor 55 (GPR55), to investigate their potential roles in HCV replication. Challenging our previous findings, under our improved experimental conditions, Lnc-ITM2C-1 and GPR55 were neither involved in a positive regulation circuit with HCV nor induced detectable transcriptome changes. Secondary analysis of RNA-Seq data according to HCV infection status revealed statistically robust HCV-induced expression of 21 host cell genes involved in pathways like stress response (in particular ATF3), lipid metabolism, cytoskeleton organization and growth regulation. In contrast, we found that expression changed for only a limited subset of previously reported HCV-associated lncRNAs (e.g., EGOT). This highlights the necessity of stringent gDNA removal for analysis of low-abundance transcripts like lncRNAs.

title: Preliminary evidence that non-fasting serum asprosin differs by sex but not by fibrosis stage in chronic hepatitis C
abstract: Abstract Background Asprosin is an adipokine increased in diabetes and fatty liver disease, two metabolic comorbidities frequently present in chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. Moreover, low serum asprosin levels were found in cirrhosis. However, its association with liver fibrosis stages in chronic HCV remains unclear. This study examined whether serum asprosin reflects liver disease severity in patients with chronic HCV. Methods Serum asprosin levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay before direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy, during treatment, and at sustained virological response 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12). Associations with liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, body mass index, sex, diabetes, hepatic steatosis, HCV viral load, genotype, and circulating lipids were analyzed. Results Higher serum asprosin in obese men, but not in obese women, was observed in chronic HCV. After exclusion of obese patients, women had higher serum asprosin levels than men. Serum asprosin did not differ in patients with or without diabetes and/or hepatic steatosis, irrespective of obesity status. It was not associated with liver fibrosis assessed by shear-wave elastography or fibrosis-4 score. Patients with ultrasound-defined cirrhosis had serum asprosin levels comparable to those without cirrhosis. Serum asprosin was also unrelated to liver function markers, the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score, HCV viral load, or genotype. DAA therapy did not alter serum asprosin levels, which were 1.38 (0.32–4.61) ng/ml before therapy, 1.30 (0.16–2.27) ng/ml at 12 weeks of therapy, and 1.32 (0.40–3.75) ng/ml at SVR12. Females had modestly higher serum asprosin levels than males at therapy end and SVR12. Serum asprosin correlated positively with phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine before and after therapy. Conclusions Serum asprosin levels in chronic HCV show sex-specific differences. In contrast, it does not reflect metabolic comorbidities, liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, or virological features and remains stable during DAA therapy. Its positive relationship with circulating phospholipids before and after treatment suggests a role in lipid metabolism that merits further study.

Moreover, low serum asprosin levels were found in cirrhosis. However, its association with liver fibrosis stages in chronic HCV remains unclear. This study examined whether serum asprosin reflects liver disease severity in patients with chronic HCV. Methods Serum asprosin levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay before direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy, during treatment, and at sustained virological response 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12). Associations with liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, body mass index, sex, diabetes, hepatic steatosis, HCV viral load, genotype, and circulating lipids were analyzed. Results Higher serum asprosin in obese men, but not in obese women, was observed in chronic HCV. After exclusion of obese patients, women had higher serum asprosin levels than men. Serum asprosin did not differ in patients with or without diabetes and/or hepatic steatosis, irrespective of obesity status. It was not associated with liver fibrosis assessed by shear-wave elastography or fibrosis-4 score. Patients with ultrasound-defined cirrhosis had serum asprosin levels comparable to those without cirrhosis. Serum asprosin was also unrelated to liver function markers, the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score, HCV viral load, or genotype. DAA therapy did not alter serum asprosin levels, which were 1.38 (0.32–4.61) ng/ml before therapy, 1.30 (0.16–2.27) ng/ml at 12 weeks of therapy, and 1.32 (0.40–3.75) ng/ml at SVR12. Females had modestly higher serum asprosin levels than males at therapy end and SVR12. Serum asprosin correlated positively with phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine before and after therapy. Conclusions Serum asprosin levels in chronic HCV show sex-specific differences. In contrast, it does not reflect metabolic comorbidities, liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, or virological features and remains stable during DAA therapy. Its positive relationship with circulating phospholipids before and after treatment suggests a role in lipid metabolism that merits further study.

title: Off-Label Use of Monoclonal Antibodies in Developing Countries
abstract: Rituximab is used in different hematologic, rheumatic, neurologic, and renal disorders. As the clinical applications of this agent continue to expand, its use, including off-label use, requires careful and consistent evaluation. Off-label use should not be considered inappropriate by default, as it may be supported by clinical evidence or current authoritative guidelines. To what extent does rituximab prescribing conform to established clinical guidelines and approved indications, and what deficiencies exist in the implementation of prescribing criteria and pretreatment safety assessments? A prospective observational evaluation of rituximab utilization was conducted at a tertiary academic hospital in Tehran, Iran, over a 6-month period from April to October, 2023. We collected data on patients who received rituximab, including demographic characteristics, clinical indications, classification of use as on-label, off-label, or outside the applicable protocol, adherence to relevant prescribing criteria, and documentation of pretreatment screening for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus (human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)), HIV, and tuberculosis. Among the 171 patients who received rituximab, the mean age was 45.3 years, and 66.7% were female. Approximately 40 distinct indications were identified. The most common indications were granulomatosis with polyangiitis (22 patients, 12.9%), rheumatoid arthritis (21, 12.3%), multiple sclerosis (20, 11.7%), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (19, 11.1%), and lupus nephritis (9, 5.3%). Overall, 37.4% of rituximab uses were classified as on-label, 58.5% as off-label, and 4.1% as outside the applicable protocol. Conclusions: Rituximab was widely used in clinical practice; however, its implementation protocols and safety-monitoring practices varied considerably. In light of these findings, it is important to distinguish between off-label use and inappropriate use, and to ensure that treatment decisions are evaluated against current evidence, clinical guidelines, and indication-specific criteria.

title: Geographic representation of phase 2–4 trials in eight gastrointestinal and liver diseases relative to global disease burden: a cross-sectional meta-research study
abstract: This cross-sectional meta-research study examines whether the geographic distribution of interventional phase 2–4 trials in gastroenterology and hepatology matches where the disease burden lies. Using ClinicalTrials.gov (2000–2025) and Global Burden of Disease 2023 data, it covers eight conditions: hepatitis B, hepatitis C, MASLD/MASH, liver cancer, cirrhosis, inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer and stomach cancer. For each region (with Egypt as its own unit), a representation index is calculated as the region's share of trial-country pairs divided by its share of global DALYs, with bootstrap confidence intervals. Secondary analyses cover time periods, sponsor type, phase, inequality measures and sensitivity analyses. We expect sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia and the Middle East and North Africa to be underrepresented relative to burden, and North America, Europe and East Asia to be overrepresented.

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title: Hubungan Dukungan Keluarga Terhadap Pemberian Vaksin DPT-HB-Hib Di Wilayah Kerja Puskesmas Pengaron
abstract: Vaksin DPT-HB-Hib merupakan salah satu imunisasi dasar yang berperan penting dalam melindungi bayi dari penyakit difteri, pertusis, tetanus, hepatitis B, dan infeksi Haemophilus influenzae tipe b. Berdasarkan data periode Januari–Mei 2026 dengan jumlah sasaran 280 bayi, rata-rata cakupan hanya 14,3% untuk DPT-HB-Hib1, 11,4% untuk DPT-HB-Hib2, dan 8,9% untuk DPT-HB-Hib3, serta masih terdapat desa dengan cakupan 0%. Salah satu faktor yang diduga memengaruhi kelengkapan pemberian vaksin adalah dukungan keluarga. Tujuan penelitian enganalisis hubungan antara dukungan keluarga dengan pemberian vaksin DPT-HB-Hib pada anak di wilayah kerja UPTD Puskesmas Pengaron Tahun 2026. Metode Penelitian ini menggunakan desain kuantitatif dengan pendekatan cross-sectional. Populasi penelitian adalah ibu yang memiliki anak usia 2 tahun – 5 tahun di wilayah kerja UPTD Puskesmas Pengaron dengan jumlah sampel sebanyak 61 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik Purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner dukungan keluarga, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji Chi-Square. Dari 27 orang yang mendapat dukungan keuarga, terdapat 85% yang mendapatkan imunisasi lengkap dan dari 34 responden yang tidak mendapat dukungan, terdapat 82,3% yang tidak lengkap imunisasi. Hasil uji Chi-Square menunjukkan nilai ρ value = 0,001 (p < 0,05), yang berarti terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara dukungan keluarga dengan pemberian vaksin DPT-HB-Hib pada bayi. Terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara dukungan keluarga dengan pemberian vaksin DPT-HB-Hib pada anak di wilayah kerja UPTD Puskesmas Pengaron Tahun 2026. Semakin baik dukungan keluarga, semakin tinggi kemungkinan bayi memperoleh vaksin DPT-HB-Hib secara lengkap. Diperlukan upaya inovatif untuk meningkatkan dukungan keluarga dalam melengkapi imunisasi dasar bayi sesuai jadwal.

title: Associations Of Husbands’ Support, Maternal Knowledge, And Culture With Neonatal Immunization Completeness
abstract: Latar Belakang: Kelengkapan imunisasi Hepatitis B dosis lahir (HB-0), BCG, dan Polio 1 pada neonatus masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat karena cakupannya belum mencapai target nasional. Di Puskesmas Padang Cermin, cakupan HB-0 sebesar 52,1%, sedangkan BCG dan Polio 1 sebesar 65,5%. Faktor keluarga dan sosial budaya, termasuk dukungan suami, pengetahuan ibu, dan budaya, dapat berkaitan dengan kelengkapan imunisasi neonatus.Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan dukungan suami, pengetahuan ibu, dan budaya dengan kelengkapan imunisasi HB-0, BCG, dan Polio 1 pada neonatus di Wilayah Kerja Puskesmas Padang Cermin Kabupaten Pesawaran Tahun 2026.Metode: Penelitian kuantitatif analitik dengan pendekatan cross-sectional melibatkan 73 ibu yang memiliki neonatus dan seluruhnya diikutsertakan melalui total sampling. Data dukungan suami, pengetahuan ibu, dan budaya dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner terstruktur. Status imunisasi diverifikasi melalui Buku KIA dan/atau register imunisasi Puskesmas berdasarkan tanggal lahir, tanggal penilaian, serta tanggal pemberian HB-0, BCG, dan OPV1. Analisis dilakukan secara univariat dan bivariat menggunakan uji Chi-square.Hasil: Sebagian besar responden memperoleh dukungan suami (54,8%), memiliki pengetahuan baik (60,3%), berada pada lingkungan budaya yang mendukung (58,9%), dan memiliki neonatus dengan imunisasi lengkap (67,1%). Analisis bivariat menunjukkan hubungan antara dukungan suami (p = 0.005; OR = 5,009), pengetahuan ibu (p 0.001; OR = 10,364), dan budaya (p = 0.004; OR = 5,000) dengan kelengkapan imunisasi neonatus.Kesimpulan: Dukungan suami, pengetahuan ibu, dan budaya berhubungan secara signifikan dengan kelengkapan imunisasi neonatus. Temuan ini menunjukkan hubungan statistik dan tidak membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat karena desain penelitian bersifat cross-sectional.Saran: Orang tua diharapkan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan dukungan terhadap pemberian imunisasi neonatus serta mengikuti jadwal imunisasi sesuai ketentuan. Kata Kunci: Dukungan Suami, Pengetahuan, Budaya, Imunisasi Neonatus ABSTRACT Background: The completeness of Hepatitis B birth dose (HB-0), BCG, and Polio 1 immunization among neonates remains a public health concern because coverage has not yet reached the expected target. At Padang Cermin Community Health Center, HB-0 coverage was 52.1%, while BCG and Polio 1 coverage was 65.5%. Family and sociocultural factors, including husbands’ support, maternal knowledge, and culture, may be associated with neonatal immunization completeness.Objective: This study aimed to analyze the associations of husbands’ support, maternal knowledge, and culture with the completeness of HB-0, BCG, and Polio 1 immunization among neonates in the working area of Padang Cermin Community Health Center, Pesawaran Regency, in 2026.Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study included all 73 eligible mothers with neonates using total sampling. Husbands’ support, maternal knowledge, and culture were assessed using structured questionnaires. Immunization status was verified using the Maternal and Child Health (KIA) handbook and/or the health-center immunization register based on the infant’s date of birth, assessment date, and documented dates of HB-0, BCG, and OPV1 administration. Data were analyzed using univariate analysis and the Chi-square test.Results: Most respondents received husbands’ support (54.8%), had good knowledge (60.3%), lived in a supportive cultural environment (58.9%), and had neonates with complete immunization (67.1%). Significant associations were found between husbands’ support (p = 0.005; OR = 5.009), maternal knowledge (p 0.001; OR = 10.364), and culture (p = 0.004; OR = 5.000) and neonatal immunization completeness.Conclusion: Husbands’ support, maternal knowledge, and culture were significantly associated with neonatal immunization completeness. These findings represent statistical associations and should not be interpreted as causal relationships because of the cross-sectional study design.Suggestions: Parents are expected to improve their knowledge of and support for neonatal immunization and to follow the recommended immunization schedule. Keywords: Husbands’ Support, Maternal Knowledge, Culture, Neonatal Immunization

title: Protein kinase D1 regulates innate immune signaling pathways to promote hepatitis C virus replication
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatitis C virus (HCV) has developed multiple means to disrupt host innate immune response to promote its replication. Protein kinase D1 (PKD1) is a serine/threonine kinase involved in cell proliferation and lipid metabolism. By analyzing the effect of PKD1 on HCV replication, we found that HCV activated PKD1 via protein kinase C (PKC) early in infection and induced the cleavage of PKD1 at later timepoints of infection via caspase-3. PKD1 silencing had no effect on HCV entry, but it reduced HCV RNA levels in cells, indicating an important role of PKD1 in promoting HCV replication. PKD1 silencing also induced the expression of interferons (IFNs) and IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) and augmented the HCV-induced TNF-α expression, which enhanced the IFN response. Interestingly, the induction of inflammasomes was compromised in HCV-infected cells in the absence of PKD1, indicating an important role of PKD1 in promoting the inflammasomal response. Taken together, our results indicated that HCV activated PKD1 to suppress the IFN response and TNF-α signaling and in the meantime induce the inflammasomal response. Our results, thus, revealed an interesting interplay between HCV and host innate immune responses and an important role of PKD1 in this intricate interplay. IMPORTANCE Hepatitis C virus (HCV) establishes chronic infection in most patients that it infects, and this chronic infection can lead to severe liver diseases including steatosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. PKD1 is a multifunctional protein that regulates lipid metabolism, cell proliferation, and cellular apoptosis. In this report, we investigated the relationship between HCV and PKD1. We found that HCV could activate PKD1 to suppress interferon response and TNF-α signaling to promote its replication and in the meantime enhance the inflammasomal response. These effects of HCV on PKD1 provide important insights for understanding the mechanism of HCV persistence and pathogenesis in patients.

title: First report of anti-HDV antibodies in HBsAg-negative blood donors with detectable HBV-DNA in southern Mozambique
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the seroprevalence of hepatitis D virus in hepatitis B virus positive blood donors in southern Mozambique. A cross-sectional study was conducted among blood donors in southern Mozambique between December 2022 and January 2024. HBV infection was defined by HBsAg positivity and/or detectable HBV DNA. HDV serology was assessed among HBV-positive samples. Samples that tested positive for anti-HDV were tested for anti-HBc and HDV RNA. Among 3,855 donors screened, 72 (1.9%) were HBsAg-positive, while 65 (2.5%) HBsAg-negative donors had detectable HBV DNA, suggesting occult HBV infection. No Anti-HDV was detected in HBsAg-positive samples (0; 95% CI: 0.0–5.0%). The seroprevalence of anti-HDV in HBsAg-negative samples with detectable HBV DNA was 1.5% (1; 95% CI: 0.04–8.4%). No HDV RNA was detected in the anti-HDV-reactive sample. In conclusion, only one anti-HDV-reactive sample was identified among HBsAg-positive blood donors, suggesting a low frequency of detectable HDV exposure in this study.

title: Improved HCV genotyping based on sequence encoding and feature integration
abstract: Genomic sequence classification is an important task for understanding viral genetic variability and supporting genotype identification, particularly for viruses such as the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV). In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of different sequence encoding techniques, supplementary genomic descriptors, and class-balancing strategies for HCV genotype classification under a stricter CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation protocol designed to reduce sequence-identity leakage. Four encoding methods were investigated, namely Frequency Chaos Game Representation (FCGR), k-mer encoding, one-hot encoding, and label encoding. These representations were evaluated using multiple machine learning models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). To address class imbalance, SMOTE was applied, while GC content and GC skew were included as supplementary compositional descriptors. Overall, FCGR and k-mer encoding outperformed one-hot and label encoding. The best result was achieved using k-mer encoding with XGBoost and SMOTE, obtaining a macro F1-score of 0.890, accuracy of 0.922, macro precision of 0.866, macro recall of 0.925, macro specificity of 0.990, and MCC of 0.893 under the CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation setting. The statistical analysis showed that SMOTE had a clear positive effect on classification performance, particularly for the Random Forest model, while GC-based descriptors provided additional interpretability but did not show a statistically significant improvement in the k-mer-based experiment. Overall, this study demonstrates the importance of selecting appropriate sequence encodings and class-balancing strategies for machine-learning-based HCV genotype classification. The findings provide a comparative basis for future work on sequence-based classification tasks in virology and computational genomics.

title: Trend Analysis of Hepatitis C Seroreactivity in Voluntary Blood Donors at a Stand-Alone Blood Centre: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Background: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a major transfusion-transmitted infection and remains an important public health concern.Blood donor screening is essential for ensuring blood safety.This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of HCV and analyse its temporal trend among voluntary blood donors at a standalone blood centre in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat, over a six-year period.Methods: A retrospective record-based study was conducted at stand-alone blood centre in Ahmedabad District, Gujarat, India, over a six-year period from January 2020 to December 2025.Data from all voluntary blood donors who successfully donated blood during the study period were included.Donor blood samples were initially screened for anti-HCV antibodies using a third-generation Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA).Initially reactive samples were retested and confirmed using Chemiluminescent Microparticle Immunoassay (CMIA).The collected data were analysed to calculate annual and overall HCV prevalence and to observe changes across the study years.Results: A total of 332,639 blood donations were analysed.Overall, 230 donations were confirmed HCV reactive, giving a prevalence of 0.069%.Annual prevalence ranged from 0.039% to 0.111%.The highest prevalence was observed in 2025.While the overall prevalence remained low, an increase in HCV-reactive donations was observed during 2024 and 2025. Conclusion:The findings demonstrate that HCV seroreactivity among voluntary blood donors remained consistently low over the six-year study period, reflecting the effectiveness of existing blood safety measures.The late increase in seroprevalence highlights the need to monitor local donor demographics and evaluate whether supplementary testing methods like nucleic acid testing (NAT) should be integrated to reduce window-period risks.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

source_records.abstract: Background: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a major transfusion-transmitted infection and remains an important public health concern.Blood donor screening is essential for ensuring blood safety.This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of HCV and analyse its temporal trend among voluntary blood donors at a standalone blood centre in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat, over a six-year period.Methods: A retrospective record-based study was conducted at stand-alone blood centre in Ahmedabad District, Gujarat, India, over a six-year period from January 2020 to December 2025.Data from all voluntary blood donors who successfully donated blood during the study period were included.Donor blood samples were initially screened for anti-HCV antibodies using a third-generation Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA).Initially reactive samples were retested and confirmed using Chemiluminescent Microparticle Immunoassay (CMIA).The collected data were analysed to calculate annual and overall HCV prevalence and to observe changes across the study years.Results: A total of 332,639 blood donations were analysed.Overall, 230 donations were confirmed HCV reactive, giving a prevalence of 0.069%.Annual prevalence ranged from 0.039% to 0.111%.The highest prevalence was observed in 2025.While the overall prevalence remained low, an increase in HCV-reactive donations was observed during 2024 and 2025. Conclusion:The findings demonstrate that HCV seroreactivity among voluntary blood donors remained consistently low over the six-year study period, reflecting the effectiveness of existing blood safety measures.The late increase in seroprevalence highlights the need to monitor local donor demographics and evaluate whether supplementary testing methods like nucleic acid testing (NAT) should be integrated to reduce window-period risks.

title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system. The US score, which included seven parameters, was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Serum HBV DNA, ALT, AST, and immune parameters were also measured. The strong correlations support the use of US as a non-invasive biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 回顾性纳入 100 名接受 TAF 单药治疗(25 毫克/天)至少 24 个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者。
elements_zh.methods: 在基线、12 个月和 24 个月时计算七参数半定量 US 评分,包括肝脏回声性、包膜轮廓、边缘形状、血管清晰度、门静脉直径 (PVD)、脾厚度 (ST) 和脾静脉速度 (SVV)。同时,测量血清 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 脱氧核糖核酸 (DNA)、丙氨酸转氨酶 (ALT)、天冬氨酸转氨酶 (AST)、外周 T 细胞亚群,包括分化簇 3 阳性 (CD3 + )、CD4 + 、CD8 + T 细胞、CD4 + / CD8 + 比率和自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。

title_zh: 半定量超声评分揭示慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)在接受替诺福韦艾拉酚胺治疗期间肝脏结构恢复和免疫调节
source_body_en: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。方法 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。在基线、12个月和24个月时计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。分析了超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的相关性。结果 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。CD4+ T细胞比例和CD4+/CD8+比值增加,而CD8+ T细胞比例下降;NK细胞活性从42.7 ± 7.3%上升至52.4 ± 6.2%(P < 0.05)。超声评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4+/CD8+比值(r = −0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = −0.38)呈负相关(所有P < 0.01)。结论 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。

title: A dual recombinant strategy to quantify PreS1 antibody in hepatitis B patients with genotype B or C virus by ELISA
abstract: Elevated levels of anti-preS1 antibodies in patients correlate with faster hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, since preS1 is vital for viral entry. However, accurate quantification of preS1 antibodies is hindered by the variation of HBV genotypes. Herein, a quantitative preS1 antibody assay was developed for Chinese patients with predominant HBV genotypes B and C. First, to address genotype diversity, we constructed a dual recombinant protein combining genotype B and C preS1. Second, a mouse-human chimeric antibody with high and comparable affinity for both B and C preS1 is developed as the standard for quantification by screening and cloning. An optimized ELISA kit using these components demonstrated good specificity, accuracy, reproducibility and stability, with a linear range of 10–100 ng/mL. This approach extends the patient coverage in China to over 95%, providing a valuable diagnostic tool. This work demonstrates a proof-of-concept model for developing broad-coverage assays for other multi-genotype viral diseases.

abstract_zh: 患者体内抗PreS1抗体水平升高与更快的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)清除相关,因为PreS1对病毒进入至关重要。然而,由于HBV基因型的差异,准确量化PreS1抗体受到阻碍。本文开发了一种针对中国主要为基因型B和C的乙型肝炎病毒患者的定量PreS1抗体检测方法。首先,为应对基因型多样性,我们构建了一种结合基因型B和C PreS1的双重组蛋白。其次,通过筛选和克隆,开发了一种对B和C型PreS1具有高且可比亲和力的小鼠-人嵌合抗体,作为定量的标准。使用这些组分优化的ELISA试剂盒表现出良好的特异性、准确度、可重复性和稳定性,线性范围为10–100 ng/mL。该方法将中国患者的覆盖范围扩展至超过95%,提供了一种有价值的诊断工具。本研究展示了一种开发适用于其他多基因型病毒疾病的广泛覆盖检测方法的概念验证模型。
